title: SSR redirects a `redirectTo` that uses a route parameter to the literal `:id` instead of the parameter value
body:
### Command

serve, build

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

With server rendering, a route whose `redirectTo` reuses one of its own route parameters is redirected to the literal parameter name. The Angular router substitutes the matched parameter on the client:

```ts
export const routes: Routes = [
  { path: 'old/:id', redirectTo: 'new/:id' },
  { path: 'new/:id', component: Detail },
];
```

- Client-side navigation to `/old/5` ends up at `/new/5`.
- A server-rendered request for `/old/5` responds `302` with `Location: /new/:id`.

`resolveRedirectTo` in `packages/angular/ssr/src/routes/ng-routes.ts` replaces parameters of the parent route with `*`, but leaves `:id` in the `redirectTo` string unchanged. `buildPathWithParams` in `packages/angular/ssr/src/utils/url.ts` then only fills `*` segments from the request path, so the `:id` placeholder is never replaced.

### Minimal Reproduction

```sh
ng new repro --ssr --defaults   # outputMode: server
```

Routes as above, `serverRoutes` with `{ path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Server }`, then:

```sh
ng build && node dist/repro/server/server.mjs
curl -i http://localhost:4000/old/5
```

### Exception or Error

```text

Expected `Location: /new/5`.
```

title: ng update: "Package '@angular/core' is not a dependency" in a bun workspace member
body:
### Command

update

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

20.3.40

### Description

In a bun workspace where the Angular project is a workspace member (not the root package), `ng update <package>` cannot find any of the project's dependencies:

```
$ bunx ng update @angular/core
Using package manager: bun
Collecting installed dependencies...
Found 1 dependencies.
Package '@angular/core' is not a dependency.
```

The same layout behaves differently by CLI version (checked today with bun 1.4.3):

- 20.3.40: `Found 20 dependencies`, then `Package '@angular/core' is already up to date.`
- 21.2.27: `Found 1 dependencies.` then `Package '@angular/core' is not a dependency.` (`ng update` without arguments still lists the packages)
- 22.2.3: same failure. This also blocks `ng update @angular/core@22 @angular/cli@22` from 21, since the temporary 22 CLI fails the same way.

#32787 fixed this for npm workspaces (#34308). The bun path has no equivalent, and on `main` it is unchanged:

- `listDependenciesCommand` for bun is `['pm', 'ls']`. Run from the member's directory, it prints the root's dependencies, that is the workspace members themselves:

  ```
  /tmp/repro node_modules (405 installed)
  └── app@workspace:app
  ```

- `parseBunDependencies(stdout, logger)` does not use the `{ workspacePackageName }` options that `#populateDependencyCache` passes. It returns that single entry, so every requested package is "not a dependency".

#32781 reported this for bun (same layout) and was closed as a duplicate of #32787, but the npm fix does not cover it.

Since `bun pm ls` has no per-member output, one possible direction is to build the member's dependency map from its `package.json` and the installed manifests. The `migrateOnly` path already falls back to that through `findPackageJson`.

### Minimal Reproduction

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro
printf '{ "name": "root", "private": true, "workspaces": ["app"] }\n' > package.json
bunx @angular/cli@22.2.3 new app --skip-git --skip-install --package-manager bun --defaults --interactive=false --ssr=false --ai-config=none
bun install
cd app
bunx ng update @angular/core
```

### Exception or Error

```text
Using package manager: bun
Collecting installed dependencies...
Found 1 dependencies.
Package '@angular/core' is not a dependency.
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.3
Node.js           : 24.21.0
Package Manager   : bun 1.4.3
Operating System  : darwin arm64
```

### Anything else relevant?

Workaround: update the versions with bun (`bun add @angular/core@^22.2.3 …`), then run each package's migrations with `ng update <package> --migrate-only --from=<old> --to=<new>`. That path does not depend on the dependency list.

title: Allow index.preloadInitial to preload the full static closure of the initial bundle (number or "all")
body:
### Command

build

### Description

#27581 limited modulepreload hints to a shallow set of 10 initial chunks, as a safe default for all applications (#27490). For an application with a deep initial import graph that default costs one network round trip per depth level: the browser only discovers the chunks at depth N after the chunks at depth N-1 have arrived and been parsed.

Our `main` has a static closure of 45 chunks across six depth levels. We post-process `index.html` after `ng build` to preload all of them. Measured in production RUM over three weeks (roughly a million initial loads per week), weekdays before versus after:

| Segment | LCP p75 before | LCP p75 after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| all initial loads | 2.00 s | 1.84 s |
| effective connection type 4g, desktop | 2.07 s | 1.91 s |
| effective connection type 3g, desktop | 7.0 s | 5.3 s |
| effective connection type 2g, desktop | 22.8 s | 14.7 s |

The slowest connections gained the most, which is the opposite of what the HTTP Archive correlation cited in #27490 would predict. That correlation covers preloads of any resource. Chunks in the entry point's static closure are all required before the application can execute at all, so preloading them does not compete with anything more critical than the stylesheet.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Let `index.preloadInitial` accept a number or `"all"` in addition to the current boolean, keeping `true` as today's shallow-10 behaviour. That would let us delete a post-build script that has to track the CLI's `index.html` output, and which broke on the `integrity` attributes added in 22.x.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Post-processing `index.html` (what we do now); setting `preloadInitial: false` and writing every hint ourselves (same fragility); eager-loading the landing route into the main bundle (adds 330 KB gzipped to every first load for the 70% of visits that land elsewhere).

title: subresourceIntegrity leaves initial chunks beyond the modulepreload cap without any integrity metadata
body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

With `subresourceIntegrity: true`, the application builder covers the emitted JavaScript in three places:

1. the entry scripts (`main`, `polyfills`) and the stylesheet get an `integrity` attribute;
2. up to `MODULE_PRELOAD_MAX` (10) initial chunks get a `<link rel="modulepreload">` carrying `integrity`;
3. every other `.js` output goes into the integrity-only `<script type="importmap">`.

Step 3 skips initial files on purpose (`index-html-generator.ts`: `if (!file.path.endsWith('.js') || initialFiles.has(file.path)) continue;`), on the assumption that step 2 carries their hash. But step 2 is capped at 10, sorted by depth. Any initial chunk past the cap is therefore hashed nowhere: it is loaded through a static `import` from `main` with no integrity check, even though SRI is enabled.

In our application `main`'s static closure is 45 chunks. A production build hashes 10 of them in preload tags and 0 in the import map, leaving 34 initial chunks without integrity metadata. The import map has 451 entries, all of them lazy chunks.

### Minimal Reproduction

Any application whose initial bundle splits into more than 10 chunks, built with `"subresourceIntegrity": true` in the production configuration:

```sh
ng build --configuration production
grep -o 'integrity="sha384-[^"]*"' dist/<app>/browser/index.html | wc -l   # tags
ls dist/<app>/browser/chunk-*.js | wc -l                                     # emitted chunks
```

Diff the chunk names present in `index.html` (tags plus the import map's `integrity` keys) against the chunks in the output directory. The chunks statically imported by `main` at depths beyond the first 10 preloads appear in neither.

### Exception or Error

```text
No error. The chunks load without an integrity check.
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.2
Node.js           : 24.20.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.19.0
@angular/build    : 22.2.2
@angular/core     : 22.2.1
OS                : macOS (local), Linux (CI)
```

### Anything else relevant?

Expected: every emitted chunk is covered either by a tag or by the import map. The simplest fix seems to be dropping the `initialFiles.has()` exclusion for initial chunks that did not receive a preload tag, or including every chunk in the import map. A chunk hashed in both places is harmless, since both hashes must match the same file.

title: unit-test: browser-mode runs stall ("iframe did not become ready") when a Docker container starts alongside
body:
### Command

test

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

With `"browsers": ["chromiumHeadless"]` and `@vitest/browser-playwright`, `ng test` stalls in roughly 4 runs of 10 when a Docker container starts while the tests start up. That is what happens when another package of a workspace runs integration tests with Testcontainers at the same time. A few test iframes load Vitest's runtime and never request the Angular test setup (`init-testbed.js`) or their spec chunks; after 60 s the run fails.

On a fresh `ng new` app with six generated components:

| | runs | stalled |
|---|---:|---:|
| `ng test` | 15 | 0 |
| `ng test` with `docker run -d alpine:3 sleep 8` starting beside it | 47 | 21 |
| plain Vitest browser mode (no Angular builder), seven trivial files, same container | 11 | 0 |

The last row (on Vitest 5.0.4; the others on 5.0.4 and 5.0.5 alike) is why I am filing it here rather than with Vitest. Ruled out on the same machine: CPU load (all 16 cores busy), synchronous disk writes, touching a source file mid-run, the image or a published port (`alpine sleep` is enough), and the headless shell itself (the full Chromium build stalls too, less often). Chromium logs no failed request and no console error, and a page opening ~1000 fresh connections to localhost while a container starts loses none.

With `DEBUG=vitest:browser:*`, all seven sessions connect to the tester API at the same moment, then only two send their first command (`__vitest_viewport`); the other five stay silent until the 60 s timeout. A Vite request trace (`DEBUG=vite:time`) of a stalled run shows those five iframes fetched `index`, `plugins` and `rolldown-runtime` from the optimized deps and nothing after; a passing run goes on to `init-compiler.js`, `init-testbed.js`, the Angular deps and the spec files.

It may be the same family as vitest-dev/vitest#11171 (a rejected import inside the tester iframe never fires `iframe.onerror`, so the orchestrator waits until the timeout), closed there for want of a reproduction.

### Minimal Reproduction

```sh
npx @angular/cli@22.2.3 new ng-docker-stall --defaults --skip-git --ssr=false --style=css
cd ng-docker-stall
for c in alpha bravo charlie delta echo foxtrot; do npx ng g c "$c"; done
npm install -D --save-exact vitest@5.0.5 @vitest/browser-playwright@5.0.5 playwright@1.64.1
npx playwright install --only-shell chromium
npx ng config projects.ng-docker-stall.architect.test.options.browsers '["chromiumHeadless"]'
npx ng test    # passes
```

Then, with Docker running, this script, `./stall.sh 10`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Runs `ng test` several times while a Docker container starts beside it, and
# counts the runs whose test iframes stall.
runs=${1:-5}
stalled=0
for i in $(seq 1 "$runs"); do
  (id=$(docker run -d alpine:3 sleep 8); sleep 9; docker rm -f "$id" > /dev/null) &
  if npx ng test 2>&1 | grep -q 'did not become ready'; then
    stalled=$((stalled + 1))
    echo "run $i: stalled"
  else
    echo "run $i: passed"
  fi
  wait
done
echo "$stalled of $runs runs stalled"
```

Expected: every run passes, as without the container. Actual: some runs stall and fail after 60 s.

### Exception or Error


title: `ng new --view-encapsulation` has no effect on generated components
body:
### Command

new

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

The `--view-encapsulation` option of `ng new` / `ng generate application` is documented as "Sets the view
encapsulation mode for components in the initial project", but it currently has no effect:

1. The root `App` component is generated without `encapsulation`, so its styles stay scoped (Emulated).
2. The value is not saved to the project's `@schematics/angular:component` defaults in `angular.json`, so components
   generated later with `ng g c` also use Emulated.
3. For `--no-standalone` apps, `main.ts` gets `bootstrapModule(AppModule, { defaultEncapsulation: ViewEncapsulation.X })`.
   `defaultEncapsulation` is only read by the JIT compiler, so it has no effect with AOT, which is the default for
   `ng build` and `ng serve`.

This looks like #13689 again: it was fixed in 89797900db by setting the encapsulation on the root component and in
`bootstrapModule`, but the root component part was removed in 58bc5b8f2a (for #13742, invalid generated code), leaving
only the JIT-only option.


### Minimal Reproduction

1. `ng new ve-repro --defaults --view-encapsulation=None` (same result with `--no-standalone`)
2. Add `h1 { color: red; }` to `src/app/app.css`
3. `ng build --configuration development`
4. The output contains `h1[_ngcontent-%COMP%]`, i.e. the styles are still encapsulated.
5. `angular.json` has no `viewEncapsulation` under `projects.ve-repro.schematics`, so `ng g c foo` also generates an
   Emulated component.


### Exception or Error

```text

```

### Your Environment

```text
Latest
```

### Anything else relevant?

Possible fix: set `encapsulation` on the generated root component, save `viewEncapsulation` in the component schematic
defaults, and drop `defaultEncapsulation` from `main.ts`. Happy to send a PR.

title: `ng generate web-worker` adds `webWorkerTsConfig` to the `@angular/build:unit-test` target, breaking `ng test`
body: ### Command generate ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description Running `ng generate web-worker` in a newly created application breaks `ng test`. The `web-worker` schematic adds `webWorkerTsConfig` to the options of the project's `test` target, regardless of which builder that target uses. New applications use the `@angular/build:unit-test` builder, whose schema does not have a `webWorkerTsConfig` option, so `ng test` fails schema validation afterwards. The option is still needed on the `build` target (where the schematic also adds it). Removing it from the `test` target makes `ng test` pass again, including with the worker in place. Relevant code: `packages/schematics/angular/web-worker/index.ts` if (testTarget) { (testTarget.options ??= {}).webWorkerTsConfig ??= workerConfigPath; } ### Minimal Reproduction 1. `ng new ww-repro --defaults` 2. `cd ww-repro` 3. `ng test --watch=false` → passes 4. `ng generate web-worker app` 5. `ng test --watch=false` → fails with the error below After step 4, the `test` target in `angular.json` is: "test": { "builder": "@angular/build:unit-test", "options": { "webWorkerTsConfig": "tsconfig.worker.json" } } Deleting `webWorkerTsConfig` from the `test` target options makes `ng test` pass again. ### Exception or Error ```text Error: Schema validation failed with the following errors: Unknown option "webWorkerTsConfig". Valid options are: buildTarget, tsConfig, runner, runnerConfig, browsers, browserViewport, include, exclude, filter, watch, headless, debug, ui, isolate, splitting, quiet, coverage, coverageInclude, coverageExclude, coverageReporters, coverageThresholds, coverageWatermarks, reporters, outputFile, providersFile, setupFiles, progress, listTests, dumpVirtualFiles. ``` ### Your Environment ```text Angular CLI : 22.2.3 Node.js : 24.15.0 Package Manager : npm 11.12.1 OS : darwin arm64 @angular/build : 22.2.3 vitest : 5.0.5 ``` ### Anything else relevant? Suggested fix: only add `webWorkerTsConfig` to the `test` target when it uses a Karma builder (`@angular-devkit/build-angular:karma` / `@angular/build:karma`). The unit-test builder gets build options from its `buildTarget`. Happy to send a PR with a spec.

title: @angular/build: lazy routes get no SSR modulepreload hints when the app's tsconfig is not at the workspace root (ɵentryName relative to basePath, chunk map relative to workspace root)
body:
### Command build ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description When an application's `tsconfig.app.json` is not at the workspace root, SSR adds no `` for any lazy route. That includes the CLI's own multi-project layout (`ng generate application` puts it in `projects//`) and every Nx workspace. The routes are written in the shape `lazyRoutesTransformer` recognises, and the pages render correctly. Only the hints are missing, and nothing warns about it. **Cause.** The two sides of the lookup use different base directories: - `lazyRoutesTransformer` stamps `ɵentryName` as a path relative to `compilerOptions.basePath` ([`lazy-routes-transformer.ts#L151`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.3/packages/angular/build/src/tools/angular/transformers/lazy-routes-transformer.ts#L151)). The compiler sets `basePath` to the directory of the tsconfig, here `projects/site`. - `generateLazyLoadedFilesMappings` keys `entryPointToBrowserMapping` by esbuild's `entryPoint` ([`manifest.ts#L262`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.3/packages/angular/build/src/utils/server-rendering/manifest.ts#L262)). That path is relative to `absWorkingDir`, which is the workspace root ([`application-code-bundle.ts#L631`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/v22.2.3/packages/angular/build/src/tools/esbuild/application-code-bundle.ts#L631)). So the stamp reads `src/app/home/home.ts` and the key reads `projects/site/src/app/home/home.ts`. `appendPreloadToMetadata` finds nothing and every route's `preload` stays empty. When the tsconfig is at the workspace root, as in a default `ng new`, the two bases happen to coincide, which is probably why this has gone unnoticed. | `projects/site/tsconfig.app.json` | `ɵentryName` in the server bundle | `preload` in `angular-app-manifest.mjs` | route hints in `index.html` / `pricing/index.html` | | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | | as generated | `src/app/home/home.ts` | none | 0 / 0 | | `"angularCompilerOptions": { "basePath": "." }` added | `projects/site/src/app/home/home.ts` | on both routes | 1 / 1 (the route's own chunk) | **Workaround.** `"angularCompilerOptions": { "basePath": "." }` in the app's tsconfig. It works only because the value is read raw and resolved against the process cwd, and the build happens to run from the workspace root. **Expected.** Route hints do not depend on where the tsconfig lives. One option is for the transformer to stamp paths relative to the workspace root, which the builder already knows, instead of relative to `basePath`. **Real-world impact.** In our Nx workspace (22 lazy routes, `@nx/angular:application`, which delegates to `buildApplication` unchanged), no route had ever received a hint. With the workaround every route does. On the home page, the shell route's chunk finishes 5.8 s earlier in throttled Lighthouse runs (mobile, devtools throttling, 8× CPU, 5 runs), and TTI drops by 1.3 s. ### Minimal Reproduction ```bash npx -p @angular/cli@22.2.3 ng new ws --create-application=false --skip-git --package-manager=npm --defaults --ai-config=none cd ws npx ng generate application site --ssr --routing --style=css --skip-tests --defaults ``` `projects/site/src/app/app.routes.ts` ```ts import { Routes } from '@angular/router'; export const routes: Routes = [ { path: '', loadComponent: () => import('./home/home').then((m) => m.Home) }, { path: 'pricing', loadComponent: () => import('./pricing/pricing').then((m) => m.Pricing), }, ]; ``` `projects/site/src/app/home/home.ts` (and `pricing/pricing.ts`, the same with `Pricing`) ```ts import { Component } from '@angular/core'; @Component({ selector: 'app-home', template: '

Home

' }) export class Home {} ``` ```bash npx ng build site grep -c '"preload"' dist/site/server/angular-app-manifest.mjs # 0 grep -o ']*>' dist/site/browser/index.html # only the shared initial chunk grep -rhoE 'entryName:"[^"]*"' dist/site/server/*.mjs # src/app/home/home.ts, src/app/pricing/pricing.ts ``` Then add `"angularCompilerOptions": { "basePath": "." }` to `projects/site/tsconfig.app.json` and build again. Both routes get `preload`, each page gets its own chunk's hint, and the stamps become `projects/site/src/app/…`. ### Exception or Error ```text None. The build succeeds and the pages render; only the lazy-route modulepreload hints are missing. ``` ### Your Environment ```text Angular CLI : 22.2.3 Angular : 22.2.3 Node.js : 24.20.0 Package Manager : npm 11.19.0 Operating System : darwin arm64 @angular/build 22.2.3 @angular/cli 22.2.3 @angular/common 22.2.3 @angular/compiler 22.2.3 @angular/compiler-cli 22.2.3 @angular/core 22.2.3 @angular/platform-browser 22.2.3 @angular/platform-server 22.2.3 @angular/router 22.2.3 @angular/ssr 22.2.3 typescript 6.0.3 ``` ### Anything else relevant? Also observed on 22.2.1, in our Nx workspace. The transformer's `relative(basePath, …)` is unchanged since it was introduced in 8d7a51dfc ("feat(@angular/ssr): add `modulepreload` for lazy-loaded routes").

extractLicenses crashes with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')" when using Module Federation shared modules with webpack >= 5.107
body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

21.x (with webpack <= 5.106.2)

### Description

`@angular-devkit/build-angular:browser` production builds that use Module Federation `shared` modules (for example, via `@angular-architects/module-federation`) crash when `extractLicenses` is `true`.

The crash comes from `license-webpack-plugin` 4.0.2, a dependency of `@angular-devkit/build-angular`. webpack 5.107.0 (webpack/webpack#20860) changed `ProvideSharedModule.identifier()` from `provide module (scope) name@version = request` to `provide module (scope) name@version|request`. The plugin still parses the identifier with `filename.split('=')[1].trim()` (`dist/WebpackInnerModuleIterator.js`), which throws.

`@angular-devkit/build-angular` 22.2.x depends on webpack 5.111.0, so every Module Federation app on the webpack builder is affected unless it disables `extractLicenses` (and so loses `3rdpartylicenses.txt`).

`license-webpack-plugin` has had no commits since 2023. I reported the bug there as well: <LINK TO THE license-webpack-plugin ISSUE>.

Possible actions:
- patch, fork or vendor `license-webpack-plugin` in `@angular-devkit/build-angular`, or
- guard the `provide module` case (the fix is a few lines, see the linked issue).

### Minimal Reproduction

1. `ng new mf-app` (Angular 22), then `ng add @angular-architects/module-federation --type host`.
2. Make sure `webpack.config.js` declares at least one `shared` package (the default `shareAll(...)` is enough).
3. `ng build --configuration production` (with `extractLicenses: true`, the default for production).

### Exception or Error

```text
- Generating browser application bundles (phase: setup)...
✔ Browser application bundle generation complete.
An unhandled exception occurred: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI: 22.2.x
Node: 24.21.0
@angular-devkit/build-angular: 22.2.2
@angular-architects/module-federation: 22.0.0
webpack: 5.111.0
license-webpack-plugin: 4.0.2
OS: Linux
```

### Anything else relevant?

Workaround: apply the fix to `license-webpack-plugin` with `patch-package`. Setting `"extractLicenses": false` also avoids the crash, but then no license file is generated.

title: module.register() in the prerender loader prints DEP0205 on Node 26
body:
### Command

build

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

`@angular/build` registers its in-memory ESM loader with `module.register()`, which Node runtime-deprecated in Node 26. The call is in `src/utils/server-rendering/esm-in-memory-loader/register-hooks.js`:

```js
register('./loader-hooks.js', { parentURL: pathToFileURL(__filename), data: workerData });
```

`esm-in-memory-loader/utils.js` points `IMPORT_EXEC_ARGV` at that file, and `server-rendering/prerender.js` passes it as the `execArgv` of every prerender worker, so each worker prints DEP0205 to stderr during `ng build`.

Node runtime-deprecated the API in nodejs/node#62401, merged 2026-04-01 and labelled semver-major, so the warning starts at Node 26. `@angular/build` 22.2.2 declares `engines.node` as `^22.22.3 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0`, so this is a supported Node version.

This is not an Angular regression, the code did not change, Node did.

### Minimal Reproduction

Any app with prerendering, built on Node 26:

1. `ng new repro --ssr` and keep prerendering enabled.
2. `ng build` on Node 26.
3. DEP0205 appears on stderr, once per prerender worker.

Measured on our app with Angular CLI 22.2.2, `@angular/build` 22.2.2, Node 26.5.0 on Windows, and on our CI agent (Linux, Node 26) in the production build step.

Also reproduced without a build, which isolates the loader from the rest of the pipeline. A worker created the way `prerender.js` creates one:

```js
const { Worker } = require('node:worker_threads');
const { IMPORT_EXEC_ARGV } = require('@angular/build/src/utils/server-rendering/esm-in-memory-loader/utils.js');
new Worker('./stay-alive.cjs', {
  execArgv: [IMPORT_EXEC_ARGV],
  workerData: { outputFiles: {}, workspaceRoot: process.cwd() },
});
```

with `stay-alive.cjs` holding the worker open for a moment (`setTimeout(() => {}, 700)`). Without the flag it prints DEP0205 in 3 of 3 runs, with `NODE_OPTIONS=--disable-warning=DEP0205` it is clean in 3 of 3 runs.

Worth knowing when reproducing: DEP0205 is emitted asynchronously, so a worker whose body is `process.exit(0)` exits before the warning flushes and the run looks clean.

### Exception or Error

```text
(node:24372) [DEP0205] DeprecationWarning: `module.register()` is deprecated. Use `module.registerHooks()` instead.
(Use `node --trace-deprecation ...` to show where the warning was created)
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.2
Angular           : 22.2.1
Node.js           : 26.5.0
Package Manager   : pnpm 12.3.1
Operating System  : win32 x64

@angular-devkit/build-angular   22.2.2
@angular-devkit/core            22.2.2
@angular-devkit/schematics      22.2.2
@angular/build                  22.2.2
@angular/cli                    22.2.2
@angular/core                   22.2.1
@angular/platform-server        22.2.1
@angular/ssr                    22.2.2
rxjs                            7.8.2
typescript                      6.0.3
zone.js                         0.16.3
```

### Anything else relevant?

A possible fix, from reading the two hook files. `module.registerHooks()` takes synchronous hooks, and `loader-hooks.js` is almost there already: `initialize` and `resolve` are synchronous, and `load` has exactly one await, `await readFile(filePath)`, which `readFileSync` covers. The `data: workerData` channel is not needed either, because the hooks already run inside a worker that can read `workerData` directly.

The one real difference to weigh is that `registerHooks` runs the hooks on the calling thread rather than on a separate loader thread, so the synchronous read would block it.

The same Node 26 warning reported elsewhere, in case it helps: payloadcms/payload#18361 and Julien-R44/hot-hook#18.

What we do meanwhile: `NODE_OPTIONS=--disable-warning=DEP0205` on the build step, which silences only this code.

title: unit-test builder (Vitest): test bundle output is not deterministic, which defeats Vitest 5 `fsModuleCache`
body:
### Command

test

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Building the same project twice in a row with `@angular/build:unit-test` (Vitest runner), with no source change in between, produces different output files: the same modules end up with different chunk names, because the import statements inside some chunks and spec entry points come out in a different order.

Only the order changes, never the code. Normalising the chunk names (`chunk-[A-Z0-9]{8}` → `chunk-X`) and comparing the files, every difference is one of:

- side-effect imports reordered in a spec entry point:
  ```diff
  -import "./chunk-X.js"; // (A)
  -import "./chunk-X.js"; // (B)
  +import "./chunk-X.js"; // (B)
  +import "./chunk-X.js"; // (A)
  ```
- named imports moved between two `import { … } from "./chunk-X.js"` statements:
  ```diff
  +import {
  +  SomeMapper
  +} from "./chunk-X.js";
   ...
  -import {
  -  SomeMapper
  -} from "./chunk-X.js";
  ```
- identifiers swapped in a re-exported list (`ModuleA, ModuleB` → `ModuleB, ModuleA`).

Since the chunk file names are content hashes, one reordered chunk renames itself and, in cascade, every chunk or spec that imports it.

Measured on two applications of the same workspace (two consecutive `ng test <app> --no-watch --dump-virtual-files`):

| project | JS files in the test bundle | files renamed between two runs |
|---|---|---|
| app A, JIT test build (`aot: false`) | 593 | 79 to 89 |
| app B, JIT test build | 89 | 10 |
| app B, AOT (default `build:development`) | 88 | 18 |
| two small libraries | 9 and 11 | 0 |

It happens with and without `--coverage`, in AOT and JIT, and with `NG_BUILD_MAX_WORKERS=1`, so it does not look like a worker race in the Angular compilation.

**Why it matters.** Vitest 5 enables `fsModuleCache` by default and keys it on file content and id. With the builder's output changing between runs, part of the cache is invalidated on every run (about 20 % of the entries for app A), so the cache cannot be reused between CI pipelines. Disabling `splitting` makes the output stable (100 % cache reuse) but the option is deprecated ("No longer needed with Vitest 5") and the suite is much slower without shared chunks (app A with coverage, warm cache: ~45 s instead of ~30 s).

Expected: identical inputs give byte-identical test bundles, as they would for a reproducible build.

### Minimal Reproduction

Not yet reduced to a public repository. Any workspace whose specs share enough code to produce many shared chunks should show it:

1. `ng test <project> --no-watch --dump-virtual-files`
2. Copy `.angular/cache/<version>/<project>/unit-test/output-files` aside.
3. Run step 1 again, without touching anything.
4. Compare the two lists of `*.js` file names: some chunk names differ. Diffing a renamed chunk against its counterpart only shows reordered imports.

Small projects (around ten output files) do not show it in our workspace.

### Exception or Error

_No response_

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.2
Angular           : 22.2.2
Node.js           : 24.21.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.19.0
Operating System  : darwin arm64 (on the node:24-alpine CI image, the persisted Vitest cache also grows on every pipeline instead of being reused)

@angular/build    : 22.2.2
vitest            : 5.0.4
esbuild           : 0.28.2
typescript        : 6.0.3
```

Unit-test target: `@angular/build:unit-test`, Vitest runner, jsdom, `isolate: false`, v8 coverage.

### Anything else relevant?

Related but distinct: #31724 (unit-test builder slow for testing and coverage). A deterministic test bundle would let `fsModuleCache` be persisted between CI runs, which would help there.

title: @angular/ssr: page under nested empty-path routes is prerendered without the modulepreload hints of its lazy chunks (regression since 19.1.6)
body:
### Command build ### Is this a regression? Yes, the previous version in which this bug was not present was: 19.1.5 ### Description A prerendered page reached through an empty-path route nested under another empty-path route (a componentless `''` route whose `''` child is a `loadChildren`, whose own `''` route is a `loadComponent`) is emitted without any `` hint for its own lazy chunks. A sibling page reached through a non-empty path with exactly the same lazy depth (`'pricing'` → `loadChildren` → `''` `loadComponent`) gets both of its hints. The page itself renders correctly; only the hints are missing. Measured with 22.2.2, `outputMode: "static"` (`index.csr.html` has 0 hints): | Routes | `/` | `/pricing` | | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | | `''` (componentless) → `''` loadChildren → `''` loadComponent | **0** (expected 2: `home.routes`, `home-page`) | 2 (`pricing.routes`, `pricing-page`) | | home flattened to a top-level `''` loadComponent | 1 (`home-page`, its only chunk) | 2 | Same nested routes on 19.1.5 vs 19.1.6 (both builds share 2 initial chunks, which `index.csr.html` also has): | Version | `/` | `/pricing` | | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------- | | 19.1.5 | 4 (2 shared + `home.routes` + `home-page`) | 4 | | 19.1.6 | **2** (shared only) | 4 | | `@angular/ssr` 19.1.5 with `@angular/build` 19.1.6 | 4 | 4 | The chunk hashes are identical across these builds; only `@angular/ssr` makes the difference. **Likely cause** (`packages/angular/ssr/src/routes/ng-routes.ts`): `traverseRoutesConfig` keys an empty-path route as `addTrailingSlash(currentRoutePath)`. Under a non-empty parent the parent and its `''` child get different keys (`/pricing` and `/pricing/`), which `RouteTree.insert` later merges with the last entry winning, the leaf that carries the accumulated `preload`. Under an empty-path parent both get the same key (`/`, or `/es/` for `es` → `''` → `''`), and `getRoutesFromAngularRouterConfig` keeps only the first result per key (`seenRoutes`, added in 5bf5e5fd2 "fix(@angular/ssr): prioritize the first matching route over subsequent ones", #29539). The first result is the outer route, yielded before `handleRoute` appends its `loadChildren` preloads and before any descendant's `loadComponent` preloads, so the leaf's metadata with the preloads is dropped. That dedupe is right for competing sibling routes with the same path; here the later entry is a descendant in the same match chain, the route the router actually activates. **Expected:** the prerendered page carries the hints of the route chain that renders it, as on 19.1.5 (for example, let a later result replace the kept one, or merge its `preload`, when it is a descendant of it rather than a sibling). **Real-world impact:** our home page had 3 modulepreload hints against 12 on `/pricing`; flattening the home route to a top-level `loadComponent` gave 9. ### Minimal Reproduction ```bash npx -p @angular/cli@22.2.2 ng new repro --ssr --routing --style=css --skip-git --skip-tests --defaults --ai-config=none --package-manager=npm cd repro # angular.json: set "outputMode": "static" # src/app/app.html: replace its content with (optional, only trims the placeholder) # app.routes.server.ts stays as generated: [{ path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Prerender }] ``` `src/app/app.routes.ts` ```ts import { Routes } from '@angular/router'; export const routes: Routes = [ { path: '', children: [ { path: '', pathMatch: 'full', loadChildren: () => import('./home/home.routes') }, { path: 'pricing', loadChildren: () => import('./pricing/pricing.routes') }, ], }, ]; ``` `src/app/home/home.routes.ts` (and `src/app/pricing/pricing.routes.ts`, the same with `./pricing-page`) ```ts import { Routes } from '@angular/router'; export default [{ path: '', loadComponent: () => import('./home-page') }] satisfies Routes; ``` `src/app/home/home-page.ts` (and `src/app/pricing/pricing-page.ts`, the same with `PricingPage`) ```ts import { Component } from '@angular/core'; @Component({ template: '

Home page

' }) export default class HomePage {} ``` ```bash npx ng build grep -o ']*>' dist/repro/browser/index.html # nothing grep -o ']*>' dist/repro/browser/pricing/index.html # 2 links ``` Workaround that brings `/` back to its hint, the page as a top-level route: ```ts export const routes: Routes = [ { path: '', pathMatch: 'full', loadComponent: () => import('./home/home-page') }, { path: 'pricing', loadChildren: () => import('./pricing/pricing.routes') }, ]; ``` ### Exception or Error ```text None. The build succeeds ("Prerendered 2 static routes.") and both pages render their content; only the modulepreload hints of `/` are missing. ``` ### Your Environment ```text Angular CLI : 22.2.2 Angular : 22.2.2 Node.js : 24.21.0 Package Manager : npm 11.19.0 Operating System : darwin arm64 @angular/build 22.2.2 @angular/cli 22.2.2 @angular/common 22.2.2 @angular/compiler 22.2.2 @angular/compiler-cli 22.2.2 @angular/core 22.2.2 @angular/forms 22.2.2 @angular/platform-browser 22.2.2 @angular/platform-server 22.2.2 @angular/router 22.2.2 @angular/ssr 22.2.2 rxjs 7.8.2 typescript 6.0.3 ``` ### Anything else relevant? - At the root, one empty-path level under another is enough: a top-level `{ path: '', pathMatch: 'full', loadChildren: () => import('./home/home.routes') }` with no componentless wrapper also gives `/` 0 hints. So removing only the wrapper is not a workaround; the page itself must be the top-level `''` route. - Not specific to the root: `{ path: 'es', children: [{ path: '', pathMatch: 'full', loadChildren: ... }, { path: 'pricing', loadChildren: ... }] }` gives `/es` 0 hints and `/es/pricing` 2. - The per-route `preload` feature itself worked in 19.1.0–19.1.5; the `seenRoutes` dedupe appears in 19.1.6 and is still there in 22.2.2.

title: `ng serve` crashes with `EMFILE: too many open files, watch` on macOS when `preserveSymlinks` is enabled (22.2 regression)
body:
### Command

serve

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

22.1.9

### Description

Since 22.2.0, `ng serve` (and any watch build) crashes on macOS right after the first successful build when the build target sets `preserveSymlinks: true` and the workspace contains more than 4096 directories outside `node_modules`.

`setupWatcher` passes `preserveSymlinks` on as `followSymlinks`, and `createWatcher` then always picks chokidar over `@parcel/watcher`:

```js
if (options?.polling || options?.followSymlinks) {
  return createChokidarWatcher(options);
}
```

Chokidar 5 calls `fs.watch` once per directory and file under the workspace root. On macOS, Node reports `EMFILE` as soon as one process holds more than 4096 directory watches: 4096 `fs.watch` calls on directories work, 4097 fail. File watches do not count towards this (50,000 worked), and `ulimit -n` has no influence: the crash reproduces with the hard limit at `unlimited`.

The error is emitted on the `FSWatcher` without a listener, so the dev server process exits.

In our application (about 1,250 source directories plus the packages it imports from `node_modules`, which chokidar also watches whole) the dev server made 33,703 `fs.watch` calls before crashing. With 22.1.9 and watchpack the same workspace needs 4. We depend on `preserveSymlinks` because plugin frontends are symlinked into `src/`.

### Minimal Reproduction

On macOS:

```sh
npx @angular/cli@22.2 new emfile-repro --defaults --skip-git
cd emfile-repro
node -e "for (let i = 0; i < 4200; i++) fs.mkdirSync('many/d' + i, { recursive: true })"
npx ng config projects.emfile-repro.architect.build.options.preserveSymlinks true
npx ng serve
```

The server prints its local URL and exits a moment later with the error below. It keeps running with `preserveSymlinks` unset, or with 3000 directories instead of 4200.

### Exception or Error

```text
Error: EMFILE: too many open files, watch
    at FSWatcher._handle.onchange (node:internal/fs/watchers:267:21)
Emitted 'error' event on FSWatcher instance at:
    at FSWatcher._handleError (node_modules/chokidar/index.js:558:18)
    at NodeFsHandler._boundHandleError (node_modules/chokidar/handler.js:297:49)
    at node_modules/chokidar/handler.js:144:9
    at foreach (node_modules/chokidar/handler.js:76:9)
    at fsWatchBroadcast (node_modules/chokidar/handler.js:143:5)
    at FSWatcher.<anonymous> (node_modules/chokidar/handler.js:191:17)
    at FSWatcher.emit (node:events:509:28)
    at FSWatcher._handle.onchange (node:internal/fs/watchers:273:12) {
  errno: -24,
  syscall: 'watch',
  code: 'EMFILE',
  filename: null
}
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.2
Angular           : 22.2.2
Node.js           : 24.18.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.16.0
Operating System  : darwin arm64 (macOS 27.0.1)

@angular/build            22.2.2
@angular/cli              22.2.2
@angular/compiler-cli     22.2.2
typescript                6.0.3
```

### Anything else relevant?

`@parcel/watcher` loads and subscribes fine on the same machine, so this is not the load-failure fallback. With `preserveSymlinks` off the dev server holds no `fs.watch` handles at all. Would it be possible to keep the parcel watcher for `preserveSymlinks` workspaces, or to limit chokidar to the files the build actually reports instead of the whole workspace root?

Workaround: pin `@angular/build` to 22.1.9, or run with `--watch false`.

title: compiler: stateful /g and /y regular expression literals inside template array/object literals are memoized in pure functions
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

compiler

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

Template regex optimization deliberately skips regular expression literals with stateful flags (`g` and `y`) using `SAFE_REGEX_FLAGS` in [`regular_expression_optimization.ts`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/0dafb368349f6d2c436296801f2f642747899d2d/packages/compiler/src/template/pipeline/src/phases/regular_expression_optimization.ts#L15-L48), because calling `.test()` or `.exec()` mutates `.lastIndex`.

When used directly (e.g. `{{ /hello/g.test(value) }}`), the compiler emits the literal inline so each evaluation gets a fresh `RegExp` instance.

However, [`RegularExpressionLiteralExpr.isConstant()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/0dafb368349f6d2c436296801f2f642747899d2d/packages/compiler/src/output/output_ast.ts#L577-L579) unconditionally returns `true` without checking `this.flags`. As a result, when a `/g` or `/y` regular expression appears inside an array or object literal in a template, [`generatePureLiteralStructures`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/0dafb368349f6d2c436296801f2f642747899d2d/packages/compiler/src/template/pipeline/src/phases/pure_literal_structures.ts#L37-L95) treats the entry as constant and hoists the structure into a 0-argument pure function (`ɵɵpureFunction0`), caching and reusing the exact same `RegExp` instance across checks.

Because `.test()` advances `.lastIndex` on `/g` and `/y` regexes (e.g. from `0` to `5` after matching `'hello'`), reusing the memoized instance causes subsequent evaluations on the same input to return `false`. In dev mode, this throws `NG0100: ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenCheckedError` on the first `detectChanges()` pass (between the initial check and `checkNoChanges`); in production, results flip between `true` and `false` across change detection runs.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

Minimal component reproduction (verified locally in `packages/core/test/acceptance/integration_spec.ts` via `bazel test //packages/core/test/acceptance:acceptance`):

```ts
import {ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component} from '@angular/core';

@Component({
  template: '{{ [/hello/g][0].test(value) }}|{{ {re: /hello/y}.re.test(value) }}',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.Eager,
})
export class App {
  value = 'hello';
}
```

Expected rendered output after `detectChanges()`: `true|true` (and remaining `true|true` on subsequent `detectChanges()` calls).

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```text
Error: NG0100: ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenCheckedError: Expression has changed after it was checked. Previous value: 'true'. Current value: 'false'. Expression location: App component. Find more at https://next.angular.dev/errors/NG0100
    at throwErrorIfNoChangesMode (./packages/core/src/render3/errors.ts:85:9)
    at bindingUpdated (./packages/core/src/render3/bindings.ts:68:9)
    at bindingUpdated2 (./packages/core/src/render3/bindings.ts:89:21)
    at interpolation2 (./packages/core/src/render3/instructions/interpolation.ts:82:21)
    at ɵɵtextInterpolate2 (./packages/core/src/render3/instructions/text_interpolation.ts:112:24)
    at App_Template (ng:///App.js:8:17)
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```text
@angular/compiler: 22.3.0-next.4 (main @ 0dafb368349f6d2c436296801f2f642747899d2d)
Node: v26.10.0
OS: darwin arm64
```

### Anything else?

Related prior change: commit `636cc9410523b7a78ed0360c720ae44713746170` introduced `SAFE_REGEX_FLAGS` in `regular_expression_optimization.ts`, whereas `RegularExpressionLiteralExpr.isConstant()` still returns `true` regardless of flags.

body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

common

### Is this a regression?

### Description

### Bug

Hi Angular team! When a search filter has no selected tags, passing `tag: []` to `HttpParams` makes `has('tag')` return `true` and `get('tag')` return `undefined`. The serialized URL omits `tag`.

### Minimal reproduction

```ts
import { HttpParams } from '@angular/common/http';

const params = new HttpParams({ fromObject: { tag: [], page: 1 } });

params.has('tag');  // Actual: true      Expected: false
params.get('tag');  // Actual: undefined Expected: null
params.toString();  // 'page=1'
```

### Cause and possible fix

The constructor stores the empty array in the `fromObject` branch. `has()` finds the key, and `get()` reads the missing first element. Skipping empty arrays would match `appendAll()`. [Relevant code in params.ts](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/0dafb368349f6d2c436296801f2f642747899d2d/packages/common/http/src/params.ts#L165-L198)

title: compiler: interpolation ends early when a regular expression literal contains }}
body:
### Bug

Hi Angular team! Angular treats `}}` inside a regular expression literal as the end of an interpolation.

### Minimal reproduction

```html
{{ /[}}]/u.test('}') }}
```

Expected `true`. Actual `Unexpected closing block`. The same expression fails in a `title` interpolation with `Unterminated regular expression` but parses successfully in a property binding. The equivalent pattern `/[}]/u` also parses in interpolation. AOT compilation with `ngc` reports `NG5002` for `{{ /}}/.test('}}') }}`.

### Cause and possible fix

The scanners appear to treat `}}` inside the regex as a closing delimiter. A possible fix is to skip regex literal contents while preserving division expressions such as `{{ 6 / 2 }}`. [HTML lexer](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/0dafb368349f6d2c436296801f2f642747899d2d/packages/compiler/src/ml_parser/lexer.ts#L1280-L1334) · [Expression parser](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/0dafb368349f6d2c436296801f2f642747899d2d/packages/compiler/src/expression_parser/parser.ts#L523-L537)

### Environment

Angular compiler 22.2.5, Node.js 24.22.2, macOS arm64. Regression status unknown.

title: compiler: distinct array literals can share a constant pool key and produce incorrect results
body:
### Bug

Hi Angular team! Two different array literals in the same template can share a constant pool key. The template compiles but returns the wrong result.

### Minimal reproduction

Use this as a component template:

```html
{{ ["a", "b"].length }}|{{ ['a","b'].length }}
```

Expected `2|1`. Actual `2|2` in JIT and AOT. Reversing the expressions in JIT produces `1|1` instead of `1|2`.

### Cause and possible fix

`GenericKeyFn.keyOf()` wraps strings in quotes without escaping embedded quotes, giving both arrays the same key. Returning `JSON.stringify(expr.value)` in the string branch produced the expected result in local JIT and AOT tests. [Relevant code in constant_pool.ts](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/0dafb368349f6d2c436296801f2f642747899d2d/packages/compiler/src/constant_pool.ts#L247-L259)

### Environment

Angular compiler 22.2.5, Node.js 24.22.2, macOS arm64. Regression status unknown.

### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

None of them; this is about the agent skills in `skills/dev-skills`, which are published to https://github.com/angular/skills. That repo's README sends feedback to this tracker.

### Description

Angular already ships agent skills in `skills/dev-skills` (published to `angular/skills`): `angular-developer`, `angular-new-app`. 

What I couldn't find is a one-command install for Claude Code or Codex. Both can install a plugin from a git repository that carries a small marketplace file, and the file can point at skills a repo already has, so nothing needs copying or maintaining twice.

**Proposal:** add `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at the repo root, along these lines:

```json
{
  "name": "angular",
  "owner": {
    "name": "Angular"
  },
  "description": "Angular agent skills",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "angular",
      "source": "./skills/dev-skills",
      "strict": false,
      "skills": [
        "./angular-developer",
        "./angular-new-app"
      ],
      "description": "Angular agent skills for Claude Code"
    }
  ]
}
```

Then `claude plugin marketplace add <owner>/<repo>` followed by `claude plugin install angular@angular` installs the skills. Codex has its own marketplace file (`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, documented at https://developers.openai.com/codex/plugins/build) and could be added the same way if you want it.

**What I checked:** I validated and installed exactly this manifest in Claude Code against a stand-in folder with the same layout and placeholder `SKILL.md` files named like yours; `claude plugin details` listed all 2 skills. Separately I installed Chakra UI's real `skills/` through a different marketplace with a `git-subdir` source, and its three skills appeared with no change to Chakra's repo. I only read each skill's front matter and README to judge that they are meant for end users.

If you'd rather not carry a marketplace file, tell me and I won't pursue it. I'm not offering a PR unless you ask for one.

<sub>Drafted with Claude Code.</sub>

### Proposed solution

A `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` as above, in whichever location flows to `angular/skills` through your publishing setup. I don't know how that output is generated, so I haven't guessed at the path.

### Alternatives considered

Keeping `npx skills add https://github.com/angular/skills` as the only install route, which works for tools that read that format but is not a one-command install inside Claude Code or Codex.

title: KeyValuePipe keeps the previous sort order when compareFn changes to null
[Feature Request] Resolve conflicting classes from a component, its directives, and its template
Report bindings that have no effect on ng-container, ng-template, and ng-content
body:
### Which @angular/\* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

compiler, compiler-cli, core

### Description

`<ng-container>`, `<ng-template>`, and `<ng-content>` don't render an element. Angular accepts
bindings and attributes on them that can never take effect, and most of them compile and run
without a word:

```html
<ng-container class="card" [class.active]="isActive" (click)="select()">...</ng-container>
<ng-template [title]="label" (click)="missing()">...</ng-template>
<ng-content selector="h1" />
```

Nothing on these lines does anything:

- Class, style, and event bindings on `<ng-container>` and `<ng-template>` are ignored, unless a
  directive claims them.
- Bindings that no directive claims on `<ng-template>` aren't type-checked, so
  `(click)="missing()"` compiles.
- `<ng-content>` ignores every binding, and every attribute except `select` and `ngProjectAs`. The
  `selector` typo (for `select`) silently makes the slot a default slot. Angular's own upgrade
  examples have had this typo since 2017.
- `NO_ERRORS_SCHEMA` hides unknown properties on `<ng-container>`, although no schema can give it
  a property.
- Inside `<svg>`, `[attr.x]` on `<ng-container>` skips its parse error and throws a misleading
  assertion in dev mode.

### Proposed solution

Report what Angular ignores, and nothing that takes effect. Code generation and runtime behavior
don't change.

**Step 1, not breaking:**

- **NG8031 `ignoredBinding`**, a new type-check diagnostic. It needs
  `strictTemplates`, is a warning by default, and is configured through
  `extendedDiagnostics.checks`, like NG8011. It reports class, style, `attr.`, animation, and
  event bindings that no directive claims, every binding on `<ng-content>`, and static attributes
  that nothing reads.
- **NG8032**, a template type-check warning for a component whose selector matches
  `<ng-container>` or `<ng-template>`. That compiles today and fails only when the template
  renders, in dev and production mode.
- The language service stops suggesting DOM attributes on `<ng-container>`.
- **NG0319**, a dev-mode runtime log for class, style, and event bindings on `<ng-container>` and
  `<ng-template>`, so JIT is covered too.
- The `<svg>` parse fix.

**Step 2, breaking:** severities only, in two independent PRs.

- NG8032 is an error.
- NG8031 is an error by default, and NG0319 throws under `errorOnUnknownProperties`.

Every new error points at a binding or component that never worked. NG8031 can be set back to
`"warning"` or `"suppress"`.

Not reported: bindings a directive claims, directive host bindings (directives are reusable),
global event targets, and static attributes that a directive, a structural directive, a content
projection slot, or Angular itself reads.

Question for the team: are the step 2 PRs fine for a minor release, or should they wait for a
major? They can land separately.

PRs: #71882 (step 1); #71883 (NG8032 error) and #71884 (NG8031 error), each building on #71882

### Alternatives considered

- **A template parse error.** The linker re-parses published libraries, so a parse error would
  break libraries that compile today.
- **Only an extended diagnostic.** It can warn, but step 2 needs the same check in the type
  checker. One check in the type checker serves both levels.
- **Only a runtime error.** It reports late, in dev mode only, and can't see bindings on
  `<ng-content>` or which static attributes something reads.
- **Also reporting directive host bindings.** A directive can apply to elements where those
  bindings work, so reporting them would be noise.

title: Feature request: Type-safe component CSS with implicit "$styles" in templates
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

compiler, compiler-cli

### Description

Angular provides style encapsulation but doesn't type-check CSS class references in templates. Renaming or removing a class from a component stylesheet can silently break its usage.

Validating existing `class` attributes or `[class.name]` bindings isn't viable because classes may come from global stylesheets, Tailwind, or third-party libraries.




### Proposed solution


Introduce an implicit, compiler-provided `$styles` object in Angular templates, exposing class names declared in the component's own stylesheets (`styleUrl`, `styleUrls`, or inline `styles`).

**Example:**

```css
/* button.component.css */
.primary { background: blue; }
.loading { opacity: 0.5; }
```

```html
<!-- Existing syntax remains unrestricted -->
<button class="flex items-center" [class.loading]="loading()">
  Save
</button>

<!-- Explicitly type-checked local CSS references -->
<button [class]="$styles.primary">Save</button>
<button [class]="$styles.missing">Save</button>
<!-- Error: 'missing' does not exist -->
```

This could enable compile-time diagnostics, autocomplete, go-to-definition, and rename refactoring across templates and stylesheets.

### Alternatives considered

TypeScript 7.1 content mappers could potentially provide stylesheet-derived types to Angular's existing template type-checking infrastructure.

`$styles` would be a compile-time abstraction resolving to ordinary class names, requiring no runtime object, CSS Modules imports, or changes to Angular's existing view encapsulation.

Angular would control the content mapper and language service highlighting.
Can leverage css modules under the hood. The limitation is not having access to the $styles  object in the ts but existing `@let` synax should be good enough for dynamic class composition directly in the template.

Edge case: `<component [prop]="$styles" (emit)="handler($styles)/>` - can leak into the ts. Which basicaly forces a css module implementation if to be supported. Alternative is compile error.

css modules had been rejected before when used "as is", but this is a controlled angular api that would leverage content mappers so it deserves a discussion.

title: NgOptimizedImage makes the browser select each image source again during hydration
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

common

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

During hydration, `NgOptimizedImage` makes the browser select the source of each image again. There are two separate causes.

**The directive writes its attributes again.** `setHostAttributes()` calls `renderer.setAttribute()` for `src`, `srcset`, `sizes`, and six other attributes. The server rendered the same values. A draft pull request skips the writes when the element already has the value.

**The value of `sizes` changes twice on a lazy image.** The directive prepends `auto` to `sizes` on lazy images, so the value that it computes differs from the template. This happens only on a lazy image with a static `sizes` attribute:

```text
server HTML            sizes="auto, 50vw"
hydration, core        sizes="50vw"          setupStaticAttributes() writes the template value
hydration, directive   sizes="auto, 50vw"    setHostAttributes() prepends auto again
```

The directive computes the same value on the server and in the browser, but core's write runs before the directive exists. Each of these two writes really changes the value, so checking for an unchanged value doesn't remove them.

The browser also fires `load` again on images that loaded before hydration. Event replay delivers the original `load` event too, so a `(load)` handler runs twice on those images.

On a page with 200 images, where hydration starts after the window `load` event, hydration takes 35.0 ms today and 27.7 ms with the draft pull request. When the same page uses `[width]`, `[height]`, and `[sizes]` bindings, which core doesn't write to the DOM, hydration takes 9.9 ms with the draft pull request.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/jsaguet/ngimg-hydration-repro

To see the `(load)` handler run twice, run `npm ci`, `npm run build:variants`, and `npm run serve:stock`, and open `http://localhost:4000/?bootAfterLoad`. A badge under each image counts the calls. The README has the measurements.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

No exception.

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```
Angular CLI       : 22.2.6
Angular           : 22.2.5
Node.js           : 26.11.1
Package Manager   : npm 11.20.0
Chrome            : 156
```

### Anything else?

Until the `sizes` case is fixed, bind the input, for example `[sizes]="'50vw'"`, so that core doesn't write it to the DOM.

I don't have a proposal for the `sizes` case that I'm confident about. These are the options I looked at:

- Don't prepend `auto` when the template already has it, so that a developer can write `sizes="auto, 50vw"`. This is one condition in the directive. It helps only the templates that change.
- Make the check in core treat `auto, X` in the DOM as equal to `X` in the template. This covers existing templates, but core would then know about something that the directive does.
- Let a directive declare the host attributes that it writes itself, so that core doesn't write them. This covers existing templates, and it adds an internal mechanism for a single attribute.

Which direction would you prefer, if this case is worth fixing?

title: Hydration writes values that the server already rendered, which restarts playing videos
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

core

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

During hydration, Angular writes values that the server already rendered, and the browser reacts to each write.

A video with `autoplay` starts playing as soon as the browser parses the server HTML. When Angular hydrates the page, the video jumps back to the start. All of these templates have the problem:

```html
<video src="clip.webm" autoplay muted></video>
<video [src]="clip" autoplay muted></video>
<video [attr.src]="clip" autoplay muted></video>
```

There are two causes:

- `elementLikeStartShared()` calls `setupStaticAttributes()` on every element, including DOM nodes reused from the server. It writes each static attribute, the static `class`, and the static `style` again.
- On the first update after hydration, attribute and property bindings write their values, because they have no previous value to compare with.

In Chrome, writing the same value to `src` restarts the load algorithm of a media element. Writing the same `src` to an `<iframe>` loads a new document. I checked the `<iframe>` case in plain JavaScript, not in an Angular app.

The writes also cost time. On a table with 300 rows of static classes, ARIA attributes, and SVG icons, hydration makes 12,961 attribute writes, and 12,871 of them keep the same value. After hydration, Chrome restyles 1,247 elements.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/jsaguet/ngimg-hydration-repro

To see the video restart, run `npm ci`, `npm run build:variants`, and `npm run serve:stock`, and open `http://localhost:4000/media?bootAfterLoad&bootDelay=3000`. The README has screenshots and measurements.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

No exception. The video restarts during hydration.

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```
Angular CLI       : 22.2.6
Angular           : 22.2.5
Node.js           : 26.11.1
Package Manager   : npm 11.20.0
Chrome            : 156
```

### Anything else?

A draft pull request follows with one possible fix. It writes a value during hydration only if the DOM has a different value. The problem stands if you prefer another approach.

A fix affects event handlers that run today only because of these writes. For example, a `(canplay)` handler on a video that was ready before hydration runs once today, because the video restarts. It wouldn't run after a fix, because event replay doesn't cover `canplay`.

title: language-server: project reload loop and OOM with a deleted open TS file and solution-style external template (22.2.0)
body:
### Is this a bug report or a feature request?

- [x] Bug Report
- [ ] Feature Request

### Summary

Angular Language Service 22.2.0 entered a self-sustaining project-reload/diagnostics loop in a multi-root Nx workspace. A TypeScript file had been deleted on disk while its editor remained open, and an external Angular component template from a different worktree was also open. The server repeatedly failed to find the deleted file's configured project, reloaded/re-analyzed the template's library project roughly every 1–2 seconds, and eventually aborted with a JavaScript heap OOM near 4 GB.

Closing the two editors associated with the deleted path (ordinary editor and Git diff), then running **Angular: Restart Angular Language server**, stopped the loop without reloading VS Code. The external template remained open and its language features worked afterwards.

### Please provide the steps to reproduce the issue [Bug Report only]

**Observed sequence in the affected workspace; not yet independently reproduced in a standalone minimal project:**

1. Open an Nx monorepo in VS Code with multiple linked worktree folders in one multi-root window.
2. Keep an external `.component.html` template open in a library whose `tsconfig.json` is solution-style (`files: []` with references to the library/spec configs). Its sibling component TypeScript editor is not open.
3. Have a TypeScript editor open in another worktree, then delete that TypeScript file on disk while leaving its editor open. In the observed incident, both its ordinary editor and Git diff remained open.
4. The server repeatedly logs `No config file` for the deleted path, interleaved with repeated enabling of the template library project.
5. Within approximately 43–60 seconds per process lifetime, the heap reaches approximately 4 GB and the server aborts. Automatic restarts repeat the same sequence until the language client gives up after five crashes in three minutes.

There is no public minimal reproduction yet; the original workspace is private. The path names and layout below are anonymized. These steps describe the observed state and sequence, not a confirmed universal reproducer.

### Please provide the expected behavior vs the actual behavior you encountered [Bug Report only]

**Expected:** An editor whose file was removed from disk should not cause repeated teardown/recreation and full Angular analysis of another open template's configured project. The server should settle and continue providing template features.

**Actual:** The same project-loading messages repeat about once per second, including repeated `No config file` errors for the deleted TS path. The server exhausts its heap, restarts, and eventually stops restarting. Template diagnostics/navigation become unavailable.

**Recovery observed:** Close only the saved editors for the deleted path, then restart the Angular language server. With the same workspace folders and external template still open, the log settled after about eight seconds. The replacement process remained alive for more than four minutes at approximately 1.4 GB RSS, with no further missing-file messages or crash. Template-to-component navigation was manually verified. This is current-session recovery, not evidence of permanent prevention.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw [Bug Report only]

Representative excerpt, with paths anonymized:

```text
[Info  - 19:44:51] Disabling language service for /workspace/worktree-a/tsconfig.json because project is not an Angular project ('@angular/core' could not be found).
[Error - 19:44:51] No config file for /workspace/worktree-a/libs/backend/src/deleted-file.ts
[Info  - 19:44:51] Disabling language service for /workspace/worktree-b/tsconfig.json because project is not an Angular project ('@angular/core' could not be found).
[Info  - 19:44:51] Enabling language service for /workspace/worktree-b/libs/frontend/shared/tsconfig.lib.json.
[Info  - 19:44:52] Disabling language service for /workspace/worktree-a/tsconfig.json because project is not an Angular project ('@angular/core' could not be found).
[Error - 19:44:52] No config file for /workspace/worktree-a/libs/backend/src/deleted-file.ts
[Info  - 19:44:53] Disabling language service for /workspace/worktree-b/tsconfig.json because project is not an Angular project ('@angular/core' could not be found).
[Info  - 19:44:53] Enabling language service for /workspace/worktree-b/libs/frontend/shared/tsconfig.lib.json.

[3348:0x12800810000] 43091 ms: Scavenge 4014.9 (4071.5) -> 4002.6 (4083.2) MB, pooled: 0.0 MB, 4.70 / 0.00 ms (average mu = 0.527, current mu = 0.565) allocation failure;
[3348:0x12800810000] 43122 ms: Scavenge 4026.8 (4083.2) -> 4011.4 (4090.7) MB, pooled: 0.0 MB, 4.83 / 0.00 ms (average mu = 0.527, current mu = 0.565) allocation failure;

FATAL ERROR: MarkCompactCollector: young object promotion failed Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
[Error - 19:45:28] Server process exited with signal SIGABRT.
[Error - 19:45:28] The Angular Language Service server crashed 5 times in the last 3 minutes. The server will not be restarted. See the output for more information.
```

### Environment

- VS Code: 1.145.0
- OS: macOS 26.6.2, arm64
- Extension: `angular.ng-template` 22.2.0
- Loaded `@angular/language-service`: 22.2.0
- Loaded `typescript/lib/tsserverlibrary`: 6.0.3
- Angular in the affected worktrees: 22.2.4. Other folders in the multi-root window use 21.2.10 and 22.1.8.
- Multi-root window: 35 linked worktree folders
- Server runtime: VS Code's `Code Helper (Plugin)` process
- `angular.server.useClientSideFileWatcher`: enabled (visible in the server arguments)

The same window/folder set was stable for approximately 20 minutes before the deleted-file error/reload loop began. Workspace size may amplify the cost, but does not by itself explain the transition into the continuous loop.

### Suspected mechanism (code-traced; not an isolated reproduction)

There appears to be an interaction between external-template project recovery and TypeScript project cleanup:

1. Project loading calls `enableLanguageServiceForProject`, which performs Angular analysis and `refreshDiagnostics()`.
2. A projects-updated event schedules diagnostics for open files.
3. For the deleted TypeScript file, `getDefaultProjectForScriptInfo` calls `openClientFile`, cannot find a configured project, and reports `No config file`.
4. TypeScript's open-client-file path also runs orphan project cleanup. A solution-style template's association established by `attachToComponentProject` may not be preserved by that cleanup.
5. Processing the still-open external template then calls `loadProjectForExternalTemplate` / `attachToComponentProject`, loading and analyzing the library project again and scheduling more diagnostics.

This is consistent with the repeated log sequence and the observed recovery, but **the exact heap-retention cause and causality of every internal step have not been independently established**.

The recovery methods are present in [14fbe04612](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/14fbe04612d29460c5d01d6c65cde579f0a42e95), which fixed #69768. This may be a relevant interaction/regression to investigate, not a claim that the commit alone is proven to cause the OOM.

An earlier log episode also showed repeated external-template project reloads and OOMs without a deleted-file error, so a deleted TS file may be one trigger rather than a necessary condition.

Related reports checked: #65356 and #65484 describe older language-service OOM incidents, but do not identify this particular solution-style template/project-reload sequence.

title: Router: with canceledNavigationResolution 'computed', cancelling the first navigation after a reload calls history.go() with a stale page id
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

router

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

With `canceledNavigationResolution: 'computed'`, cancelling (or erroring) the **first navigation after a page reload** makes the router call `history.go()` with a non-zero delta, so the browser jumps to an unrelated history entry instead of staying on the current one.

Cause (from `HistoryStateManager` in `_router-chunk.mjs`, 22.2.3):

- `currentPageId` starts at `0` in every new app instance.
- After a reload (or when the user comes back from another site via Back), `history.state` still carries the previous instance's `ɵrouterPageId` (for example `2`), and the initial navigation restores that state, so `browserPageId` returns `2`.
- If that initial navigation is cancelled (a guard returns `false`, a resolver errors, a `NavigationError` happens), `restoreHistory()` computes `targetPagePosition = this.currentPageId - this.browserPageId = 0 - 2` and calls `this.location.historyGo(-2)`.
- `lastSuccessfulId` is still `-1` at that point: there is no previous router-owned position to go back to, so any non-zero `historyGo` is wrong. If the first navigation keeps failing (e.g. a guard that rejects on startup), the app walks back through the history one batch at a time.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

No StackBlitz yet; minimal steps:

1. `provideRouter(routes, withRouterConfig({ canceledNavigationResolution: 'computed' }))` with routes `/a`, `/b`, `/c`, where `/c` has a `canActivate` guard that returns `false` when a flag (e.g. a `sessionStorage` key) is set.
2. Navigate in-app `/a` → `/b` → `/c`. `history.state.ɵrouterPageId` is now `2` on the `/c` entry.
3. Set the flag and reload the page on `/c`.

Expected: the cancelled initial navigation leaves the history position unchanged (at most resets the URL of the current entry).
Actual: the router calls `history.go(-2)` and the browser ends up on the entry before `/a`.

The same happens when the initial navigation fails for other reasons (startup error in a guard, a resolver throwing), and when the user returns with Back from another site to an entry that carries a page id.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
No exception; the browser silently navigates to another history entry (history.go(0 - restoredPageId)).
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular: 22.2.3 (router 22.2.3)
Browser: Chrome (latest stable)
```

### Anything else?

Possible fixes:
- When the initial navigation restores a state with `ɵrouterPageId`, initialize `currentPageId` from it (so `currentPageId - browserPageId === 0` until a navigation succeeds), or
- In `restoreHistory()` for `'computed'`, skip `historyGo` when no navigation has succeeded yet (`lastSuccessfulId === -1`) and only reset the URL of the current entry.

Our workaround is to never cancel the first navigation: guards return `NEVER` (hold the navigation) instead of `false`/`UrlTree` on startup failures, which is not obvious and changes first-navigation semantics.
