title: zone.js: Promise reactions cause cross request `AsyncLocalStorage` context leakage in SSR
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

zone.js

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description


With zone.js loaded on the server, `AsyncLocalStorage.getStore()` can return the store of a different SSR request.

zone.js replaces the global `Promise`. In `then()` it saves `Zone.current`, but not Node's async context promise
 https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/124bf448091d0b2314275ca9bed12d82b3b7ef7e/packages/zone.js/lib/common/promise.ts#L545-L550

The reactions then go into one queue for the whole process, and the queue is drained from a single native microtask, scheduled by whatever queued first 

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/124bf448091d0b2314275ca9bed12d82b3b7ef7e/packages/zone.js/lib/zone-impl.ts#L1513-L1565

Node runs that microtask in the async context of the code that scheduled it. So when two requests have reactions in the same drain, all of them run with the first request's store. `Zone.current` is still right for each task, and `inject(REQUEST)` was right in every render I measured. What's wrong is Node's async context, which is what `AsyncLocalStorage` reads.

A lot of server code finds the current request that way: express-http-context, a pino logger with a request context, OpenTelemetry's context manager, Sentry. In my test app an interceptor forwards the user's token from express-http-context, and 20 concurrent renders called the backend with the same user's token.

Code in the app always goes through `then()`, because with zone.js in `polyfills` the CLI compiles `async`/`await` to generators over the global `Promise`. In both apps below, the zone.js server bundle has no native `await` left, while the zoneless build of the same source keeps 70 (Angular 22) and 80 (Angular 21).

```text
node v24.16.0, zone.js 0.16.3

test                          request   Zone.current   als.getStore()  verdict
A same-turn .then()           victim    req-victim     victim          ok
A same-turn .then()           attacker  req-attacker   victim          LEAK
B shared in-flight promise    victim    req-victim     victim          ok
B shared in-flight promise    attacker  req-attacker   victim          LEAK
C still wrong 3 hops later    victim    req-victim     victim          ok
C still wrong 3 hops later    attacker  req-attacker   victim          LEAK
D native await                victim    <root>         victim          ok
D native await                attacker  <root>         attacker        ok

AsyncLocalStorage store from another request: 3/8
Zone.current from another request:            0/8 (2 are <root> after native await)
```

With 0.16.3 it's the same on Node 20.19.5, 22.23.4, 24.16.0 and 26.13.0,


Two renders have to be waiting on the same pending work. 

| | what both renders wait on | what the app needs | first requests of a process | after warm-up |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the SSR manifest's `import()` of `main.server.mjs` and the index HTML | nothing | yes | no |
| 2 | the router's `loadComponent` | a lazy route that reads the identity | yes | no |
| 3 | the chunk of a `@defer` block with a `hydrate` trigger | that block, with incremental hydration on | yes | no |
| 4 | every `import()`, once an async ESM loader hook is registered | `@sentry/node` on Node 22 | yes | yes |
| 5 | a request shared through a `useValue` provider | that provider | yes | yes |

In all five, the same app without zone.js is correct. The other pieces only decide when two renders end up in the same drain.

Angular 22.2.4, on the Node versions it supports. `/account`, 20 concurrent renders with their own session cookie, first requests of a new process. Distinct bearer tokens the backend received:

| | Node 22.23.4 | 24.22.2 | 26.13.0 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `@sentry/node` 11.10.0 with `--import`, no cache (4) | 1 | 20 | 20 |
| `useValue` cache (5) | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| neither | 20 | 20 | 20 |
| zoneless, with Sentry or with the cache | 20 | 20 | 20 |

The Sentry row has no cache and no shared state in the app, and it gives the same result with the manifest's imports loaded before the server starts listening. On Linux with Node 22.22.3, which is Angular 22's minimum, it's also 1 token for 20 renders. It keeps happening after warm-up: over three runs on 22.23.4 the backend got 14 to 16 distinct tokens for 100 renders, and 84 to 86 log lines had the wrong user.

Sentry uses the synchronous `module.registerHooks()` only on Node 24.13+ and 25.1+ (`@sentry/server-runtime-injection/build/cjs/register.js:28-34`). On older versions it registers two asynchronous `module.register()` hooks, and `@angular/ssr` imports the index HTML on every render (`ssr.mjs:1172`), so there is always an `import()` that two renders can wait on.

The cache in row 5 holds public settings and is shared on purpose: one `HttpClient` call, `shareReplay`, and `await firstValueFrom(...)` in each render. What crosses is the identity, not the cached value. After warm-up it was 69 tokens for 100 renders on 22.23.4 and 81 on 26.13.0.

The application doesn't have to use `AsyncLocalStorage` itself. I removed all the identity code and kept only OpenTelemetry's zero-code agent and the cache, and the backend received 1 trace id for 20 renders, on 22.23.4 and on 26.13.0. OpenTelemetry's context manager reads the store in `active()` (`AsyncLocalStorageContextManager.cjs:41`).

Cases 1 to 3 are inside Angular, and they need Node older than 22.18.0. Angular 21.2.26 on Node 22.17.1, 3 new processes with 20 concurrent requests each, renders that read another request's identity:

| route | zone.js | zoneless |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `/account`, identity read in a resolver (1) | 57/60 | 0/60 |
| `/profile`, lazy, identity read in the component (2) | 57/60 | 0/60 |
| `/` and `/settings`, `@defer (hydrate on …)` panel (3) | 30/33 | 0/33 |

Same numbers on 20.19.5 and 22.16.0. On `/account` without the cache, the backend received 1 distinct token for 20 renders and pino logged 19 of 20 lines under the wrong user. These three happen in the first requests of a process, after a deploy or a restart.

They stop at 22.18.0 because a new request arrives in an I/O callback, so it can only join an `import()` that is still pending after a turn of the event loop. One cold chunk import spans 11 to 18 turns on 22.17.1 and none on 22.18.0, the release with nodejs/node#57419 (*esm: syncify default path of `ModuleLoader.load`*). That covers Angular 21 on Node 20 and on Node 22 before 22.18.0.


### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/zone-als-leak

 ### Expected behavior

A reaction runs in the async context where `then()` was called, as it does with native promises, so each request's `AsyncLocalStorage.getStore()` returns its own store. Node's docs ask the same of a custom thenable implementation [async_context, Troubleshooting: Context loss](https://nodejs.org/api/async_context.html#troubleshooting-context-loss).

### Anything else?


It also works the other way around. If the attacker's request is the one that starts the shared fetch, the other renders in that burst run as the attacker: they load the attacker's account with the attacker's token, and whatever they write is recorded as the attacker.

This reminds me in part of [GHSA-68x2-mx4q-78m7](https://github.com/angular/angular/security/advisories/GHSA-68x2-mx4q-78m7), where concurrent SSR requests could also end up with another request's data. There it was the global platform injector; here it is Node's async context.

title: Detect LCP images after soft navigations in NgOptimizedImage
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

common

### Description

`NgOptimizedImage` warns during development when an LCP image is not marked as `priority`. I think it would be useful to extend this diagnostic to soft navigations, so it also covers images displayed after navigating between routes without reloading the page.

e.g navigating from a product list to a product detail page can introduce a different LCP image. 
Developers should receive the same missing-`priority` warning when the browser identifies that image as the LCP of the soft navigation.


### Proposed solution

Extend `LCPImageObserver` to observe `soft-navigation` and `interaction-contentful-paint` entries when supported, associating them through `interactionId`.

Only paints associated with a detected soft navigation should trigger this diagnostic. An unrelated interaction that displays another large image should not be treated as a new navigation.

Keep the existing initial-page-load observation and use feature detection so browsers without these entry types continue to work as they do today.


### Alternatives considered

I previously opened #69963  if someone can take care of it or suggest an better alternative

References 

* [Soft Navigations and Interaction Contentful Paint](https://github.com/WICG/soft-navigations).
* [Measuring soft navigations](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/soft-navigations)

title: Custom property style bindings ignore static and `[style]` values of same name since 22.1
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

compiler

### Is this a regression?

Yes, works in 22.0.8, broken in 22.2.4 and 22.3.0-next.3. Came with #68846

### Description

Hit this in my ui lib, had to move component inputs to separate variable

`[style.--x]` compiles to key `--%NS%x`, but static `style="--x: red"` and `[style]="'--x: red'"` keep `--x`. Styling priority looks values up by key, so these never mathc and binding stops seeing value of same name. `[style.color]` is not affected. No `provideCssVarNamespacing()` needed to hit this

- host binding `[style.--x]` now overwrites value author set on component element, before author won
- `undefined` no longer falls back to static or `[style]` value, element ends up without `--x`

| case | bound value | 22.0.8 | 22.2.4 | same case with `color`, 22.2.4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<my-cmp style="--x: red">` + host `[style.--x]` | `blue` | `--x: red` | `--x: blue` | `color: red` |
| `<my-cmp style="--x: red">` + host `[style.--x]` | `undefined` | `--x: red` | empty | `color: red` |
| `<i style="--x: red" [style.--x]="v">` | `undefined` | `--x: red` | empty | `color: red` |
| `<i [style]="'--x: red'" [style.--x]="v">` | `undefined` | `--x: red` | empty | `color: red` |
| host `style: '--x: red'` + host `[style.--x]` | `undefined` | `--x: red` | empty | `color: red` |

With `provideCssVarNamespacing('ns')` both stay on element: `--x: red; --ns_x: blue`

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

```ts
@Component({ selector: 'my-cmp', template: '', host: { '[style.--x]': 'v' } })
class MyCmp {
  @Input() v?: string;
}

@Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [MyCmp], template: `<my-cmp style="--x: red" v="blue" />` })
class App {}
```

`getAttribute('style')` on `my-cmp`: `--x: red` in 22.0.8, `--x: blue` in 22.2.4 and 22.3.0-next.3

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

None

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

@angular/core 22.0.8, 22.2.4 and 22.3.0-next.3, Chromium, JIT

### Anything else?

Compliance golden `style_bindings/css_custom_properties.js` shows same split: `--camel-case` in consts, `--%NS%camelCase` in `ɵɵstyleProp`

title: Two-way binding documentation is missing important information
body:
### Describe the problem that you experienced

When it comes to two-way binding (using the `model` signal), arguably the most important piece of information is that a `value = model<string>();` declared in a child component can be used in the parent's template as either:
1. Banana-in-a-box: `[(value)]="someValue"`
2. A pair of input and output: `[value]="someValue" (valueChange)="onSomeValueChanged($event)"`

And in the second case, we can additionally assume that whenever `someValue` changes in the parent component, and gets passed to child, `onSomeValueChanged()` will not immediately be called back on the parent component - which is critical for the "Data Down, Actions Up (DDAU)" / "unidirectional data flow" principle.

---

title: platform-server: Domino querySelector() returns undefined instead of null when nothing matches
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

platform-server

### Description

With SSR, `Document.querySelector()` and `Element.querySelector()` return `undefined` when nothing matches. The DOM spec (and `lib.dom.d.ts`, `Element | null`) says `null`. `DocumentFragment.querySelector` in the same library already returns `null`.

The bundled Domino (`@angular/platform-server/third_party/domino`) comes from `angular/domino`, where `lib/Document.js` and `lib/Element.js` have:

```js
querySelector: { value: function(selector) {
  return select(selector, this)[0];   // undefined when empty
}},
```

Because the typings promise `null`, code that type-checks fine under `strict` breaks on the server only:

```ts
const main = document.getElementById('app-content') ?? document.querySelector('main');
// browser: null; SSR: undefined
const targets = [document.body, main].filter((t): t is HTMLElement => t !== null);
// SSR: `undefined` passes the filter -> TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'classList')
```

### Minimal reproduction

```js
import domino from '@angular/platform-server/third_party/domino/bundled-domino.mjs';
const { document } = domino.createWindow('<html><body></body></html>', 'http://localhost/');
console.log(document.querySelector('main'));                  // undefined, expected null
console.log(document.body.querySelector('main'));             // undefined, expected null
console.log(document.createDocumentFragment().querySelector('main')); // null (correct)
```

Verified with `@angular/platform-server` 21.2.25.

### Proposed fix

`return select(selector, this)[0] || null;` in `Document.js` and `Element.js`. I have a patch plus a test ready for `angular/domino`. Note `test/domino.js` (added in angular/domino#48, "emptyAttributeTokenSelectors") currently asserts `undefined` with the comment "Preserve Domino's existing no-match return value"; that assertion would change to `null`.

Callers that rely on `null`/`undefined` equivalently (`if (x)`, `x ?? y`, `x?.y`, `x == null`) are unaffected. Only code checking `=== undefined` explicitly would notice, which is dead code against the typings.

Happy to open the PR against `angular/domino` if this change is acceptable.

### Related (separate, not part of this issue)

`querySelectorAll()` returns a list without `Symbol.iterator` in the bundled build, so `for (const el of document.querySelectorAll(...))` throws "is not iterable" on the server.

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in

Angular 21.2.25, `@angular/platform-server` 21.2.25, Node 22, SSR.

title: Unguarded Map access and leaked PendingTask in triggerHydrationForBlockQueue
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

core

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

`triggerHydrationForBlockQueue` in `packages/core/src/defer/triggering.ts` reads an entry from `DehydratedBlockRegistry.hydrating` without a guard, after two `await` points during which that entry can be removed.

The same Map is read three times in that function. Two of the three reads are optional-chained, one is not:

```ts
blocksBeingHydrated.get(dehydratedBlockId).resolve();   // unguarded
await blocksBeingHydrated.get(lastBlockName)?.promise;  // guarded
blocksBeingHydrated.get(dehydratedBlockId)?.reject();   // guarded
```

`DehydratedBlockRegistry.cleanup()` does `this.hydrating.delete(blockId)`, so the entry is genuinely removable while the function is suspended on `await triggerResourceLoadingForHydration()` or `await nextRender()`.

### Second defect in the same function

`pendingTasks.add()` runs at the top and `pendingTasks.remove(taskId)` further down, with no `try/finally` between them. When the unguarded access throws, the task is never released. `PendingTasksInternal` has no timeout, so `ApplicationRef.isStable` never becomes true again for that session, and anything gated on `whenStable()` or `isStable` silently stops working for the rest of the session.

Every caller of `triggerHydrationFromBlockName` is fire-and-forget, with no `await` and no `.catch()`, so the failure surfaces only as an unhandled rejection with no application frame in the stack.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

We could not build one, and we want to be upfront about that.

We built a minimal SSR app on 22.2.3 with `withIncrementalHydration()` and a `@defer (hydrate on idle)` under an `@if`, held the deferred chunk through network interception to widen the window, and destroyed the host view at several points. Six scenarios, including nested hydrate blocks, produced no error.

We believe this is because `ɵɵdefer` registers `storeTriggerCleanupFn(0, lDetails, () => removeLViewOnDestroy(lView, onLViewDestroy))`, so the destroy hook that would call `registry.cleanup()` is removed as soon as the block triggers. Something else removes the entry, and we have not identified it.

We are reporting this as a code defect rather than a reproducible behaviour: the missing `?.` and the missing `try/finally` are visible by inspection, and both fixes are small and independent of whatever triggers the removal.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'resolve')    // Chrome
TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'o.get(p).resolve') // Safari
TypeError: can't access property "resolve", o.get(...) is undefined   // Firefox
```

The throwing line is `packages/core/src/defer/triggering.ts:478`.

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in

Angular 22.2.3, SSR with incremental hydration, zoneless change detection. Chrome, Safari and Firefox, on desktop and mobile.

### Anything else?

Suggested fixes, both independent of the unknown trigger:

1. Optional-chain the read at `triggering.ts:478`, matching the two sibling reads in the same function.
2. Wrap the body of `triggerHydrationForBlockQueue` in `try/finally` so `pendingTasks.remove(taskId)` always runs.

The second one matters more than the error itself: a leaked pending task permanently breaks application stability for the rest of the session.

title: resource: obsolete loads keep the application unstable when params become unavailable
Template type checking drops errors that start at an arrow function parameter
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

compiler, compiler-cli

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

With `strictTemplates`, Angular doesn't report a type error in a template arrow function when TypeScript places that error at one of the function's parameters. The template compiles, and the mistake reaches runtime.

A common case is a callback that declares a parameter the caller never passes:

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  template: `<button (click)="retry((attempt) => load(attempt))">Retry</button>`,
})
export class App {
  retry(fn: () => void) {
    fn();
  }
  load(attempt: number) {}
}
```

`retry` calls `fn` with no arguments, so `attempt` is always `undefined`. In a `.ts` file, TypeScript rejects this call:

```text
TS2345: Argument of type '(attempt: any) => void' is not assignable to parameter of type '() => void'.
  Target signature provides too few arguments. Expected 1 or more, but got 0.
```

In the template, Angular reports nothing. The same happens when a callback returns a function instead of a value, such as `count.update((v) => () => v + 1)`.

TypeScript places most callback errors elsewhere, so Angular still reports them. For example, `count.update((v) => String(v))` reports TS2322 at `String(v)`.

Expected: Angular reports the error at the parameter (`attempt`), the same way it reports any other template type error.

**Cause:** the type-check code marks every arrow function parameter with a "skip diagnostics" comment ([expression.ts#L386](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/5d929e57e4/packages/compiler/src/typecheck/expression.ts#L386)), so [`findSourceLocation`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/5d929e57e4/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/src/tcb_util.ts#L211) drops every error that starts there. The marker was meant to hide implicit `any` errors on parameters that templates can't annotate, but [`shouldReportDiagnostic`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/5d929e57e4/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/src/diagnostics.ts#L29) already filters those by error code.

**Fix:** the linked PR gives each parameter its source location instead of the marker. Inferred parameter types don't change. Implicit `any` and unused-parameter errors stay hidden.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

No hosted reproduction. The snippet in the description is self-contained: paste it into any Angular 21.2+ app with `strictTemplates` turned on. The linked PR adds regression tests.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
None. The template compiles without errors.
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular: 21.2.0 and later, including 22.2.x and 22.3.0-next.2 (main at 5d929e57e4).
Reproduced with compiler-cli tests in packages/compiler-cli/test/ngtsc/template_typecheck_spec.ts.
```

### Anything else?

Template arrow functions were added in 21.2.0, and the marker has been there since.

title: docs(service-worker): applicationMaxAge is counted from the build timestamp, and the default is not documented
body:
### Describe the problem that you experienced

The `applicationMaxAge` section says it configures "how long the service worker will cache any requests", which reads as an age counted from when the files were cached on the device. In the worker, the age is actually counted from the manifest `timestamp`, which is set at build time (`timestamp: Date.now()` in the config generator):

```ts
const isVersionWithinMaxAge =
  appVersion?.manifest.applicationMaxAge === undefined ||
  this.adapter.time - appVersion.manifest.timestamp < appVersion.manifest.applicationMaxAge;
```

(`packages/service-worker/worker/src/driver.ts`)

So once the build is older than `applicationMaxAge`, every client bypasses the cache and goes to the network, even if the cached version is still the latest one deployed. If no new version is deployed within that window, the app no longer starts offline.

The page also does not say what happens when the property is not set: from the code above, there is no limit (cached versions are served regardless of age).

### Enter the URL of the topic with the problem

https://angular.dev/ecosystem/service-workers/config#applicationmaxage

### Describe what you were looking for in the documentation

From when the max age is counted, and the default behavior when `applicationMaxAge` is omitted.

### Describe the actions that led you to experience the problem

We set `"applicationMaxAge": "1d12h"`, expecting cached files to be refreshed after 36 hours on each device. Instead, 36 hours after each build, the service worker stopped serving the app from its cache on all devices. Online this is invisible (the network answers), but offline the app does not start until a new version is built and deployed.

### Describe what you want to experience that would fix the problem

State explicitly that:
- the age is measured from the build time (manifest `timestamp`), not from when the files were cached on the device;
- beyond it, the cache is bypassed even when no newer version exists, which disables offline support until the next deployment;
- when omitted, there is no maximum age (current default behavior).

title: Retain Angular animations in v23 until coordinated enter/leave has a supported migration path
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request? animations, core, platform-browser ### Description Please reconsider removing `@angular/animations` in v23 until there is a supported, behaviorally equivalent path for coordinated parent/child enter/leave animations, or a maintained compatibility package. I am asking sincerely as someone who wants to keep upgrading Angular, rather than freeze an application or maintain a private framework fork. Simple CSS fades are not the difficulty. The value for my application is Angular coordinating view lifetime, child queries, forward/reverse stagger, delayed entry and changing state through one reusable declaration. **Our actual setup** is a standalone, zoneless Angular media-editor application (currently testing Angular 22.1.8). A parent wizard reacts to its step signal and coordinates a child trigger inside each `@switch` branch: ```html
@switch (step()) { @case ('first') {

First step

} @case ('second') {

Second step

} }
``` The names/content above are shortened for this report. The animation structure and these timings come from our working shared triggers: ```ts const fadeItems = trigger('fadeItems', [ transition('* => *', [ query('@fadeItemsParent', animateChild(), { optional: true }), ]), ]); const fadeItemsParent = trigger('fadeItemsParent', [ transition(':enter', [ query('.fade-item', [ style({ opacity: 0 }), stagger(100, animate('250ms 469ms ease-in', style({ opacity: 1 }))), ], { optional: true }), ]), transition(':leave', [ query('.fade-item', [ stagger(-100, animate('250ms ease-out', style({ opacity: 0 }))), ], { optional: true }), ]), ]); ``` The real wizard uses overlapping/positioned step containers, so outgoing controls can finish fading while incoming controls appear after the entry delay. Callers mark their controls with `.fade-item`; they do not each manage animation parameters or lifecycle callbacks. Another current caller retains both form views and switches `HIDDEN`/`VISIBLE` states with the same shared trigger, preserving entered form data instead of destroying it. We also have an ordered variant for numbered child groups. **Evidence from our migration attempts:** I went back through the actual development records rather than relying on memory. - On 7 December 2025, we attempted a broad replacement with CSS/JavaScript/Web Animations, including a shared animation runner, structural enter/leave directive and fade-list directive, across the wizard, upload widgets, layout and video page. - The first result was only partly functional: I reported, “the fade out animation doesnt happen, it exits instantly.” The implementation had replaced parent-managed animations with enter-only list behavior, allowing outgoing DOM to disappear before the exit completed. - A subsequent pass replaced those list usages with a structural directive intended to retain the outgoing view. I still reported that the fade-out did not happen. - A further correction had to stop updating the old view's binding context before fading it out, then swap in a new view and enter it. This is the kind of subtle view-lifecycle/state bookkeeping the existing animation engine was already handling for us. These are documented unsuccessful attempts, not a claim that CSS/WAAPI is mathematically incapable of the effect. They also predate improvements since then; I am not presenting them as a newly verified bug in Angular 22's native APIs. My concern is losing supported orchestration and being required to rebuild it as application infrastructure, with recurring edge cases and a different call-site API. ### Proposed solution Please either: 1. Keep the legacy engine available and supported through v23 while advanced migration cases are resolved; or 2. Provide an officially supported compatibility package/adapter preserving the trigger API and its integration; or 3. Publish a complete, tested equivalent for the coordinated example above before removal, including nested controls, old/new view-context separation, reverse stagger, rapid step reversal, and retained forms whose visibility changes without destruction. A parity example should show the same old and new behavior, rather than a simpler single-element fade. If there is already a supported solution that preserves this setup without a large custom runner or per-caller rewrites, I would genuinely welcome being pointed to it. I would much rather adopt that than argue against progress. Please do not remove a working capability before applications with this orchestration pattern have a dependable migration path. A longer deprecation period or a maintained compatibility package would make a real difference. ### Alternatives considered - `animate.enter`/`animate.leave` plus CSS: valuable for basic effects, but our attempted replacement lost parent/child and view-lifetime coordination. A current, complete parity example is the missing piece for this case. - A custom WAAPI runner and structural wrappers: attempted, but introduced context-swap/lifecycle bugs and substantial application-owned machinery. - Pinning Angular 22: a temporary option, not a sustainable upgrade strategy. - Carrying the old package forward with dependency overrides or a private fork: this does not itself preserve removed renderer/compiler integration and transfers maintenance to application developers. Related: the completed [animation RFC](https://github.com/angular/angular/discussions/62212) and [#66359](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/66359), where a contributor also expected one-to-one migration examples. I recognize that #66359 was a resolved documentation discussion; I am linking it for context, not claiming it remains an open bug.

title: `[class]` and `[style]` bindings are dropped when a directive has an output named `class` or `style`
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? core ### Is this a regression? Yes. It works in 19.1.x and is broken from 19.2.0 onward. ### Description When a directive on an element declares an output whose public name is `class`, the template's `[class]` binding on that element never reaches the DOM. Static classes and `[class.foo]` bindings still work. The same happens with an output named `style` and `[style]`. Nothing is reported at compile time or at runtime. ```ts @Directive({selector: '[dir]'}) export class Dir { @Output('class') out = new EventEmitter(); } @Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [Dir], template: `
`, }) export class App { cls = signal('b'); } ``` Expected classes on the `div`: `b p s`, which is what you get without `dir`. Actual classes: `p s`. After `cls.set('b2')`, they are still `p s`. These forms are affected too: - `[style]` with an output named `style`. - Interpolated `class="s {{x}}"` and `style="width: {{w}}px"`. - Signal outputs, such as `output({alias: 'class'})`. - Host directives that expose an output as `class`, such as `outputs: ['out: class']`. `[className]`, `[class.foo]`, host bindings and `(class)` listeners still work. Cause: `setShadowStylingInputFlags` in `packages/core/src/render3/view/directives.ts` sets `TNodeFlags.hasClassInput`/`hasStyleInput` for outputs as well as inputs. The `[class]` value is then routed to directive inputs named `class`. None exist, so the value is dropped. This started with #60036, a refactor that moved the flag into helpers shared by inputs and outputs. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug No hosted reproduction. The snippet in the description is self-contained: paste it into any Angular 19.2+ app. The linked PR adds regression tests. ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true None. The binding is dropped silently. ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular: 19.2.0 and later, including angular/angular main at 8260542ce0. Reproduced with acceptance tests in packages/core/test/acceptance (AOT and JIT). ``` ### Anything else? A PR with a fix and regression tests follows: the flag is set only while collecting inputs.

title: Signal forms: right after a value change, a debounced async validator reports the old result instead of `pending`
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms, core

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

A field with `validateAsync({debounce})` or `validateHttp({debounce})` doesn't report `pending()` right after its value changes. Until Angular runs effects, the field keeps the async result for the previous value. Code that changes a value and then reads the form's state or calls `submit()` in the same task acts on that old result.

Without `debounce`, the same field reports `pending()` at once.

**Why it matters.**

- WebMCP's tool `execute` sets the value and submits in the same task. By reading the code, an AI agent that corrects an invalid value gets "Form submission failed" with the error for the old value.
- An app that sets a value and submits in one handler, for example from a keyboard shortcut, sees the same failure.
- The [async operations guide](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/6d32550fbbae49851a680b3dc1281d8b899352e7/adev/src/content/guide/forms/signals/async-operations.md?plain=1#L668) says that "validation always reflects the current value".

The cause is in `debounced()` in `@angular/core`, so any app that reads a `chain(debounced(...))` resource right after a write sees the same stale state. Templates rarely see it, because effects run before views refresh.

**Example.** A username field whose async check has already reported `taken` for the current value:

```ts
import {Component, resource, signal} from '@angular/core';
import {form, FormField, submit, validateAsync} from '@angular/forms/signals';

@Component({
  selector: 'username-form',
  imports: [FormField],
  template: `<input [formField]="f.username" />`,
})
export class UsernameForm {
  readonly f = form(signal({username: 'taken-name'}), (p) => {
    validateAsync(p.username, {
      params: ({value}) => value(),
      debounce: 300,
      factory: (username) =>
        resource({
          params: username,
          loader: ({params}) => fetch(`/api/username-available?u=${params}`).then((r) => r.json()),
        }),
      onSuccess: (available) => (available ? undefined : {kind: 'taken'}),
      onError: () => undefined,
    });
  });

  // Called from a keyboard shortcut, or the same thing happens through a WebMCP tool call.
  async useSuggestedName() {
    this.f.username().value.set('free-name');
    await submit(this.f, async () => {
      // Save the form.
    });
  }
}
```

**Current behavior,** right after `value.set('free-name')`:

```text
pending()   false
invalid()   true    (the 'taken' error for 'taken-name')
submit()    doesn't run the action
```

**Expected behavior (my assumption):**

```text
pending()   true
invalid()   false
submit()    runs the action, as it does for the same validator without debounce
```

This assumes that a debounced validator should behave like one without `debounce`, except for the delay before it runs. The `debounced()` guide supports that: it says that `status()` "tells you whether a new value is still pending" ([`debounced.md`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/6d32550fbbae49851a680b3dc1281d8b899352e7/adev/src/content/guide/signals/debounced.md?plain=1#L34)).

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

Failing specs in triage PR #71637, which changes no library code:

- Forms: [`validate_async_debounce_window.spec.ts`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-debounce-pending-window/packages/forms/signals/test/node/validate_async_debounce_window.spec.ts)
- Core: [`debounce_status_spec.ts`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-debounce-pending-window/packages/core/test/resource/debounce_status_spec.ts)

```bash
pnpm bazel test //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test --test_arg=--filter="validateAsync debounce window" --test_output=all
pnpm bazel test //packages/core/test/resource:resource --test_arg=--filter="debounced status before effects run" --test_output=all
```

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

There's no error. The specs fail with:

```text
validateAsync debounce window with debounce: a value change is pending at once and submit() isn't blocked
    state read synchronously after value.set():
        Expected $.pending = false to equal true.
        Expected $.invalid = true to equal false.
    submit() ran the action for the new VALID value: Expected false to be true.
debounced status before effects run reports loading as soon as the source changes
    state right after source.set(): Expected $.status = 'resolved' to equal 'loading'.
debounced status before effects run makes a chained resource report loading as soon as the source changes
    chained resource status right after source.set(): Expected 'resolved' to be 'loading'.
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```text
angular/angular main at 6d32550fbbae49851a680b3dc1281d8b899352e7 (2026-10-26), built from source
Test targets: //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test and //packages/core/test/resource:resource
OS: macOS (darwin arm64)
```

### Anything else?

**Affected areas:**

- `validateAsync()` and `validateHttp()` with `debounce`, when state is read or `submit()` is called in the same task as the write.
- WebMCP tool calls on signal forms with debounced async validators.
- Any app code that reads a `chain(debounced(...))` resource right after the source changes.
- Not affected: async validators without `debounce`, and templates, which render after effects run.

**Related work.** #70884 is about the same `chain(debounced(...))` wrapper in `validateAsync()`. #71414 tries to fix #70884 in forms, but it's stuck: the [review on Oct 25](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/71414#pullrequestreview-5640773489) requested changes, and said that the gap isn't specific to signal forms and that keeping the previous settled value while debouncing causes stale results. #71414 also doesn't fix this window. The fix I recommend follows that review: it changes `debounced()` in core.

**Fix options and tradeoffs.** The PR has code for each option.

| Option | What changes | Tradeoffs |
|--------|--------------|-----------|
| A (recommended): `debounced()` reports `loading` as soon as its source changes | The `linkedSignal` in `debounced()` returns `loading` with the previous value when the source changes, and the effect checks whether a wait is active | Fixes every `chain(debounced(...))` user. With it applied, the specs and the core resource and signal forms suites pass. Synchronous `wait` functions show `loading` until effects flush. Factories with the #70884 pattern throw as soon as the value changes, instead of after effects run |
| B: `validateAsync()` treats a params mismatch as pending | Throw the `LOADING` marker while the debounced value differs from the params | Forms only. Needs a new private export from core |
| C: WebMCP waits for the app to be stable before submitting | One `await` in WebMCP's `execute` | Mitigation only. Other code that reads `pending()` right after a write still sees the old result |

**Where to look in the code:**

- [`validateAsync()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/6d32550fbbae49851a680b3dc1281d8b899352e7/packages/forms/signals/src/api/rules/validation/validate_async.ts#L137-L141) wraps the params in `ɵchain(debounced(...))`.
- [`debounced()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/6d32550fbbae49851a680b3dc1281d8b899352e7/packages/core/src/resource/debounce.ts#L80-L85) keeps its previous state when the source changes, and only its effect moves it to `loading`.
- The [triage note](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-debounce-pending-window/packages/forms/signals/triage/debounce-pending-window.md) has the root cause, the measurements, and the full code for each option.

title: Signal forms: compatForm() FormControl errors are missing from errorSummary()
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? forms ### Is this a regression? No ### Description **In short.** A form built with `compatForm()` can be invalid because of a `FormControl` validator, while its `errorSummary()` is empty. The errors also have no `fieldTree`, although their type says they do. **Why it matters.** `errorSummary()` is how an app lists every error at once, for example next to the submit button. With compat fields, `submit()` is blocked but the list is empty, so the user can't tell what to fix. Code that follows an error to its field, such as `error.fieldTree().focusBoundControl()`, throws on a compat error. **Failure mode in user code.** ```ts @Component({ imports: [FormField], template: ` @if (showErrors()) {
    @for (error of f().errorSummary(); track error) {
  • {{ error.kind }}
    • }
} `, }) export class Signup { readonly showErrors = signal(false); readonly model = signal({ name: new FormControl('', {nonNullable: true, validators: Validators.required}), }); readonly f = compatForm(this.model); save() { submit(this.f, { action: async () => saveSignup(this.model().name.value), onInvalid: () => this.showErrors.set(true), }); } } ``` Starting state: the `FormControl` value is `''`. `f.name().errors()` holds one `required` error, and `f().invalid()` is `true`. Current behavior: ```text 1. User clicks Save the action doesn't run; onInvalid shows the list f().errorSummary() → [] the list is empty ``` Expected behavior: ```text 1. User clicks Save the action doesn't run; onInvalid shows the list f().errorSummary() → [{kind: 'required', fieldTree: f.name}] the list shows "required" ``` **Assumptions: expected vs current.** | Expected | Current | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `errorSummary()` holds "the errors of the field and its descendants", as its doc comment says. | A compat field's `errorSummary` is a shared empty signal. | | `invalid()` and `errorSummary()` agree: an invalid form has at least one error in its summary. | `f().invalid()` is `true` while `f().errorSummary()` is `[]`. | | Every error typed `ValidationError.WithFieldTree` has a `fieldTree` that points at its field, as plain errors do. | `CompatValidationError` declares `fieldTree` but never sets it. | **Affected areas.** - `CompatValidationState` in `packages/forms/signals/compat/src/compat_validation_state.ts`: `errorSummary` and `errors`. - `CompatValidationError` in `packages/forms/signals/src/compat/validation_errors.ts`. - `errorSummary()` on any form with compat fields, including its DOM-order sort. - Consumers that read `error.fieldTree` on compat errors. **Tradeoffs of the fix.** - The summary fix needs `fieldTree` first. On the client, the root summary sorts errors by DOM position through `error.fieldTree()`, so adding compat errors without it would throw a `TypeError` once the summary has two or more errors. - Setting `fieldTree` in `CompatValidationState` with the existing `addDefaultField()` helper keeps the public `CompatValidationError` class unchanged. Adding a constructor parameter instead changes public API. - Nested errors of a `FormGroup` or `FormArray` value all point at the compat field, because nested controls have no `FieldTree` of their own. - A compat field bound with `[formControl]` instead of `[formField]` has no bound element, so its errors sort to the end of the summary. **Related.** #71633, where compat fields drop parse errors, changes the same class. **Details.** - Triage PR with the recommended fix, design decisions, and questions: #71630 - [Triage notes](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/df91c393eb29637719c4f8bcd5608fbaf23d6092/packages/forms/signals/triage/compat-error-summary.md): observed output, root cause, and the sort hazard. - [`CompatValidationState.errorSummary`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/compat/src/compat_validation_state.ts#L55-L56), [`FieldValidationState.errorSummary`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/field/validation.ts#L275-L288), [`CompatValidationError`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/compat/validation_errors.ts#L19-L31), [`addDefaultField()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/field/validation.ts#L394-L414), [DOM-order sort](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/field/validation.ts#L416-L444). ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug [`compat_error_summary.spec.ts`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/df91c393eb29637719c4f8bcd5608fbaf23d6092/packages/forms/signals/test/node/compat/compat_error_summary.spec.ts) in the triage PR. Each spec asserts the expected behavior, so 2 of them fail today: ```bash pnpm bazel test //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test --test_output=all ``` ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```text No error is thrown. The repro specs report: root errorSummary(): Expected $.length = 0 to equal 1. fieldTree of the compat field error: Expected undefined to be Function. ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```text angular/angular main at ce30bb0889 (2026-10-16), Bazel target //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test. The affected source files are unchanged on main at 3e173fc844 (2026-10-24). ``` ### Anything else? I searched for an existing issue or PR and found none.

title: Signal forms: compatForm() fields ignore parse errors, so submit() sends the last valid value
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? forms ### Is this a regression? No ### Description **In short.** When a `compatForm()` field is bound with `[formField]` to a control that can't parse what the user typed, the field ignores the parse error. For example, `` with `30e` in it. The field stays valid, no error shows, and `submit()` runs with the last value that parsed. The same template on a plain `form()` field blocks the submit. **Why it matters.** `compatForm()` is the documented way to migrate a reactive form to signal forms step by step, and the [migration guide](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/adev/src/content/guide/forms/signals/migration.md?plain=1#L46-L76) binds compat fields with `[formField]`. The failure is silent: the user sees one value, and the app saves another. **Failure mode in user code.** ```ts @Component({ imports: [FormField], template: ` @if (f.age().invalid()) {

Enter a valid age.

} `, }) export class Profile { readonly model = signal({age: new FormControl(30, {nonNullable: true})}); readonly f = compatForm(this.model); save() { submit(this.f, async () => { await saveProfile({age: this.model().age.value}); }); } } ``` Starting state: the `FormControl` value is `30`, the input shows `30`, `f.age().errors()` is `[]`, and `f.age().invalid()` is `false`. Current behavior: ```text 1. User types "30e" input shows "30e"; FormControl value stays 30 f.age().errors() → [] f.age().invalid() → false no error message 2. User clicks Save the action runs and saves {age: 30} ``` Expected behavior: ```text 1. User types "30e" input shows "30e"; FormControl value stays 30 f.age().errors() → [{kind: 'parse', ...}] f.age().invalid() → true "Enter a valid age." shows 2. User clicks Save the action doesn't run ``` **Assumptions: expected vs current.** | Expected | Current | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | A compat field reports its controls' parse errors like a plain field does: in `errors()`, in `invalid()`, and at the submit gate. | `CompatValidationState.parseErrors` is hardcoded to `[]`. | | The `FormControl`'s own state still shows through ("Reactive state is proxied automatically" in the guide). Parse errors add to it. | `errors`, `valid`, `invalid`, and `syncValid` come only from the `FormControl`. | | The control that reported the parse error can show it. | `FormField.errors()` filters the field's `errors()`, so the binding's own errors are empty too. | **Affected areas.** - `CompatValidationState` in `packages/forms/signals/compat/src/compat_validation_state.ts`: `parseErrors`, `errors`, `syncValid`, `valid`, and `invalid`. - Every source of parse errors, on a compat field: - Native inputs with bad input, such as number, date, and time. - Legacy `NG_VALIDATORS` on a CVA, which are shimmed into parse errors. - Custom controls that report `parseErrors`. - `submit()` on a compat root, and on a plain root with compat children. - The migration guide's statements that reactive state is proxied and that `errors()` returns `CompatValidationError`. **Tradeoffs of the fix.** - After the fix, `f.age().invalid()` is `true` while the `FormControl` and its parent `FormGroup` still report valid. Parse errors live in the signal-forms layer, so reactive code that checks `formGroup.valid` disagrees with `submit()`. - Writing parse errors into the `FormControl` with `setErrors()` would avoid that split, but the next `updateValueAndValidity()` wipes them, and it fights reactive forms' ownership of the control. - `errors()` would mix `CompatValidationError` with parse errors, which have no `control` or `context`. The public type doesn't change, and the guide's `errorMessage()` helper on `main` already falls back to `error.message ?? error.kind`. - Only documenting the limitation is cheapest, but it leaves a silent submit with the wrong value. For comparison, the two APIs that compat bridges both catch this case. Reactive forms' `NumberValueAccessor` writes `null` for bad input, so `Validators.required` fails. Plain signal forms block the submit. **Related bug, same file.** A compat field's `errorSummary` is always empty, so the root's `errorSummary()` omits every `FormControl` error: #71634. **Details.** - Triage PR with the recommended fix, design decisions, and questions: #71628 - [Triage notes](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/9a747b865e1f4725fde103a947f5308ce8d1b365/packages/forms/signals/triage/compat-parse-errors.md): observed output, root cause, and history. - [`CompatValidationState`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/compat/src/compat_validation_state.ts#L26-L75), [`FieldValidationState.parseErrors` and `errors`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/field/validation.ts#L258-L273), [`FormField.errors`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/directive/form_field.ts#L196-L202), [`submit()` gate](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/api/structure.ts#L528-L540), [`errorMessage()` in the guide on `main`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3e173fc844c440775d3f110da8505442e227dee5/adev/src/content/guide/forms/signals/migration.md?plain=1#L79-L91). ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug [`compat_parse_errors.spec.ts`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/9a747b865e1f4725fde103a947f5308ce8d1b365/packages/forms/signals/test/web/compat_parse_errors.spec.ts) in the triage PR. The repro spec asserts the expected behavior and fails today. The web test runner ignores `--filter`, so this runs the whole Chromium suite: ```bash pnpm bazel test //packages/forms/signals/test/web:test_chromium --test_output=all ``` ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```text No error is thrown. The repro spec reports: Expected $.fieldErrors.length = 0 to equal 1. Expected $.fieldInvalid = false to equal true. Expected $.rootInvalid = false to equal true. Unexpected $.actionSaw[0] = 5 in array. ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```text angular/angular main at ce30bb0889 (2026-10-16), Bazel target //packages/forms/signals/test/web:test_chromium. The affected source files are unchanged on main at 3e173fc844 (2026-10-24). Native inputs have produced parse errors since v22.0.0-next.0. ``` ### Anything else?
