title: Signal forms: a parse error on one control shows up on every other control bound to the same field
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms

### Is this a regression?

Yes

### Description

**In short.** When one field is bound to several controls and one of them has a parse error, CVA and
native hosts receive that parse error in their `errors` too. So does `NgControl.errors`. Each
control should receive only the parse errors it produced, as custom controls do today.

**Why it matters.** Binding one field to two controls is a common pattern, for example a slider
next to a number input. Typing `5e` into the number input then makes the slider show the number
input's parse error as its own. Parse errors became common in v22: native inputs produce them, and so do
legacy CVA validators.

**Failure mode in user code.**

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-slider',
  template: `
    <input type="range" min="0" max="100" />
    @for (error of errors(); track error) {
      <small>{{ error.message ?? error.kind }}</small>
    }
  `,
  providers: [{provide: NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR, useExisting: Slider, multi: true}],
})
export class Slider implements ControlValueAccessor {
  readonly errors = input<readonly ValidationError[]>([]);
  // writeValue, registerOnChange, and registerOnTouched omitted.
}

@Component({
  imports: [FormField, Slider],
  template: `
    <app-slider [formField]="f.volume" />
    <input type="number" [formField]="f.volume" />
  `,
})
export class Mixer {
  readonly f = form(signal({volume: 50}));
}
```

Starting state: `f.volume().value()` is `50`, both controls show `50`, and neither has errors.

Current behavior:

```text
1. User types "5e" into the number input
   number input  FormField.errors() → [{kind: 'parse'}]
   slider        errors input       → [{kind: 'parse'}]   the slider shows the error
   both          invalid input      → true
```

Expected behavior:

```text
1. User types "5e" into the number input
   number input  FormField.errors() → [{kind: 'parse'}]
   slider        errors input       → []                  the slider shows nothing
   both          invalid input      → true
```

**History.** The filter existed for every host in v21.2.0-next.1
([`ebae211add`](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/ebae211add37700858adeb8fc5d87bf503a59721)).
The refactor in v21.2.0-next.2
([`a67e00741c`](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/a67e00741c23d7ae4c93970c026bd7f9d41521ee))
kept it only for custom controls. The leak became visible in v22.0.0-next.0, when native inputs
started producing parse errors
([`22afbb2f36`](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/22afbb2f36be89c2ae575df343571a918dec5985)).

**Assumptions: expected vs current.**

| Expected                                                                                                                         | Current                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Each control receives only the parse errors of its own binding. `ebae211add` states this, and custom controls still work this way. | CVA and native hosts receive the field's unfiltered `errors()`.           |
| `inject(NgControl).errors` reflects the binding it was injected for.                                                              | It converts the field's unfiltered `errors()`.                             |
| `invalid` is field-level, so every control on the field receives `true`.                                                          | Same. This doesn't change.                                                 |

**Affected areas.**

- `readFieldStateBindingValue()` in `packages/forms/signals/src/directive/bindings.ts`, and its
  callers in `control_cva.ts`, `control_native.ts`, and `control_custom.ts`.
- `InteropNgControl.errors` in `packages/forms/signals/src/controls/interop_ng_control.ts`, and how
  `FormField` creates it.
- Consumers: directives with an `errors` input on native elements, CVA components with an `errors`
  input, and components that read `NgControl.errors`.
- Not affected: `FormField.errors()`, which is already filtered, and custom controls.

**Tradeoffs of the fix.**

- Routing every host through one helper that reads `FormField.errors` changes an internal
  function's signature and its three callers. Copying the special case into two more files is a
  smaller diff, but three copies are how the behavior drifted.
- Filtering `NgControl.errors` means passing the binding's errors into `InteropNgControl`, which is
  an internal constructor change. It can land with the fix or later.
- A control can receive `invalid: true` with empty `errors`. Custom controls already get that
  today, so UI that shows invalid styling without a message stays as it is.

**Details.**

- Triage PR with the recommended fix, design decisions, and questions: #71629
- [Triage notes](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/7e43a71da8e7763a078ac5c4dbbe0d847ef52efa/packages/forms/signals/triage/errors-per-control.md):
  observed output, history, and the `NgControl` path.
- [Custom host, filtered](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/directive/control_custom.ts#L41-L45),
  [CVA host](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/directive/control_cva.ts#L99-L101),
  [native host](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/directive/control_native.ts#L113-L114),
  [`readFieldStateBindingValue()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/directive/bindings.ts#L58-L64),
  [`InteropNgControl.errors`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/controls/interop_ng_control.ts#L93-L95).

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

[`form_field_errors_per_binding.spec.ts`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/7e43a71da8e7763a078ac5c4dbbe0d847ef52efa/packages/forms/signals/test/web/form_field_errors_per_binding.spec.ts)
in the triage PR. Both specs assert the expected behavior and fail today. The web test runner
ignores `--filter`, so this runs the whole Chromium suite:

```bash
pnpm bazel test //packages/forms/signals/test/web:test_chromium --test_output=all
```

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```text
No error is thrown. The repro specs report:

Unexpected $[1].errorsInput[0] = 'parse from native (bad input)' in array.
Unexpected $[2].errorsInput[0] = 'parse from native (bad input)' in array.
Unexpected $[1].errors[0] = 'parse' in array.
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```text
angular/angular main at ce30bb0889 (2026-10-16), Bazel target
//packages/forms/signals/test/web:test_chromium. The affected source files are unchanged on main at
3e173fc844 (2026-10-24). First affected prerelease: v21.2.0-next.2.
```

### Anything else?

I searched for an existing issue or PR and found none.

title: Signal forms: a custom debouncer's abort listener runs late, inside a computation
body: ### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? forms ### Is this a regression? No ### Description **In short.** Signal forms pass an `AbortSignal` to a custom debouncer. It should fire when the user moves on before the debounce finishes. Today it fires at the wrong time, and its listeners run inside a `linkedSignal` computation. An abort listener that touches a signal breaks: - Writing a signal throws NG0600, so the write is lost. - Reading a signal can make the form drop the value the user typed. - A debounce that already finished is aborted on the next blur, so the listener runs anyway. **Why it matters.** The obvious use of a custom debouncer is a "searching" indicator, and its abort listener writes a signal. In such an app, every blur after a finished debounce logs NG0600, and a programmatic model write can leave the indicator stuck on. The built-in debouncers, `debounce(path, ms)` and `debounce(path, 'blur')`, aren't affected. **Failure mode in user code.** ```ts @Component({ imports: [FormField], template: ` @if (searching()) { Searching… } `, }) export class Search { readonly searching = signal(false); readonly model = signal({query: ''}); readonly f = form(this.model, (p) => { debounce(p.query, (_ctx, abortSignal) => { this.searching.set(true); return new Promise((resolve) => { const timer = setTimeout(() => { this.searching.set(false); resolve(); }, 300); abortSignal.addEventListener('abort', () => { clearTimeout(timer); this.searching.set(false); resolve(); }); }); }); }); } ``` Starting state: `model().query` is `''`, `searching()` is `false`, and no debounce is pending. Current behavior: ```text 1. User types "ng" searching() → true, model().query → '' (debounce pending) 2. 300 ms pass searching() → false, model().query → 'ng' (debounce finished) 3. User tabs out (blur) the finished debounce is aborted; the listener's searching.set(false) throws NG0600: Writing to signals is not allowed in a `computed`. The error is reported as uncaught. ``` Expected behavior: ```text 1. User types "ng" searching() → true, model().query → '' (debounce pending) 2. 300 ms pass searching() → false, model().query → 'ng' (debounce finished) 3. User tabs out (blur) nothing to abort; no error ``` Two more failure modes, each covered by a repro spec: - **Stuck indicator.** Type "ng", then set `model` in code, for example in an Escape key handler, and blur before 300 ms pass. The listener clears the timer, then throws on `searching.set(false)` before `resolve()`. `searching()` stays `true`. - **Lost value.** If an abort listener reads a signal while it runs inside the computation, that signal becomes a dependency of the internal `pendingSync`. When it changes, the next read aborts the *live* debounce. The input shows what the user typed, but the model keeps the old value after blur. **Assumptions: expected vs current.** | Expected (from the docs and the code's own comments) | Current | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | The abort fires when the value changes before the debounce resolves (guide, `pendingSync` doc comment). | A direct model write only marks `pendingSync` dirty. The abort fires at the next keystroke, touch, or reset. | | A debounce that finished is never aborted. | The finished controller stays in `pendingSync` and is aborted at the next read. | | Abort listeners run like any event listener, outside a reactive context, so they can read and write signals. | They run inside the `linkedSignal` computation, with dependency tracking on. | **Affected areas.** - `FieldNode` in `packages/forms/signals/src/field/node.ts`: `pendingSync`, `debounceSync()`, `flushSync()`, and `_reset()`. - Custom debouncers passed to `debounce(path, fn)` whose abort listeners read or write signals. - The guide's description of the abort timing in `async-operations.md`. - Tests: an NG0600 caught by `dispatchEvent` surfaces as an uncaught error and can fail an unrelated spec that runs later. **Tradeoffs of the fix.** - The recommended fix keeps today's timing for direct model writes and rewords the guide. An immediate abort needs an `effect` per debounced field, and effects run asynchronously anyway. - Replacing the `linkedSignal` with a plain field removes one `linkedSignal` from every field, debounced or not. It changes one flow: touching after a direct write now reaches `sync()`. That's a no-op for plain fields, but on a `compatForm()` field it calls `FormControl.setValue()` and emits `valueChanges` again, unless the fix also skips that `sync()`. - Keeping the `linkedSignal` gives a smaller diff, but user listeners still run during a computation. **Details.** - Triage PR with the recommended fix, design decisions, and questions: #71627 - [Triage notes](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/c1bcad6ef84ba8e5a6ed7d269df186ba4901194a/packages/forms/signals/triage/debounce-abort-signal.md): observed output, root cause, and the measured fix options. - [`pendingSync`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/field/node.ts#L140-L152), [`flushSync()` and `debounceSync()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/field/node.ts#L413-L447), [`linkedSignal` computation](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/core/primitives/signals/src/linked_signal.ts#L156-L178), [guide text](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/adev/src/content/guide/forms/signals/async-operations.md?plain=1#L472), [built-in debouncers](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/ce30bb0889018ad9da521d6ad729294e1aa3b5ff/packages/forms/signals/src/api/rules/debounce.ts#L64-L94). ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug [`debounce_abort.spec.ts`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/c1bcad6ef84ba8e5a6ed7d269df186ba4901194a/packages/forms/signals/test/node/debounce_abort.spec.ts) in the triage PR. Each spec asserts the expected behavior, so 6 of them fail today: ```bash pnpm bazel test //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test --test_output=all ``` ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```text Error: NG0600: Writing to signals is not allowed in a `computed`. Signal: 'debouncing'. ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```text angular/angular main at ce30bb0889 (2026-10-16), Bazel target //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test. The affected source files are unchanged on main at 3e173fc844 (2026-10-24). ``` ### Anything else? I searched for an existing issue or PR and found none.

title: Signal forms: `required()`, `min()`, and other built-in rules create an injector for every field
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

In a signal form, each field can get its own injector, so that a managed metadata key, like the one `validateAsync()` uses, can create resources in the field's injection context. But today a field creates an injector as soon as it has **any** metadata rule. Most built-in rules add metadata, so `required()`, `min()`, `max()`, `minLength()`, `maxLength()`, `minDate()`, `maxDate()`, `pattern()`, `validateStandardSchema()`, and `debounce()` all give each field an injector that nothing uses.

Removing a field also creates an injector if it didn't have one, just so the cleanup can destroy it.

**Why it matters.** The cost grows with the number of fields. Large tables, line-item lists, and dynamic arrays usually put `required()` or `min()` on every row. Each injector took about 1.1 to 1.5 µs to create in my measurement, and it also holds memory, which I didn't measure. This doesn't break anything, but it's work that the feature doesn't need.

**Example.** An order form with 1,000 line items:

```ts
import {Component, signal} from '@angular/core';
import {applyEach, form, FormField, min, required} from '@angular/forms/signals';

@Component({
  selector: 'order-lines',
  imports: [FormField],
  template: `
    @for (line of f; track $index) {
      <input [formField]="line.sku" />
      <input type="number" [formField]="line.qty" />
    }
  `,
})
export class OrderLines {
  readonly lines = signal(Array.from({length: 1000}, () => ({sku: '', qty: 1})));
  readonly f = form(this.lines, (p) => {
    applyEach(p, (line) => {
      required(line.sku);
      min(line.qty, 1);
    });
  });
}
```

**Current behavior:**

```text
read every line's fields, as the template does   → 2,000 injectors (one per sku field, one per qty field)
lines.set([])                                    → 1,000 more injectors (one per line, created only to be destroyed)
```

**Expected behavior (my assumption):**

```text
read every line's fields, as the template does   → 0 injectors (neither rule needs an injection context)
lines.set([])                                    → 0 injectors
```

This assumes that only managed metadata keys need a field injector. That's what the [field metadata guide](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3e173fc844c440775d3f110da8505442e227dee5/adev/src/content/guide/forms/signals/field-metadata.md?plain=1#L314) documents: a managed key's `create` runs in the field's injection context. Plain metadata keys only compute a value. Fields with `validateAsync()` or `validateHttp()` would still get an injector.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

Failing specs: [`field_injector_allocation.spec.ts`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-injector-allocation/packages/forms/signals/test/node/field_injector_allocation.spec.ts) in triage PR #71626. The PR changes no library code.

```bash
pnpm bazel test //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test --test_arg=--filter="field injector allocation" --test_output=all
```

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

There's no error. The specs count `Injector.create` calls for 50 array items with one rule each. They fail with:

```text
creates injectors only for fields with managed metadata keys (50 items per rule)
    Expected $.required = 50 to equal 0.
    Expected $.min = 50 to equal 0.
    Expected $.debounce = 50 to equal 0.
creates no injectors to destroy 50 removed fields that never had one
    Injector.create calls while the cleanup sweep destroys the removed items: Expected 50 to be 0.
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```text
angular/angular main at 3e173fc844c440775d3f110da8505442e227dee5 (2026-10-24), built from source
Test target: //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test
OS: macOS (darwin arm64)
```

### Anything else?

**Affected areas:**

- Fields with any of these rules: `required()`, `min()`, `max()`, `minLength()`, `maxLength()`, `minDate()`, `maxDate()`, `pattern()`, `validateStandardSchema()`, and `debounce()`.
- Fields with custom `metadata()` rules that use plain keys from `createMetadataKey()`.
- Removing any field that never had an injector, including fields with no rules.
- Combined with #70627, where the cleanup sweep materializes every reachable field, every field with one of these rules gets an injector after the first sweep, even if nothing reads it. I found this by reading the code, and no spec checks it.
- Not affected: fields with no rules, or with `validate()` only. Fields with `validateAsync()` or `validateHttp()` need their injector and keep it.

**Fix options and tradeoffs.** The PR has code for each option.

| Option | What changes | Tradeoffs |
|--------|--------------|-----------|
| A (recommended): create the injector only for managed keys | Move `runInInjectionContext()` inside the check for `key.create`, and don't create an injector during cleanup | Small change, same documented contract. A field with several managed keys enters the injection context once per key |
| B: cache a "has managed keys" flag on the schema logic | Return early before touching the injector | Also skips a loop per field, but the cached flag could go stale, because metadata keys are added lazily |
| C: replace field injectors with a lightweight scope | Shared with the host teardown issue (#71622) | Cheapest per field, but a much larger change |

**Where to look in the code:**

- [`runMetadataCreateLifecycle()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3e173fc844c440775d3f110da8505442e227dee5/packages/forms/signals/src/field/metadata.ts#L34-L58) enters the field's injection context before it checks whether any key needs it.
- [`FieldNodeStructure.destroy()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3e173fc844c440775d3f110da8505442e227dee5/packages/forms/signals/src/field/structure.ts#L216-L218) reads the lazy `injector` getter, which creates an injector if there wasn't one.
- The [triage note](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-injector-allocation/packages/forms/signals/triage/injector-allocation.md) has the counts for each rule, the root cause, and the full code for each option.

title: Signal forms: destroying a form's component doesn't destroy its fields, so async validation keeps running
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

When the component that owns a signal form is destroyed, the form's fields aren't. Anything a field sets up for its own lifetime keeps going:

- An async validation request that's in flight isn't cancelled.
- Cleanup that a managed metadata key registers with `DestroyRef` never runs.
- If the form was created with an environment injector, its validators keep reacting to model changes and start new requests after the injector is destroyed.

Fields that are removed from the model, such as deleted array items, are cleaned up correctly. Only the teardown of the whole form is missing.

**Why it matters.** Users who leave a page with a pending username check, address lookup, or similar validator keep that request running. Libraries that build on `createManagedMetadataKey()` can't rely on `DestroyRef` for cleanup, even though the [field metadata guide](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3e173fc844c440775d3f110da8505442e227dee5/adev/src/content/guide/forms/signals/field-metadata.md?plain=1#L314) says that cleanup is tied to the field's lifecycle.

**Example.** A form checks whether a username is available:

```ts
import {Component, resource, signal} from '@angular/core';
import {form, FormField, validateAsync} from '@angular/forms/signals';

@Component({
  selector: 'signup-form',
  imports: [FormField],
  template: `<input [formField]="f.username" />`,
})
export class SignupForm {
  readonly f = form(signal({username: ''}), (p) => {
    validateAsync(p.username, {
      params: ({value}) => value(),
      factory: (username) =>
        resource({
          params: username,
          loader: ({params, abortSignal}) =>
            fetch(`/api/username-available?u=${params}`, {signal: abortSignal}).then((r) => r.json()),
        }),
      onSuccess: (available) => (available ? undefined : {kind: 'taken'}),
      onError: () => undefined,
    });
  });
}
```

The user types `alice`, and the form starts `GET /api/username-available?u=alice`. Before it returns, the user navigates away, and Angular destroys `SignupForm`.

**Current behavior:**

```text
SignupForm destroyed
  username field: still alive
  GET /api/username-available?u=alice: still running (abortSignal.aborted === false)
```

**Expected behavior (my assumption):**

```text
SignupForm destroyed
  username field: destroyed
  GET /api/username-available?u=alice: cancelled (abortSignal.aborted === true)
```

This assumes that a form's fields live as long as the injector the form was created with: the component's injector by default, or the `injector` option. Neither the API docs nor the guide says when a whole form's fields are destroyed, so this needs a maintainer decision. I've listed the open questions in the triage PR.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

Failing specs: [`form_host_teardown.spec.ts`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-host-teardown/packages/forms/signals/test/node/form_host_teardown.spec.ts) in triage PR #71625. The PR changes no library code.

```bash
pnpm bazel test //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test --test_arg=--filter="form host teardown" --test_output=all
```

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

There's no error. The specs fail with:

```text
runs root-field DestroyRef callbacks when the form injector is destroyed
    root-field DestroyRef callbacks after env.destroy(): Expected spy destroyed to have been called once. It was called 0 times.
runs live child-field DestroyRef callbacks when the form injector is destroyed
    live child-field DestroyRef callbacks after env.destroy(): Expected spy destroyed to have been called once. It was called 0 times.
aborts an in-flight validateAsync load when the form injector is destroyed
    loader AbortSignal.aborted after env.destroy(): Expected false to be true.
aborts an in-flight validateAsync load when the host component is destroyed
    loader AbortSignal.aborted after fixture.destroy(): Expected false to be true.
starts no validation loads after the form injector is destroyed
    loads started, including any after env.destroy(): Expected 2 to be 1.
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```text
angular/angular main at 3e173fc844c440775d3f110da8505442e227dee5 (2026-10-24), built from source
Test target: //packages/forms/signals/test/node:test
OS: macOS (darwin arm64)
```

### Anything else?

**Affected areas:**

- `validateAsync()`, `validateHttp()`, and `validateStandardSchema()` with async schemas: in-flight loads aren't aborted when the host is destroyed.
- Custom managed metadata keys (`createManagedMetadataKey()`): `DestroyRef` callbacks, `effect()`s, and `resource()`s that `create` sets up aren't cleaned up.
- Forms created with an environment injector, for example through the `injector` option: validation effects keep running, so new loads start after the injector is destroyed.
- `compatForm()` fields: they use a separate structure class that would need the same fix.
- Not affected: fields removed from the model. The form's cleanup sweep destroys them, and the triage PR has a passing spec that shows it.

**Fix options and tradeoffs.** The PR has code for each option.

| Option | What changes | Tradeoffs |
|--------|--------------|-----------|
| A (recommended): the form destroys all of its fields when its injector is destroyed | One `DestroyRef` hook per form, plus registering the root field | About 15 lines. Defines the lifetime contract above. Doesn't define what happens if code reads a new field after teardown |
| B: each field's injector registers with the form's injector | A hook per field instead of per form | No bookkeeping, but more hooks on the host, and removing hooks during teardown needs care |
| C: replace the per-field injectors with a lightweight scope | A new small `Injector` type for fields | Also removes the per-field injector cost in #71623. Much larger, and it touches dependency injection behavior |

**Where to look in the code:**

- [`FieldNodeStructure.injector`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3e173fc844c440775d3f110da8505442e227dee5/packages/forms/signals/src/field/structure.ts#L96-L102) creates each field's injector as a child of the form's injector. A child `R3Injector` isn't destroyed with its parent.
- [`FormFieldManager.createFieldManagementEffect()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3e173fc844c440775d3f110da8505442e227dee5/packages/forms/signals/src/field/manager.ts#L56-L71) is the only code that destroys fields, and only removed ones.
- The [triage note](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-host-teardown/packages/forms/signals/triage/host-teardown.md) has the full root cause, the behavior for each host type, and the spec output.

title: Signal forms: every app that uses `form()` ships `AbstractControl` and `Validators` from reactive forms
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

`form()` includes a safety check: if a rule reads another field with `valueOf()` and that field's value is a reactive forms control, it throws `NG1907` and suggests `compatForm()`. The check uses `instanceof AbstractControl`. That reference alone keeps `AbstractControl` in the production bundle, and `AbstractControl` brings `Validators`, the control event classes, and parts of RxJS with it. This happens in every app that calls `form()`, including apps that never import reactive forms.

**Why it matters.** Apps that use only signal forms pay for reactive forms code they never run. A minimal app pays about 4.7 KB gzipped (10.7%) for code it never runs. An app that binds fields with `[formField]` pays about 1.9 KB (3.3%).

**Example.** A minimal app that uses only signal forms:

```ts
import {Component, provideZonelessChangeDetection, signal} from '@angular/core';
import {form, required} from '@angular/forms/signals';
import {bootstrapApplication} from '@angular/platform-browser';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  template: `{{ f.name().value() }} {{ f.name().valid() }}`,
})
class App {
  readonly f = form(signal({name: ''}), (p) => {
    required(p.name);
  });
}

bootstrapApplication(App, {providers: [provideZonelessChangeDetection()]});
```

**Current behavior** (production build, gzipped `main.js`):

```text
44,490 B
includes AbstractControl, Validators, the control event classes, RxJS forkJoin and from
```

**Expected behavior (my assumption):**

```text
39,742 B
without AbstractControl, Validators, the control event classes, or RxJS forkJoin and from
```

The expected size is what I measured with the check limited to development builds. This assumes that the `NG1907` check is a development aid that doesn't need to run in production, which is how many Angular diagnostics work. If the team wants it in production, a check that doesn't reference the class gives the same size. I've listed this decision in the triage PR.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

Measurement apps: [`forms_signals_model`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-abstract-control-bundle/packages/core/test/bundling/forms_signals_model/main.ts) and [`forms_signals_field`](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-abstract-control-bundle/packages/core/test/bundling/forms_signals_field/main.ts), in triage PR #71624. The PR changes no library code.

```bash
pnpm bazel build //packages/core/test/bundling/forms_signals_model:bundles //packages/core/test/bundling/forms_signals_field:bundles
```

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

There's no error. These are the production bundle sizes in bytes:

```text
App            Today (raw / gzip / brotli)    Check in dev mode only (raw / gzip / brotli)    Saved (gzip)
model only     141,563 / 44,490 / 39,869      124,217 / 39,742 / 35,722                       4,748 B (10.7%)
[formField]    182,983 / 56,835 / 50,450      173,946 / 54,939 / 48,812                       1,896 B (3.3%)
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```text
angular/angular main at 3e173fc844c440775d3f110da8505442e227dee5 (2026-10-24), built from source
Build: optimize_angular_app (production Angular CLI build), default settings
OS: macOS (darwin arm64)
```

### Anything else?

**Affected areas:**

- Every app that calls `form()`, whether or not any rule calls `valueOf()`.
- Apps that use `[formField]` gain less from a fix: they still ship `Validators`, `NgControl`, and a few other reactive forms classes through the `ControlValueAccessor` interop. That's a separate, larger cleanup.
- Apps that use `compatForm()` already depend on reactive forms, so they gain nothing.
- With the recommended fix, the `NG1907` error throws only in development. In production, a rule that reads a `FormControl` through `valueOf()` would get the control back instead of an error.

**Fix options and tradeoffs.** The PR has code for each option.

| Option | What changes | Tradeoffs |
|--------|--------------|-----------|
| A (recommended): check only in development | `if (ngDevMode && result instanceof AbstractControl)` | One line, measured. Development keeps the error, production doesn't |
| B: check with a private helper from `@angular/forms` | A symbol on `AbstractControl` and a private `ɵisAbstractControl()` export | Keeps the production error. Adds a cross-package private API. Not measured |
| C: remove the check | Delete it | Smallest change, but it loses the diagnostic everywhere |

**Where to look in the code:**

- [`FieldNodeContext.valueOf`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3e173fc844c440775d3f110da8505442e227dee5/packages/forms/signals/src/field/context.ts#L168-L179) holds the check.
- The [triage note](https://github.com/Flarette/angular/blob/triage/forms-abstract-control-bundle/packages/forms/signals/triage/abstract-control-bundle.md) has the full measurements, the list of names that ship only because of the check, and the full code for each option.

title: SVG `<use>` `href` bindings bypass sanitization allowing XSS
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

core / compiler

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description


`SECURITY_SCHEMA` registers one attribute for the SVG namespace, on `<a>` ([`dom_security_schema.ts#L106`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/v22.2.3/packages/compiler/src/schema/dom_security_schema.ts#L106)):

```ts
registerContext(SecurityContext.URL, SVG_NAMESPACE, [['a', ['href', 'xlink:href']]]);
```

`use` is not there, so `securityContext(':svg:use', 'href', true)` lands on `checkSecurityContext('use', 'href', 'svg')` and returns `SecurityContext.NONE`, and `'xlink:href'`
resolves through the same lookup to the same thing. The compiler emits `ɵɵattribute` with the sanitizer slot empty, and its own checked-in golden uses this element and shows it
([`namespace_attr.js#L7`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/v22.2.3/packages/compiler-cli/test/compliance/test_cases/r3_compiler_compliance/elements/namespace_attr.js#L7)):

```js
$r3$.ɵɵattribute('href', ctx.value, null, 'xlink');
//                                  ^^^^ the sanitizer argument
```

`<use href>` fetches a document and clones it into the page, and handlers and hyperlinks in that clone are live, so the attribute does what `iframe[src]`, `object[data]` and `embed[src]` do. Those three are `RESOURCE_URL`. That one missing schema entry is the whole defect, and since every spelling of the binding fails through the same lookup, one entry fixes all of them.

A dangerous form is the one where the bound value reaches the document part of the URL, and `[attr.href]` / `[attr.xlink:href]` is the only way to bind this attribute, so there is no other syntax an application can move to.

**Route A, a `data:` URL in any field the app binds.** An
attacker's: one stored text field that the app later binds is the entire vector.

```html
<!-- iconUrl = 'data:image/svg+xml;base64,' + btoa(profile.icon) + '#x' -->
<svg><use [attr.href]="iconUrl"></use></svg>
```

It executed on Chrome 116 and on Firefox 104 to 121, and on Chrome 113, 114 and 115, with
15, 20 and 16 hits out of 24 launches against 24 of 24 on 116. I bound it as a literal string and as one
built with `btoa()` at runtime, with the same result. On WebKit no `data:` URL reached the document in 30
spellings and the `<use>` box stayed 0x0, so there the refusal is at the load and not at the handler.

**Route B, bytes at a URL on the app's own origin.** Two ways to put them there, an upload the app serves
back or any endpoint whose response parses as XML and carries the attacker's `<svg>` somewhere inside it:

```html
<svg><use [attr.href]="iconUrl"></use></svg>
<!-- iconUrl  = '/uploads/avatar.png#x' -->
<svg><use [attr.xlink:href]="iconUrl"></use></svg>
<!-- the more common spelling in real code -->
<svg><use [attr.href]="apiUrl"></use></svg>
<!-- apiUrl   = '/api/profile.xml#x', no upload -->
<svg><use [attr.href]="assetUrl"></use></svg>
<!-- assetUrl = '/asset.svg', WebKit from 26.5 -->
```

`<use>` resolves the fragment to an element id, so the response does not have to be an SVG file. 9 of the 12 envelopes I served through the app's own `/api/profile.xml` ran on Chrome 121, and the same 9 onWebKit: a feed, a SOAP body, a sitemap, an XML API response, an XHTML page, a record list, an `<?xml?>`prologue, bytes after the root element, and the `<svg>` four levels deep in an unrelated namespace. Firefox 156 stops at the trailing bytes, so it ran 8; a JSON envelope, bytes before the root and no
`xmlns` never ran.

Route B needs from that response is the follow Same-origin, with or without CORS, and a 2xx status, on every engine.

Chrome and Firefox also require an XML or SVG media type and a fragment in the URL. WebKit never checks the media type: the same bytes run as `image/png`, `text/plain`,
`application/octet-stream` and `text/html`, which are the four a team picks on purpose to be safe. And from 26.5 it needs no fragment either, which is the fragmentless shape above. `Content-Disposition: attachment`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, a `.png` path and a CSP on the response itself change nothing anywhere, and that is the usual "serve user uploads safely" configuration, the default in Rails ActiveStorage proxy mode and Django `FileResponse(as_attachment=True)`. On WebKit nothing on the response blocks it, and the only control left is serving uploads from another origin.

By browser build:

| Browser          | Route A | Route B                |
| ---------------- | ------- | ---------------------- |
| Chrome 113–115   | yes     | no                     |
| Chrome 116       | yes     | yes                    |
| Chrome 117–121   | no      | yes                    |
| Chrome 122–158   | no      | no, the sprite renders |
| Firefox 104–121  | yes     | yes                    |
| Firefox 122–159  | no      | yes                    |
| WebKit 16.0–27.2 | no      | yes                    |

Firefox still runs Route B, and Mozilla closed [bug 1912763](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1912763) as INVALID because these handlers only run when everything is same-origin, which an app serving user SVG from its own origin is.

Two things in the clone are a different mechanism rather than another route. The cloned `<a>` is not a handler at all but a live hyperlink, so `<a href="javascript:">` runs on a trusted click on Chrome **115 and 122**, where every handler sink is inert, which puts its window at 115 to 122 rather than 116 to 121. And `<foreignObject><details open="open" ontoggle>` fires with **no interaction and no resource load**, which is what defeats stripping `on*` from uploads or refusing `<image>`.


### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

See https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/ng-bypass-svg-xss

You can run 

```bash
npm install
npm run fixtures
npm run matrix -- --angular 22 --chrome 121 --firefox 121 --suite floor
npm run matrix -- --angular 22 --chrome 121 --suite xml
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular: 20.3.34, 21.2.25, 22.2.3
Node: 24.16.0
OS: Windows 11 x64

Chrome for Testing 113–123, 125, 130, 135, 140, 145, 150, 155–158; Chromium 107–116, 121, 122
Firefox 104, 112, 115, 117–123, 133, 138, 143, 148, 153, 156, 159; ESR 115, 140, 153
WebKit 16.0 to 27.2, 19 Playwright builds over 11 versions (not Safari itself)
```

### Anything else?

All tests were performed on Windows, so I can't give a completely reliable guarantee for Safari. I believe the WebKit validation should be relatively reliable, and I would appreciate it if someone could validate it manually. (I have validated this completely manually in both Chrome and Firefox.)

title: signal forms: keyInParent() returns a string for array items (typed as number)
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

In signal forms, the type of `FieldState.keyInParent()` doesn't match what it returns at runtime for array items.

It is declared as `Signal<TKey>`, where `TKey` is `number` for children of an array field, and the JSDoc says:

> If the parent field is array-valued, for example, this is the index of this field in that array.

At runtime it returns a string:

```ts
const f = form(signal({items: [{n: 'a'}, {n: 'b'}]}));

f.items[1]().keyInParent(); // '1' (string); the type says number
```

Because the type says `number`, code like this compiles but never matches:

```ts
items.filter((_, i) => i !== item().keyInParent());
```

The string seems to come from how keys are produced rather than from a deliberate choice: the parent's children map is built from `Object.keys(value)` (`packages/forms/signals/src/field/structure.ts`, `computeChildrenMap`), and the field proxy's `get` trap receives `'1'` for `f.items[1]`, so the key is a JS property-key string. `FieldNode.keyInParent` passes that string through as-is. (`FieldContext.index` already converts the same key with `Number(key)`.)

Two ways to resolve it:

1. Return a number for children of array fields, which matches the declared type and the JSDoc.
2. Keep the string and change the type (and JSDoc) to `string`.

I'll open a PR for option 1, since it follows the existing type and docs, but either option removes the mismatch.

This was also noticed in passing in a comment on #67241.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

Inline above. As a test:

```ts
it('keyInParent is a number for array items', () => {
  const f = TestBed.runInInjectionContext(() =>
    form(signal({items: [{n: 'a'}, {n: 'b'}]})),
  );
  expect(f.items[1]().keyInParent()).toBe(1); // fails: received '1'
});
```

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```
Expected '1' to be 1.
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```
@angular/forms 22.2.3
Also reproduced on main (5244ea781d).
```

### Anything else?

_No response_

title: SSR drops property bindings that domino doesn't reflect, like `[popover]`, `[inert]` or `[max]` on `<meter>`
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? platform-server ### Is this a regression? No ### Description During SSR, a property binding ends up as `el[name] = value` on the domino element. When domino doesn't define that property, the value is stored as a plain JavaScript property and never reaches the HTML. The browser shows that HTML until hydration, and content in `@defer (hydrate never)` keeps it for good. ```html
Popover content
``` Server output: ```html
Popover content
``` So until the app hydrates, the popover content shows up inline and the button doesn't open it, the fieldset accepts input, and the meter is drawn full (42 against the default max of 1). To see how far this goes, I compared every property in the compiler's DOM schema with what domino defines, and kept the ones Chrome reflects to an attribute. Leaving out obsolete elements, the main ones are: - all elements: `popover`, `inert`, `autofocus`, `autocapitalize`, `inputMode` (domino defines `autoFocus` and `autoCapitalize`, so the standard names don't match) - `img`: `decoding` - `video`: `playsInline`, `disablePictureInPicture`, and `disableRemotePlayback` on media elements - `button` and `input`: `popoverTargetAction`; `input`: `formAction` - `meter`: `min`, `max`, `low`, `high`, `optimum` - `td` and `th`: `headers` A few others are lost too, like `contentEditable`, `slot`, `part` and token lists such as `relList`. #71470 adds `command`, `name` on `details`, `autocorrect`, `webkitdirectory` and `rel` on `form` to the schema, and they hit the same problem. It leaves `fetchPriority` out for this reason: a priority hint that only arrives after hydration is too late. While looking at this, I also found that `button`, `fieldset`, `label`, `meter`, `object`, `output` and `progress` share a single property object in domino's `htmlelts.js`. Each of them inherits the reflected attributes of the ones defined before it, so `fieldset.type` returns `"submit"` and `progress` has `formAction` and `data`. I opened angular/domino#54, which fixes all of the above. With it, the server output of the template above has `popover="auto"`, `inert=""` and `max="100"`. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug There's no StackBlitz since this is about the server output. In any SSR app, add the template above and look at the page source, or call `renderApplication()` with it. ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true No error with an AOT build: the attributes are just missing from the server HTML. ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular: 22.2.3 (@angular/platform-server bundles domino 1929b1e, same as main) Node: 24.21.0 ``` ### Anything else? This is the same kind of problem as #69785, which was fixed in angular/domino#34. Once the domino version is bumped here, `fetchPriority` on `img` and `link` could be added to the schema.

title: Router reloads the page when it rolls back a navigation with `withExperimentalPlatformNavigation()`
Support `focusReset` in `NavigationBehaviorOptions`
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

router

### Description

With `withExperimentalPlatformNavigation()`, the router intercepts `navigate` events and passes `scroll` to `NavigateEvent#intercept()`, but not `focusReset`. The browser default for `focusReset` is `'after-transition'`: when a navigation finishes, focus moves to the first `autofocus` element or to the `<body>`. That's right after following a link to another page. It isn't for navigations that keep the user on the same view, like a search field that writes its value to a query param while the user types.

angular.dev runs into this on its API reference page:

1. Open https://angular.dev/api in Chrome. The filter field has focus.
2. Type `signal` at a normal speed.
3. The field only contains `s`. The URL is `/api?query=s` and focus is on `<body>`, so the other keys never reach the field.

next.angular.dev behaves the same. The filter does this on each change (`api-reference-list.component.ts`):

```ts
this.router.navigate([], {
  queryParams: params,
  replaceUrl: true,
  preserveFragment: true,
  scroll: 'manual',
});
```

It already turns off scrolling with `scroll: 'manual'`, but nothing can turn off the focus reset. The classic router never moves focus, so this code worked until angular.dev switched to platform navigation in #71504. Any app with a search-as-you-type field will hit the same thing when it makes that switch.

`scroll` was added to `NavigationBehaviorOptions` to match the `NavigateEvent#intercept()` options (a03c82564d, #64417). `focusReset` is the other one, and today every router navigation gets the browser default.

### Proposed solution

A `focusReset` option next to `scroll`, with the same values (`'manual' | 'after-transition'`), passed to `intercept()`:

```ts
this.router.navigate([], {
  queryParams: params,
  replaceUrl: true,
  scroll: 'manual',
  focusReset: 'manual',
});
```

When it isn't set, nothing changes: the browser default still applies, so link navigations keep resetting focus. With the classic router the option has no effect, since that router never moves focus.

#71595 implements it.

### Alternatives considered

- A `navigate` listener in the app that calls `event.intercept({focusReset: 'manual'})` after the router's own `intercept()` call. It works (I tried it on angular.dev), but the app has to decide, far from the `router.navigate()` call, which navigations keep focus. It also relies on two listeners calling `intercept()` on the same event.
- The router skipping the focus reset on its own when only the query params change. It would be closer to the classic router, but it's a guess: some of those navigations may want focus to go back to the top of the page, and there would be no way to ask for it.

title: Router intercepts `<a download>` links with `withExperimentalPlatformNavigation()`
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? router ### Is this a regression? No ### Description With `withExperimentalPlatformNavigation()`, the router intercepts every same-origin `navigate` event under the app's base href, except reloads. That includes two kinds of navigations it can't handle: - ``: the event has `downloadRequest` set and `canIntercept: true`. The router turns it into an SPA navigation to `/report.csv`, and the file is never downloaded. - `
`: the event has `formData` set and `canIntercept: true`. The router navigates to `/submit` inside the app, and the POST request is never sent. Without the feature, both work as expected, since the router only handles clicks on `RouterLink`. GET forms are fine either way: they don't carry `formData`, and turning them into SPA navigations is the point of the feature. angular.dev hits the first case since #71504. On next.angular.dev (22.3.0-next.2+sha-16932e9), the download links on [/ai/develop-with-ai](https://next.angular.dev/ai/develop-with-ai) (`` and the ones in the table below it) open the "Page Not Found" page instead of downloading the file. #71504 is on 22.2.x too, so angular.dev will get the same behavior with its next deployment. `NavigationStateManager.handleNavigate` returns early when `canIntercept` is false or when `navigationType` is `'reload'` (added in dbd50be7f7 for #66746), but doesn't check `downloadRequest` or `formData`. The `shouldNotIntercept` example in the Chrome article linked from the `withExperimentalPlatformNavigation` docs leaves both of them to the browser. #71552 leaves both to the browser. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug No hosted reproduction, but this is self-contained: ```ts import {Component} from '@angular/core'; import {bootstrapApplication} from '@angular/platform-browser'; import {provideRouter, withExperimentalPlatformNavigation} from '@angular/router'; @Component({ selector: 'app-root', template: ` Download report.csv
`, }) class App {} bootstrapApplication(App, { providers: [provideRouter([{path: '**', children: []}], withExperimentalPlatformNavigation())], }); ``` In Chrome, clicking the link changes the URL to `/report.csv` and nothing is downloaded. Submitting the form changes the URL to `/submit`, and the server never gets the POST. The download case can also be seen live on https://next.angular.dev/ai/develop-with-ai. ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true No error. Both become SPA navigations. ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular 22.2.1 in Chrome 155, and next.angular.dev (22.3.0-next.2+sha-16932e9). 22.2.3 ships the same check. ``` ### Anything else? _No response_

title: Event replay: early click leaves stale __jsaction cache, making prerendered target="_blank" links permanently unclickable
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? Don't known / other ### Is this a regression? Yes ### Description # Angular issue: an early click makes a prerendered `target="_blank"` link permanently unclickable (stale `__jsaction` cache) **Package:** `@angular/core` (event replay / incremental hydration) **Version:** 22.2.3 (reproduced on a fresh `ng new --ssr` project; first seen after upgrading an app from 19 to 22) **Browser:** Chrome (stable) ## Description With the v22 default `provideClientHydration()` (incremental hydration, which brings event replay), a prerendered `` that is clicked while event replay is still active becomes **permanently unclickable**. Every later click is `preventDefault()`ed by the event contract, even after Angular has removed the `jsaction` attribute. No new tab opens until the page is reloaded. Clicking only after the app is stable works. Using `withNoIncrementalHydration(), withEventReplay()` also works. ## Minimal reproduction `ng new repro --ssr --routing --defaults` (Angular 22.2.3), then replace three files: `src/app/app.ts` ```ts import { Component, PendingTasks, inject } from '@angular/core'; import { RouterLink, RouterOutlet } from '@angular/router'; @Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [RouterLink, RouterOutlet], template: ` Open /other in a new tab `, }) export class App { constructor() { // Stand-in for an HTTP request in flight after load: keeps the app unstable for 3 s. inject(PendingTasks).run(() => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 3000))); } } ``` `src/app/other.ts` ```ts import { Component } from '@angular/core'; @Component({ selector: 'app-other', template: `

Other page

` }) export class Other {} ``` `src/app/app.routes.ts` ```ts import { Component } from '@angular/core'; import { Routes } from '@angular/router'; import { Other } from './other'; @Component({ selector: 'app-home', template: `

Home page

` }) class Home {} export const routes: Routes = [ { path: '', component: Home }, { path: 'other', component: Other }, ]; ``` `app.config.ts` stays as generated: `provideClientHydration()`. Build (`ng build`, prerender), serve `dist/repro/browser` statically, open `/`. ## Steps 1. Within the first ~3 s (app bootstrapped, not yet stable), click "Open /other in a new tab". 2. Wait until the app is stable; the `jsaction` attribute disappears from the link. 3. Click the link again. **Expected:** step 3 opens `/other` in a new tab. **Actual:** nothing happens. The click is `preventDefault()`ed by the event contract; this repeats on every click until reload. Control cases (same app, real trusted clicks): | Configuration | Early click, then click at 6 s | Clicks only at 6 s and 8 s | |---|---|---| | `provideClientHydration()` (v22 default) | **6 s click: no tab** (`defaultPrevented=true`) | both open a tab | | `provideClientHydration(withNoIncrementalHydration(), withEventReplay())` | both open a tab | both open a tab | Stack of the `preventDefault()` on the 6 s click (dev build): `Dispatcher.dispatch` → `EventDispatcher.dispatch` → `_EventContract.dispatcher` → `_EventContract.handleEventInfo` → `_EventContract.handleEvent` → listener on ``. ## Root cause (from the 22.2.3 sources) 1. On the early click, `ActionResolver.parseActions(element)` parses `jsaction="click:;"` and caches the parsed map **on the element** as the property `element.__jsaction` (`set(actionElement, actionMap)`). 2. When the block/app is cleaned up, `removeListeners(el)` does `el.removeAttribute('jsaction'); el.removeAttribute('ngb'); el.__jsaction_fns = undefined;` but it **does not clear `el.__jsaction`**. 3. With incremental hydration enabled, the `EventContract` is not cleaned up after `whenStable()`. `withEventReplay`'s bootstrap listener only calls `eventContract.cleanUp()` on app destroy when `isIncrementalHydrationEnabled`, so the `` listener stays active. 4. On every later click, `parseActions` returns the stale cached map, so an action is found. Because the element is an `` and the event is a click, `shouldPreventDefaultBeforeDispatching` returns true and the default (opening the new tab) is cancelled. RouterLink then leaves `target="_blank"` to the browser, so nothing navigates. Without the early click, `__jsaction` was never cached; after the attribute is removed `parseActions` sees no attribute, and the click is not prevented. With incremental hydration off, the contract is cleaned up at stable, so the stale cache is never consulted. Same-tab `routerLink`s mask the problem (RouterLink navigates itself after the default is prevented); any anchor that relies on the browser default (`target="_blank"`, plain `href` with a `(click)` listener, download links) is affected. ## Workaround we use An inline script at the end of `index.html` removes `jsaction` from `a[target="_blank"]` before any click, so these links are never intercepted or cached: ```html ``` ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug _No response_ ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular CLI : 22.2.3 Angular : 22.2.3 Node.js : 24.21.0 Package Manager : npm 11.19.0 Operating System : darwin arm64 ``` ### Anything else? _No response_

title: Inconsistent behavior in processing query params Params across different router functions
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

router

### Is this a regression?

No (same on 21)

### Description

All related functions, to my knowledge, except `createUrlTreeFromSnapshot`, allow removing specific parameters from URLs by specifing their keys with null-ish value, eg.:

```
this.router.navigate(['./'], { queryParams: { hello: null } });
```

Above would remove "hello" query parameter when executed.

The `createUrlTreeFromSnapshot` however behaves differently:

```
 this.router.navigateByUrl(
    createUrlTreeFromSnapshot(this.activatedRoute.snapshot, [], {
      hello: null,
    })
  );
```

Above would set "hello" query parameter to "null" (so ?hello=null).

This is especially perplexing, given constructing URL tree manually works just fine:

```
this.router.navigateByUrl(
    this.router.createUrlTree(['/'], { queryParams: { hello: null } })
);
```

above would also clear the "hello" key.

title: Event replay: early event contract listeners on <body> are never removed after hydration
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

core

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

When event replay is enabled (`provideClientHydration(withEventReplay())`), the server adds an inline script to the page:

```js
window.__jsaction_bootstrap(document.body, "ng", ["click"], []);
```

This script adds listeners to `<body>`. They store each event in a queue, `window._ejsas[appId].q`, so Angular can replay events that happen before the app has loaded.

After hydration, Angular replays this queue once and sets `window._ejsas[appId]` to `undefined`. From then on, Angular handles events with its own listeners.

But the inline script's `<body>` listeners are never removed. They keep pushing every event into the same queue, and nothing reads it again. Each entry holds the event and its target element. So:

- the queue grows with every click, for the whole life of the page;
- elements removed from the page later (for example, after a route change) can't be garbage collected if they were ever clicked.

### Cause

In `packages/core/src/hydration/event_replay.ts`, `initEventReplay()` replays the early events and calls `clearAppScopedEarlyEventContract(appId)`, but never calls `removeAllAppScopedEventListeners(appId)`. The same happens in the `appRef.onDestroy()` callback, for an app destroyed before it becomes stable.

For comparison, `EventContract.replayEarlyEvents()` in `@angular/core/primitives/event-dispatch` removes the early listeners right after it replays the events.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone the repro and run:
   ```bash
   pnpm install
   pnpm build
   pnpm serve:ssr:event-replay-body-listeners-repro
   ```
2. Open http://localhost:4200.
3. Click the button, or anywhere on the page, a few times.

**Actual:** "Early event queue size" goes up by 1 on every click.

**Expected:** it stays 0 after hydration.


### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/arturovt/event-replay-body-listeners-repro

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
there's no error, memory grows because every event after hydration is added to `window._ejsas[appId].q` (captured by the early <body> listeners), and nothing reads or clears it
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular           : 22.2.3
```

### Anything else?

Related:

- #59261: elements retained by the early event contract after the app is destroyed. The fix (#66371) clears `window._ejsas[appId]`, but the `<body>` listeners still hold the queue, so this part was missed.
- #66506: a different event replay leak (the stashed listener map). Different cause.

title: Assigning to a template reference in an event binding isn't reported by the compiler
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? compiler-cli ### Is this a regression? Yes The previous version in which this bug was not present was: 17.0.0 ### Description Template references can't be reassigned, but nothing stops you from doing it in an event binding: ```html

Hello

Bye

 ``` The compiler doesn't report anything, with or without `strictTemplates`. What happens next depends on how the app is built: - With the CLI's application builder, the build fails in esbuild, on the generated code. The error points at line 21 of a 14-line file, at a name I never wrote (full output below). - In JIT, the click silently does nothing. The JIT output declares the reference with `var`, so the assignment only overwrites a local variable. - If the AOT output runs without going through esbuild (I loaded it directly in Node with jsdom), the click throws `TypeError: Assignment to constant variable.` 17.0.0 rejected the same template at compile time: ``` Cannot assign value "bye" to template variable "hello". Template variables are read-only. ``` From what I can tell, that check lived in TemplateDefinitionBuilder and went away with it. The template semantics checker reports writes to template variables (`let-x`, `@for` items, `as` aliases) with NG8005, but it only looks at `TmplAstVariable`, so references aren't covered. The type-check block declares references with `var` too, so TypeScript only complains when the assigned value has an incompatible type. The more likely way to run into this is a reference that shadows a component property, like `` with `(click)="query = ''"` in a component that has a `query` field. With `strictTemplates` you get `Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'HTMLInputElement'`, which at least fails, if confusingly. Without it, you're back to the cases above. I wasn't sure whether leaving references out of that check was on purpose, so I'm starting with an issue. If it wasn't, reporting them next to variables with the same error looks like a small change in `template_semantics_checker.ts` and in its copy in the preprocessor. I have it on a branch with tests. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug No hosted reproduction, but a fresh CLI app with this component shows it: ```ts import {Component} from '@angular/core'; import {NgTemplateOutlet} from '@angular/common'; @Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [NgTemplateOutlet], template: `

Hello

Bye

 `, }) export class App {} ``` ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true Application bundle generation failed. ✘ [ERROR] Cannot assign to "hello_r2" because it is a constant src/app/app.ts:21:225: 21 │ ....ɵɵreference(3); return i0.ɵɵresetView(hello_r2 = bye_r3); }); ╵ ~~~~~~~~ The symbol "hello_r2" was declared a constant here: src/app/app.ts:21:123: 21 │ ...ɵɵrestoreView(_r1); const hello_r2: any = i0.ɵɵreference(1)... ╵ ~~~~~~~~ ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular CLI 22.2.1 (application builder), @angular/compiler-cli 22.2.1. Same on 22.3.0-next.2 and main (d0b33ad25f). Rejected at compile time on 17.0.0. ``` ### Anything else? _No response_

title: A division right after `++` or `--` in a template is read as a regular expression
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? compiler ### Is this a regression? No ### Description Since templates support `++` and `--` (#70816), a slash that follows them is read as the start of a regular expression literal instead of a division: ```html ``` ``` Parser Error: Unexpected token 'Lexer Error: Unterminated regular expression at column 18 in expression [half = count++ / 2]' at column 19 in [half = count++ / 2] ``` With a second slash it gets stranger: in `total = count-- / size / 2`, ` size ` becomes the body of a regex and the parser reports `Unexpected token ' size '`. Host listeners behave the same way. This is valid JavaScript, and `count++ * 2` works fine. The lexer's `isStartOfRegex` treats any operator before a `/` as the start of a regex. That's right after `=` or `&&`, but after `++` or `--` a slash can only be a division. Wrapping the update in parentheses works around it: `(count++) / 2`. #71510 fixes it. Only the 22.3.0-next releases are affected, since 22.2.x doesn't have the update operators. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug No hosted reproduction, but this is enough: ```ts import {Component} from '@angular/core'; import {bootstrapApplication} from '@angular/platform-browser'; @Component({ selector: 'app-root', template: `

Count: {{ count }}

Half: {{ half }}

`, }) export class App { count = 10; half: number | null = null; } bootstrapApplication(App); ``` ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true NG5002: Parser Error: Unexpected token 'Lexer Error: Unterminated regular expression at column 18 in expression [half = count++ / 2]' at column 19 in [half = count++ / 2] NG5002: Parser Error: Lexer Error: Unterminated regular expression at column 18 in expression [half = count++ / 2] at the end of the expression [half = count++ / 2] ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true @angular/compiler 22.3.0-next.2, and main (d0b33ad25f). ``` ### Anything else? _No response_

compiler-cli declares @jridgewell/sourcemap-codec ^1.4.14 but its bundled magic-string 1.x needs ^1.6.0.
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

compiler-cli

### Is this a regression?

Yes

### Description

@angular/compiler-cli 22.x bundles a copy of magic-string 1.x. Its bundle (e.g. bundles/chunk-ECVLQ2SD.js) does:

  import { encode, encodeRangeMappings } from "@jridgewell/sourcemap-codec";

`encodeRangeMappings` was added in @jridgewell/sourcemap-codec 1.6.0. But package.json declares
`"@jridgewell/sourcemap-codec": "^1.4.14"`, which also allows 1.4.x and 1.5.x.

Any project whose lockfile already resolves sourcemap-codec to 1.4.x/1.5.x (very common, since
many tools such as magic-string 0.30.x and @babel/* depend on it) keeps that version when upgrading
to Angular 22. Loading the compiler then crashes at runtime.

Expected: the declared range matches what the code needs, i.e. "^1.6.0".
Workaround: `yarn up -R @jridgewell/sourcemap-codec` (or the npm equivalent) to bump the
lockfile entry.

Not fixed in 22.2.3; it still declares ^1.4.14.

mkdir repro && cd repro && npm init -y
npm i @jridgewell/sourcemap-codec@1.5.5 @angular/compiler-cli@22.2.2 @angular/compiler@22.2.2 @angular/core@22.2.2 typescript@6.0.3 rxjs

feat(core): ship the angular-developer agent skill inside the @angular/core package
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

core

### Description

Proposes a fix for #68937.

`npx skills add https://github.com/angular/skills` copies the skill for the latest Angular version, and the copy does not change when the project upgrades. Shipping the skill in `@angular/core` keeps the skill and the framework at the same version, and `ng update` updates both.

Version alignment is the stated goal of shipping skills in npm packages ([skills-npm proposal](https://github.com/antfu/skills-npm/blob/main/PROPOSAL.md), [skills-npm#33](https://github.com/antfu/skills-npm/issues/33)). Tools that link `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` from `node_modules` into agent skill directories:

- **pnpm** 12.11.0 ([docs](https://pnpm.io/agent-skills), [RFC pnpm/rfcs#35](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/pull/35)): `pnpm install` links skills of direct dependencies after `pnpm approve`.
- **`npx skills experimental_sync`** in skills v1.7.4 ([docs](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/docs/commands.md#skills-experimental_sync), RFC [vercel-labs/skills#2323](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/2323)): links skills of installed dependencies, for any package manager. Usually run from `prepare`.
- **[antfu/skills-npm](https://github.com/antfu/skills-npm)**: same approach, being merged into the `skills` CLI.
- **vlt**: `vlt skills` / `--allow-skills` ([vltpkg/vltpkg#1983](https://github.com/vltpkg/vltpkg/pull/1983)), merged, not released yet.

### Proposed solution

Ship `skills/dev-skills/angular-developer` as `skills/angular-developer/` in `@angular/core`, via a filegroup in the `ng_package` `srcs`, like `resources/best-practices.md`.

- One level deep (`skills/<name>/SKILL.md`), which pnpm requires. No `package.json` field needed.
- Leave out `angular-new-app`, which is used before `@angular/core` is installed.

```
# pnpm
$ pnpm approve
# -> .claude/skills/pnpm-@angular+core-angular-developer -> node_modules/@angular/core/skills/angular-developer

# npm / yarn
$ npx skills experimental_sync -y
# -> .agents/skills/angular-developer -> node_modules/@angular/core/skills/angular-developer
```

### Concerns

- **Download size**: every install, including CI and production builds, downloads the skill (about 60 KB gzipped, about 4% of the 1.57 MB `@angular/core` tarball). Raised in [antfu/skills-npm#32](https://github.com/antfu/skills-npm/issues/32) and [npm/cli#9222](https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/9222), without a resolution.
- **No standard**: npm distribution is not in the Agent Skills spec ([agentskills/agentskills#81](https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills/issues/81) was closed as not planned). `experimental_sync` is experimental.
- **pnpm install failures**: after approval, `pnpm install` fails when no agent skill directory exists, for example in a Docker build that does not copy `.claude/` ([pnpm/pnpm#16744](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/16744)).
- **Duplicates**: users who ran `npx skills add` would have two copies for possibly different versions.
- **Overlap** with `resources/best-practices.md`.

`downgradeComponent()` compiles content that AngularJS directives wrote into its element
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? upgrade ### Is this a regression? No ### Description When a downgraded component is created, [`compileContents()`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/v22.2.3/packages/upgrade/src/common/src/downgrade_component_adapter.ts#L68-L83) compiles whatever is inside its element at that moment, not only the original template: ```ts const projectableNodes: Node[][] = this.groupProjectableNodes(); // this.element.contents() const linkFns = projectableNodes.map((nodes) => this.$compile(nodes)); ``` The directive is [`terminal`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/v22.2.3/packages/upgrade/src/common/src/downgrade_component.ts#L126-L129), but with priority 0, so other priority 0 directives on the same element still run. If one of them already wrote a value into the element, that value is compiled as an AngularJS template, and a `{{ }}` in the data runs as an expression. AngularJS itself takes transcluded content when the template is compiled, before any binding runs, so the same templates are inert without the downgraded component. In the examples the value is only bound as data, nothing passes it to `$compile`. The payload is ```text `{{constructor.constructor('alert(document.domain)')()}}`. ``` I found two ways the content gets there first. **1. With `downgradeModule()`, the component is created after the module bootstraps** ```html

``` `UserBadgeComponent` only has ``. It is created once the Angular module [bootstraps](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/v22.2.3/packages/upgrade/src/common/src/downgrade_component.ts#L243-L245), and by then `ng-bind` already wrote the name into the element. This affects every downgraded element linked before the module is ready, like all the items of an `ng-repeat`. Elements linked later are fine. An Angular app that lazy loads AngularJS, like the ["Lazy Loading AngularJS"](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/16.2.12/aio/content/guide/upgrade.md?plain=1#L614-L697) example, bootstraps both on every navigation to that route, so it happens on every visit. `ng-bind-html` works the same way and doesn't even need `{{ }}`. `$sanitize` keeps ``, and [`ngBind` is `restrict: 'AC'`](https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/v1.8.3/src/ng/directive/ngBind.js#L56), so filtering `{{` out of the data doesn't help. With `UpgradeModule` the component is created while the element is linked, before `ng-bind` writes anything, so these values stay text. **2. With `ng-transclude` on the element, also with `UpgradeModule`** A wrapper that forwards its content to a downgraded component: ```js .directive('profileCard', () => ({ transclude: true, template: '', })) ``` ```html {{u.name}} ``` `ngTransclude` and `appCard` both have priority 0, so AngularJS [sorts them by name](https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/v1.8.3/src/ng/compile.js#L3750-L3755) and runs their post-link functions [in reverse](https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/v1.8.3/src/ng/compile.js#L3370-L3371). `ngTransclude` appends the linked content first, and then `compileContents()` compiles it again, which the AngularJS compiler guide calls [double compilation](https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/v1.8.3/docs/content/guide/compiler.ngdoc#L383-L389). In AngularJS 1.8.3, `ng-href` and `ng-src` [write their value while linking](https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/v1.8.3/src/ng/directive/attrs.js#L424-L426), so a `{{ }}` in `u.website` runs. With `UpgradeModule` this needs a component name that sorts before `ngTransclude`. With `downgradeModule()` any name works on the first render, and even a plain `href="{{u.website}}"` runs. An `` inside the element throws `ngTransclude:orphan` ([#44753](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/44753)), so the attribute is how a wrapper can forward its content to a downgraded component. | Template | `downgradeModule()` | `UpgradeModule` | Without the downgraded component | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------- | | `ng-bind` on the element | alert | no alert | no alert | | `ng-bind-html` on the element | alert | no alert | no alert | | `ng-transclude` + `ng-href` / `ng-src` | alert | alert | no alert | | `ng-transclude` + plain `href="{{ }}"` | alert | no alert | no alert | ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug See https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/angular-upgrade-ng-bind-xss, one app per case. ### Anything else? I don't have much experience with `@angular/upgrade`, so maybe I'm missing something. But I think this is a security issue. The [upgrade guide](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/16.2.12/aio/content/guide/upgrade.md?plain=1#L224-L226) says that on a downgraded element "you can apply additional AngularJS directives to it, but _not_ Angular directives", and the AngularJS [security guide](https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/v1.8.3/docs/content/guide/security.ngdoc#L35-L36) says "If an attacker has access to control AngularJS templates or expressions, they can exploit an AngularJS application via an XSS attack". Here plain data ends up compiled as a template.

title: zone.js: CommonJS Promise.all ignores Set inputs and resolves prematurely
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

zone.js

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

In `zone.js@0.16.3`, loading Zone.js through CommonJS causes `Promise.all()` to ignore promises supplied in a `Set`. It fulfills with an empty array, including when the input contains a pending promise.

This caused intermittent database migration test failures in an application using RxDB, which passes a `Set` of pending writes to `Promise.all()`.

### Minimal reproduction

Tested with Node.js `v24.22.0`:

```sh
npm install zone.js@0.16.3

node -e 'require("zone.js"); Promise.all(new Set([Promise.resolve(1)])).then(console.log)'
```

**Expected:** `[1]`  
**Actual:** `[]`

The same expression produces the expected result with native Promises and with Zone.js loaded through `import('zone.js')`.

### Investigation

The published `bundles/zone.umd.js` contains this loop inside `ZoneAwarePromise.allWithCallback`:

```js
for (var _i = 0, values_3 = values; _i < values_3.length; _i++) {
```

Since a `Set` has no `.length` property, the loop skips its elements.

The [TypeScript source](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/zone.js-0.16.3/packages/zone.js/lib/common/promise.ts#L451) uses `for…of`. However, the separate [ES5 compilation commands](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/zone.js-0.16.3/packages/zone.js/tools/zone_bundle.bzl) omit `--downlevelIteration`.

Compiling the working bundle with those options reproduces the failure. Adding `--downlevelIteration` preserves iterable handling and fixes the reproduction.
