title: i18n hydration: ICU content is duplicated when several component instances share the same `ngh` hydration data
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? core ### Is this a regression? No ### Description With `provideClientHydration(withI18nSupport())`, an ICU expression (`plural`) is rendered twice after hydration when the same component appears more than once on a page and the instances have identical hydration annotations (same structure and same active ICU case). SSR output (correct): ```html
21 modelos
...
19 modelos
``` DOM after client hydration (production build): ```html
21 modelos
...
19 modelos19 modelos
``` The first instance hydrates correctly. Every later instance that shares the same `ngh` index gets duplicated ICU content. In a development build, the same page throws during hydration instead: ``` ERROR Error: ASSERTION ERROR: expected matching nodeType [Expected=> 8 == 3 <=Actual] ``` #### Root cause 1. On the server, `SerializedViewCollection.add()` (`packages/core/src/hydration/annotate.ts`) deduplicates serialized views by `JSON.stringify`. Both component instances therefore get the same `ngh="N"`, and the case queue for the ICU (`"l": {"": [1]}`) is serialized only once. 2. On the client, `retrieveHydrationInfoImpl()` (`packages/core/src/hydration/utils.ts`) assigns `data = nghData[Number(nghAttrValue)]` without copying it. Embedded views do the same in `locateDehydratedViewsInContainer()` (`data: serializedView`). Every instance with the same `ngh` gets **the same object**. 3. `prepareI18nBlockForHydrationImpl()` (`packages/core/src/hydration/i18n.ts`) takes that shared array and **mutates** it: ```ts const caseQueue = hydrationInfo.data[I18N_DATA]?.[index - HEADER_OFFSET] ?? []; // ... const selectedCase = state.isConnected ? context.caseQueue.shift() : null; ``` The first instance calls `shift()` and empties the shared array. For the second instance `caseQueue.shift()` returns `undefined`. No ICU case is treated as connected, so the server-rendered text nodes of the active case are never claimed and the client renders the case again next to them. In dev mode the hydration cursor is then on the wrong node, which triggers the `nodeType` assertion. The same thing happens when the views are repeated by a `MULTIPLIER` (`"x"`), because those views also share the serialized object. #### Suggested fix Do not mutate the serialized data, for example: ```ts const caseQueue = [...(hydrationInfo.data[I18N_DATA]?.[index - HEADER_OFFSET] ?? [])]; ``` Alternatively, consume the queue with an index instead of `shift()`. #### Workaround Replace the ICU with control flow and separate i18n messages: ```html @if (count === 1) { 1 item } @else { {{ count }} items } ``` ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug Minimal setup (SSR + `provideClientHydration(withI18nSupport())`): ```ts @Component({ selector: 'app-count', template: ` @if (count) { {count, plural, =1 {1 item} other {{{count}} items}} } `, }) export class CountComponent { @Input() count = 0; } @Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [CountComponent], template: ` `, }) export class AppComponent {} ``` ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug _No response_ ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true ERROR Error: ASSERTION ERROR: expected matching nodeType [Expected=> 8 == 3 <=Actual] (dev mode only; in production the ICU content is silently duplicated) ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular: 18.2.14 (application builder, SSR prerendering, compile-time localization) The same code is unchanged in 19.2.25, 20.3.34, 21.2.25, 22.2.3 and 22.3.0-next.2. ``` ### Anything else? _No response_

body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? compiler ### Is this a regression? Yes ### Description Up to 22.2, `a--b` in a template meant `a - -b`, and `a++b` meant `a + +b`. Now that `++` and `--` are update operators (#70816), `a--b` is read like in JavaScript, as `a--` followed by `b`. I think that's fine, it isn't valid JavaScript either. What's confusing is the error you get when a template still has it: ```html

{{ a--b }}

``` ``` Parser Error: Bindings cannot contain assignments at column 5 in [ a--b ] ``` There's no assignment in that template, so I went looking for one before realizing the `--` was the problem. In an event binding, `(click)="x = a--b"` gives `Unexpected token 'b'`, which is closer, but it still doesn't say why. `[title]="a--1"` and `{{ a++b }}` fail the same way. I opened #71410 to keep these as errors but say what to write instead: ``` Unexpected token 'b' after the '--' decrement operator. To subtract '-b', write '- -b' ``` ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug No hosted reproduction, but this is all it takes: ```ts import {Component} from '@angular/core'; import {bootstrapApplication} from '@angular/platform-browser'; @Component({ selector: 'app-root', template: `

{{ a--b }}

`, }) export class App { a = 5; b = 3; } bootstrapApplication(App); ``` 22.2.2 renders `8`. On main it doesn't compile. ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true Parser Error: Bindings cannot contain assignments at column 5 in [ a--b ] in ng:///App/template.html@0:3 ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Reproduced on the main branch of angular/angular (ce30bb0889). 22.2.2 compiles the same template. ``` ### Anything else? There's a related change that can't show up as an error: `(click)="x = --a"` used to set `x` to `a` (two unary minuses), and now it decrements `a` first. That's what JavaScript does, so I left it alone, but it might be worth a line in the release notes for the new operators.

title: Ability to configure custom JSON parser in HttpClient - Back again!
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

common

### Description

As stated in [the issue 48167](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/48167), there are use cases where being able to inject a custom JSON parser for HttpClient would be beneficial, and a simple solution was already provided in [this PR](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/25027).
If I take the time to write this issue, it's because I came across yet another use case: supporting circular references. I'm currently developing an app that communicates with a .NET API, which maps objects to JSON with references (using $id and $ref). So currently, with HttpClient's native JSON parser, I get objects which contain $id and $ref properties, and I have 2 options : either reconstruct the reference tree from the objects after parsing, or implement my own interceptor to set the references while parsing. And so, as stated, in the previous issue, I have to copy-paste a bunch of code to make sure to implement everything correctly (XSSI_PREFIX, null for empty response body, error handling).
And finally, [a similar issue](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/21079) was opened 9 years ago. It received, as well as the other one opened in 2022, a great number of upvotes. The reason stated each time for not implementing this feature is that it's "fairly straightforward to do via an interceptor". I think the key word here is "fairly". It's not that simple, and it's useless error-prone copy-pasting done by every developer.
Given all of that, I come to the following conclusion: the need exists, and a simple solution is already implemented. So, why not do it?

### Proposed solution

Accepting [the pull request 25027](https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/25027).

### Alternatives considered

- Add the interceptor provided in [issue 48167](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/48167) to the library, so that it can be easily subclassed by a developer to safely implement they own parsing.
- Implement a feature for my specific use case: handling of the "$id-$ref" reference system directly in the native JSON parser.

title: A guard that throws a RedirectCommand takes priority over earlier guards in the same array
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

router

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

Since 22.2, guards can throw a `RedirectCommand` instead of returning it. When a guard throws, its redirect wins
even if an earlier guard in the same array is still running and also redirects.

```ts
{path: 'admin', component: Admin, canActivate: [isLoggedIn, hasPlan]}
```

- `isLoggedIn` is async and returns `new RedirectCommand(parseUrl('/login'))`.
- `hasPlan` throws `new RedirectCommand(parseUrl('/upgrade'))`.

Expected: `/login`. The [guards guide](https://angular.dev/guide/routing/route-guards#applying-guards-to-routes)
says "the router uses the result of the first guard in the array that did not return `true`, even if a later guard
finished earlier". Returning the same `RedirectCommand` from `hasPlan` instead of throwing it gives `/login`.

Actual: `/upgrade`.

The guards' results are combined with `combineLatest` in `prioritizedGuardValue`, which errors as soon as one guard
throws, before the earlier guards have finished.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://stackblitz.com/edit/ptesajgk?file=src%2Fmain.ts

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
No error. The navigation redirects to the wrong URL.
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular: 22.2.2 (@angular/router 22.2.2)
Browser: Chrome
```

### Anything else?

I have a fix with a spec ready: a thrown `RedirectCommand` is treated as that guard's result, so the guard order
applies to it like a returned one. Other errors still fail the navigation.

body: ### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? router ### Is this a regression? No ### Description When the `routerLinkActive` input changes while the link is active, the classes applied for the previous value stay on the element. ```html Home ``` - `activeClass` changes from `'active'` to `null` → the link keeps `class="active"` (expected: no class). - `activeClass` changes from `'active'` to `'selected'` → the link has `class="active selected"` (expected: `selected`). title: docs(router): Note how to respect `prefers-reduced-motion` in `withViewTransitions()`
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

router

---

### Description

`withViewTransitions()` currently triggers a view transition on every router navigation regardless of the user's `prefers-reduced-motion` setting. When the browser supports the View Transitions API, the router always calls `document.startViewTransition()`, and the browser plays at least its default root cross-fade. This happens even for users who have asked their operating system to reduce motion.

Relevant code: [`createViewTransition()` in `packages/router/src/utils/view_transition.ts`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/packages/router/src/utils/view_transition.ts). The function decides whether to run `startViewTransition()` based only on browser support (`document.startViewTransition`) and `skipNextTransition`. There is no check against `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')`.

`prefers-reduced-motion` is not a capability fallback (that part is already handled: unsupported browsers degrade to a plain DOM update). It is a deliberate user accessibility preference, often set for vestibular/motion sensitivity reasons. Treating it as the default opt-out is in line with WCAG guidance (SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions) and with how the platform itself frames the preference.

A developer *can* already honor the preference today via the `onViewTransitionCreated` callback and `transition.skipTransition()` (current workaround):

```typescript
withViewTransitions({
  onViewTransitionCreated: ({ transition }) => {
    if (matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) {
      transition.skipTransition();
    }
  },
})
```

But this is opt-in boilerplate that most developers won't know they need. The accessible behavior should be the default, following the principle of progressive enhancement: motion is the enhancement layered on top of a working, accessible baseline and not something each team has to remember to switch off.

The View Transitions integration (`withViewTransitions()` / `ViewTransitionsFeatureOptions`) is still marked `@developerPreview`, so changing the default behavior now carries essentially no ecosystem cost, so IMO now is a good point of time where the default behavior can be changed.

Note: there is a prior related issue, [#52571 — *docs: support prefers-reduced-motion in View Transitions API*](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/52571), but it was scoped to the angular.dev **website** and closed on the basis that the API already makes it *possible* to respect the preference. This request is different: it asks for the framework to make respecting the preference the **default behavior** of `withViewTransitions()`, not merely possible. A maintainer reference for the mechanism is linked in that thread: [Reacting to the reduced-motion preference (Chrome docs)](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/view-transitions/#reacting-to-the-reduced-motion-preference).

---

### Proposed solution

Make `withViewTransitions()` skip the transition by default when `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` is `true`, while still performing the DOM update (the navigation). Concretely, in `createViewTransition()` short-circuit before calling `document.startViewTransition()` when reduced motion is requested — the same way `skipNextTransition` is handled today — so neither Angular's own named transitions nor the browser's default root cross-fade run.

Add an option to `ViewTransitionsFeatureOptions` to control this, defaulting to the accessible behavior, e.g.:

```typescript
export interface ViewTransitionsFeatureOptions {
  skipInitialTransition?: boolean;
  onViewTransitionCreated?: (transitionInfo: ViewTransitionInfo) => void;

  /**
   * Whether to skip the view transition when the user has requested reduced
   * motion via `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. The DOM update (navigation)
   * still runs; only the animation is skipped.
   *
   * @default true
   */
  skipTransitionOnReducedMotion?: boolean;
}
```

- Default `true`: accessible out of the box.
- Teams that have a reason to keep animating (and provide their own reduced-motion-safe animations) can set it to `false`.
- Media-query evaluation should be guarded so it is a no-op on the server / where `matchMedia` is unavailable.

**On the breaking-change question:** this is a behavior change, but a small and
defensible one, and arguably a bug fix rather than a breaking change:

- The API is `@developerPreview`, so it is explicitly not covered by SemVer stability guarantees.
- The current behavior arguably violates the user's expressed accessibility preference, so changing it is closer to fixing a defect than removing a feature.
- The visible effect of the new default only materializes for users who have `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` set — i.e. exactly the users who asked for less motion.

---

### Alternatives considered

1. **Keep it opt-in via `onViewTransitionCreated` (status quo).** Works, but leaves the accessible behavior as hidden boilerplate most teams never add, so real apps ship motion to users who opted out. Rejected as the default.

2. **Conditionally register `withViewTransitions()` at bootstrap** by checking `prefers-reduced-motion` first (mirrors the old `NoopAnimationsModule`/`BrowserAnimationsModule` split suggested in [#52571](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/52571)). This reads the preference only once at startup and does not react to changes, requires the developer to wire it up, and spreads config logic into bootstrap. Less ergonomic than a sensible default.

3. **Document the `onViewTransitionCreated` + `skipTransition()` pattern only, without changing the default.** Better than nothing, but documentation does not change the default experience; accessibility defaults should be safe, not something you read your way into.

4. **CSS-only mitigation** (`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` around all custom keyframes). This disables the author's own animations but does **not** stop the browser's default root cross-fade that `startViewTransition()` triggers, so motion still reaches the user. It is a complement, not a substitute, for skipping the transition at the API level.

---

### Willing to contribute

I'd be happy to work on this myself and open a PR (changes to `createViewTransition()` and `ViewTransitionsFeatureOptions`, plus tests and docs). Before I start, I'd like to confirm with the team whether the proposed direction — making reduced-motion skipping the default, with an opt-out option — is acceptable, and whether you'd prefer a different API shape or naming. Happy to adjust based on your guidance.

title: compiler: selectorless lexer loops forever on a lowercase "@" attribute (e.g. animation trigger)
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? compiler ### Is this a regression? Yes — only since selectorless lexing was added. The same template lexes fine with `selectorlessEnabled: false`. ### Description When `selectorlessEnabled` is on, the HTML lexer never terminates on any `@` inside a start tag that is not followed by `_` or an uppercase letter. `_consumeTagOpen` in `packages/compiler/src/ml_parser/lexer.ts`: ```ts if (this._selectorlessEnabled && this._cursor.peek() === chars.$AT) { const start = this._cursor.clone(); const nameStart = start.clone(); nameStart.advance(); if (isSelectorlessNameStart(nameStart.peek())) { // `_` or A-Z only this._consumeDirective(start, nameStart); } } else { this._consumeAttribute(); } ``` When the character after `@` is a lowercase letter (or a digit, or another `@`), `isSelectorlessNameStart` is `false`, so the `if` body is skipped — and the `else` is not entered, because `peek() === '@'`. Nothing consumes a character, so the enclosing `while (true)` in `_consumeTagOpen` spins forever at 100% CPU. This is reachable from valid templates: `binding_parser.ts` treats any attribute whose name starts with `@` as a legacy animation label (`isLegacyAnimationLabel(name) { return name[0] == '@'; }`), and animation triggers are conventionally lowercase. A selectorless component containing `
` therefore hangs the compiler. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction The same lexer is vendored (slightly modified) in `prettier/angular-html-parser`, where the repro is unambiguous: ```js parse('
', { enableAngularSelectorlessSyntax: true }); // never returns ``` - prettier/angular-html-parser#57 — report + repro - prettier/angular-html-parser#59 — proposed fix A unit test in `packages/compiler/test/ml_parser/lexer_spec.ts` using `{selectorlessEnabled: true}` would hang the test suite (it cannot even fail; it never returns). ### Please provide the exception or error you saw No exception — the process hangs and has to be killed. Reproduced on Node 24 against `@angular/compiler` at `main`. ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in - Angular: `main` (`v22.0.0-next`), `packages/compiler` - Node: 24 - OS: Linux ### Anything else? `isSelectorlessNameStart` being `_`/`A-Z` looks intentional (cf. angular/angular#70831, which rejects `` as a lowercase selectorless segment), so the fix is **not** to accept lowercase selectorless names. The `@` branch should fall back to `_consumeAttribute()` when it cannot start a directive — which is exactly what the lexer already does when `selectorlessEnabled` is `false`. That keeps `
` a plain attribute instead of erroring, and makes the loop always advance.

title: bug(aria/menu): ngMenuContent is never destroyed once the trigger has been focused, ignoring preserveContent
body:
### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

`ngMenu` hosts `DeferredContentAware` and exposes its `preserveContent` input, which defaults to `false`. So `ngMenuContent` should behave like `ngTabContent` and `ngAccordionContent`: rendered while the panel is visible, and destroyed when it hides.

It isn't. The menu computes the content's visibility as:

```ts
contentVisible = this._pattern.visible() || !!this.parent()?._pattern.hasBeenInteracted()
```

`hasBeenInteracted` is set to `true` in `onFocusIn` / `onKeydown` of `MenuTriggerPattern`, `MenuItemPattern`, `MenuPattern` and `MenuBarPattern`, and nothing ever sets it back to `false`. That has two effects:

1. **Content is built before the menu opens.** Tabbing onto the trigger (or onto a submenu's parent item) renders the deferred rows, even if the menu is never opened.
2. **Content is never destroyed afterwards.** Once the parent has been focused, `contentVisible` is `true` for the rest of the component's life, so `preserveContent: false` has no effect, through close, Escape, outside click and item selection alike.

For comparison, tabs and accordion set `contentVisible.set(this.visible())`, and their content is torn down when hidden.

Rendering a submenu's rows when its parent item gains focus looks intentional: it lets one ArrowRight move focus straight into the submenu. The problem is that the flag is sticky. Something like "parent is focused or active right now" would keep that benefit and still allow teardown.

**Why it matters:** the main reason to defer menu content is a menu repeated per row of a table or list. With the current behaviour, every menu the user has focused, even without opening it, keeps its rows for the life of the page, and `preserveContent` can't opt out of that.

### Reproduction

Repo: https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro (section **C**, with section **D** as the tabs control)

Steps:
1. Load the page. "Live rows C" reads **0**.
2. Tab onto "Open menu C" without opening it. "Live rows C" reads **2**.
3. Press Enter, then Escape. The menu closes, and "Live rows C" still reads **2**. The rows are never destroyed.
4. Control: in section D, switch tabs. Each panel's `ngTabContent` is created and destroyed as its tab is selected and deselected.

Probe log from the steps above:

```
D: "One" created
C: "Edit" created      ← trigger focused, menu not opened
C: "Delete" created
D: "One" destroyed
D: "Two" created
D: "Two" destroyed
D: "One" created
```

(No "C … destroyed" line at any point, including after closing the menu.)

### Expected Behavior

With `preserveContent` unset (`false`), `ngMenuContent` is destroyed when the menu hides, as `ngTabContent` and `ngAccordionContent` are. Ideally it's also not rendered merely because the trigger received focus. If eager rendering on parent focus is intended for submenus, it shouldn't make the content permanent.

### Actual Behavior

The content is rendered on the first `focusin` / `keydown` of the trigger or parent item and is never destroyed until the host view is.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4
- @angular/aria / @angular/cdk: 22.2.6 (also present in 22.2.5)
- Browser: Chromium 156
- OS: macOS

---
_This issue was drafted and filed by Claude Code (an AI coding agent) on behalf of artaommahe._

title: bug(cdk/scrolling): nested viewports and overlay content inherit the outer `scrollWindow` / `cdkVirtualScrollingElement` scroller
body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### Description

`scrollWindow` and `cdkVirtualScrollingElement` provide `VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE` through `providers`, and `CdkVirtualScrollViewport` takes it with `inject(VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE, {optional: true})`. So every viewport below them in the injector tree uses the outer scroller, not just the viewport it was meant for:

- a `cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport` nested in the rows of an outer virtual list that uses `scrollWindow` or `cdkVirtualScrollingElement`;
- a `cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport` inside an overlay opened from such a row (`cdkConnectedOverlay`, and therefore also a virtual list inside a `mat-select` panel), even though the overlay isn't inside the scrolling element in the DOM at all.

Such an inner viewport never gets the `cdk-virtual-scrollable` class, so it can't scroll by itself. The mouse wheel scrolls the page or the outer element instead, the rendered range follows the outer scroller, and the rendered items spill out of the viewport box over the following rows.

The docs describe both options per viewport ("add the `scrollWindow` attribute to the `cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport`"), and nothing says nested viewports inherit the scroller. As a workaround, `{provide: VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE, useValue: null}` on a component between the two viewports makes the inner one scroll by itself again.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/7ytfjjia-a8v2qj79

It's the docs example "Virtual scrolling window" opened via "Edit in StackBlitz", with only the example file replaced.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Open the StackBlitz. The outer list uses `scrollWindow`, and every row has its own 150px high virtual list with 100 items. The red line under each inner list already says it uses the outer scroller.
2. Hover an inner list and scroll with the mouse wheel: the page scrolls, the list doesn't.
3. The radio buttons at the top switch the outer list to `cdkVirtualScrollingElement` and move the inner list into a `cdkConnectedOverlay`. All four combinations are broken.
4. Select "its own viewport" to compare: the inner lists scroll by themselves.

### Expected Behavior

A viewport nested inside another virtual scroll viewport, or rendered in an overlay, scrolls by itself, the same way it does when the outer list uses its own viewport.

### Actual Behavior

The inner viewport uses the outer scroller (`viewport.scrollable !== viewport`) in all four combinations:

- `scrollWindow`, nested in a row: the wheel scrolls the page, the inner list renders ~40 items that overflow its 150px box and follow the page scroll.
- `scrollWindow`, in an overlay: the wheel scrolls the page instead of the list.
- `cdkVirtualScrollingElement`, nested in a row: the wheel scrolls the outer element.
- `cdkVirtualScrollingElement`, in an overlay: the list can't be scrolled at all and stays on its first 30 items, which overflow the panel.

With an outer list that scrolls itself, both placements work.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.5
- CDK/Material: 22.2.6 (same with 22.3.0-next.5)
- Browser(s): Chrome 157
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS 26

---

Not a regression: the scroller has been injected this way since `VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE` was added in #24394 (14.1.0). A possible direction: a viewport could act as a boundary for its content, so viewports and overlays declared inside it don't inherit an outer scrollable, and `scrollWindow` could apply only to its own host viewport.

We ran into this with Taiga UI dropdowns that use a virtual scroll inside virtualized lists (taiga-family/taiga-ui#10095).

title: bug(aria/grid): composed cell widgets do not activate when child inputs receive focus
body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

A complex GridCellWidget composed through hostDirectives does not enter widget mode when a child input receives focus. The same markup with ngGridCellWidget applied directly works. Focus reaches the input in both cases; the difference is widget activation.

GridCell._getWidget() searches ancestors using [ngGridCellWidget], but this attribute is absent when the directive is composed. As a result, the focusin event is not forwarded to the widget pattern. This concerns widget activation, separately from cell selection in #34074.

Regression status: unknown.

### Reproduction

[Open the minimal StackBlitz reproduction](https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-pbfss5v2?file=src%2Fmain.ts).

1. Wait for the preview to display “Grid widget child focus”.
2. Click the input under “Standard directive”. Its Mode changes from CELL to WIDGET.
3. Click the input under “Composed host directive”. The input receives focus, but its Mode stays CELL.
4. Compare the two implementations in src/main.ts: both use widgetType="complex" and contain an input; the second applies GridCellWidget through hostDirectives.

The displayed Mode reads GridCellWidget.isActivated(). No synthetic events are needed.

### Expected Behavior

Both widgets should enter WIDGET mode when their child input receives focus, so grid navigation is suspended while interacting with the widget.

### Actual Behavior

The standard widget activates. The composed widget remains in CELL mode even though its child input is focused.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4
- @angular/aria and @angular/cdk: 22.2.6
- Browser: Chrome
- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon)

Also reproduced in the repository Chromium grid tests: the standard control passes and the composed case fails.

title: bug(aria/grid): clicking child content does not select cells using hostDirectives
body: ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description When `GridCell` is applied to a reusable component through `hostDirectives`, clicking text inside a child `` moves focus to the cell but does not select it. Clicking the padding on the same cell selects it correctly. The reproduction shows a standard grid and a grid using `hostDirectives` side by side. Both use `enableSelection`, `selectionMode="explicit"`, and `multi`. The standard grid selects cells when clicking either their text or their padding. The reusable cell is defined as follows: ```ts @Component({ selector: 'composed-grid-cell', template: '', hostDirectives: [GridCell], }) class ComposedGridCell {} ``` Its content is ordinary markup, for example `Composed: Second`. This makes the clickable behavior depend on whether the user clicks the text or the surrounding padding. ### Reproduction StackBlitz: https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-1z1y55cn?file=src%2Fmain.ts Wait for the preview to load. It uses Angular 22.2.4 and @angular/aria 22.2.6. **Visual indicators:** blue background = active/focused cell; green outline = selected cell. The dashed rectangle marks the child ``; the surrounding padding belongs directly to the cell host. Steps to reproduce with actual mouse clicks: 1. In the first grid, under **Direct ngGridCell**, click the text **Standard: Second** inside the dashed rectangle. The cell turns blue and gets a green outline: it is active and selected. 2. In the second grid, under **hostDirectives**, click the text **Composed: Second** inside the dashed rectangle. The cell turns blue but gets **no green outline**: focus moves, but selection does not change. 3. Click the padding of that same **Composed: Second** cell, outside its dashed rectangle. A green outline now appears: clicking the host directly selects it. Reload the preview to reset the demonstration. ### Expected Behavior With selection enabled, clicking non-interactive child content inside a cell should select the containing cell, just as clicking the cell host does. Using `GridCell` through `hostDirectives` should behave like direct `ngGridCell` usage. ### Actual Behavior | Usage / click target | Focus moves to second cell | Second cell selected | | --- | --- | --- | | Direct `ngGridCell`: child text | Yes | Yes | | `hostDirectives`: child text | Yes | **No** | | `hostDirectives`: cell padding | Yes | Yes | After clicking **Composed: Second** text, its host has `data-active="true"` but `aria-selected="false"`. Clicking its padding changes `aria-selected` to `"true"`. Possible cause: `Grid._getCell()` searches ancestors with `closest('[ngGridCell]')`, but `GridCell` does not declare that marker as a static host attribute. The marker is present with direct template usage and absent with `hostDirectives`. This report is limited to the cell selection behavior demonstrated above. It does not claim that focus fails to move, or that `GridCellWidget` is affected. ### Environment - Angular: 22.2.4 - Angular CLI / build: 22.2.4 - @angular/aria: 22.2.6 - @angular/cdk: 22.2.6 - TypeScript: 6.0.3 - Browser: Google Chrome - Operating system: macOS (Apple silicon) - Reproduction runs in StackBlitz. Regression status: unknown; an earlier working version has not been identified.

title: feat(aria/menu): expose the trigger's tabindex as a public signal on MenuTrigger
body:
### Feature Description

`MenuTrigger` computes its own tabindex (`0`, or `-1` while its open menu holds the active item) and binds it to the host (`'[attr.tabindex]': '_pattern.tabIndex()'`), but the value is only reachable through the underscored `_pattern`:
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/menu/menu-trigger.ts#L45

`Menu` already exposes the same thing publicly (`readonly tabIndex = computed(() => this._pattern.tabIndex())`):
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/menu/menu.ts#L144

The request: add the equivalent `readonly tabIndex` signal to `MenuTrigger`, next to its public `expanded` and `hasPopup`.

### Use Case

A menu trigger inside a roving-tabindex container, such as a keyboard-navigable grid or toolbar not built on `ngToolbar`/`ngGrid`. The container keeps the trigger at `tabindex="-1"` until its cell is active, while the trigger must keep aria's own `-1` while its open menu holds focus. A wrapper directive therefore combines the container's value with the trigger's own, taking the lower of the two.

Today that wrapper has to read `trigger._pattern.tabIndex()`. Deriving it from public state (`expanded() ? -1 : 0`) is wrong while the menu is open but has no active item yet, when aria keeps `0`.

A public `tabIndex` signal would make this composition possible without depending on `_pattern`. An input to let a consumer supply the tabindex would also solve it.

---
_This issue was drafted and filed by Claude Code (an AI coding agent) on behalf of artaommahe._

title: bug(aria/menu): Enter on a menu item doesn't activate the element, so link items and (click) handlers are mouse-only
body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Activating a menu item with the keyboard never reaches the item's element:

- `<a ngMenuItem href="...">` (or with `routerLink`) doesn't navigate on Enter.
- A `(click)` handler on `<button ngMenuItem>` doesn't run on Enter.

Clicking either item with the mouse works.

The menu's `KeyboardEventManager` calls `preventDefault()` on handled keys by default (https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/private/behaviors/event-manager/keyboard-event-manager.ts#L34), which cancels the browser's own activation of a link or button. `MenuPattern.submit()` then closes the menu and emits `itemSelected`, but never activates the item itself (https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/private/menu/menu.ts#L404-L421).

Navigation menus are a common use, and the WAI-ARIA APG navigation menubar example is built from `<a role="menuitem" href>` items that Enter follows. With the current behaviour, routing has to be rebuilt by hand in `itemSelected`, which also loses the href behaviours a link gives (open in new tab, etc.).

A possible fix: have `submit()` call `item.element.click()`. That's what native buttons and links do on Enter, and it makes keyboard and pointer activation run the same path.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/github/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro
Repo: https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro (section B; `node check.mjs` runs the steps with Playwright)
Steps to reproduce:
1. Tab to "Open menu B" and press Enter. Focus is on "Go to #target" (`<a ngMenuItem href="#target">`).
2. Press Enter.
3. Reopen the menu, ArrowDown to "Button with (click)" and press Enter.
4. For comparison, click both items with the mouse.

### Expected Behavior

Step 2 navigates to #target, and step 3 runs the item's (click) handler ("(click) ran" appears in the log), the same as clicking them with the mouse.

### Actual Behavior

In both steps the menu closes and focus returns to the trigger, but the URL doesn't change and the (click) handler never runs. Mouse clicks navigate and run the handler.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4
- CDK/Material: 22.2.6 (@angular/aria 22.2.6)
- Browser(s): Chromium 156
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS

title: bug(aria/menu): Escape inside a submenu closes the whole menu instead of only the submenu
body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Pressing Escape while focus is in a submenu closes every open menu and moves focus back to the root `ngMenuTrigger`. `MenuPattern` maps Escape to `closeAll()`:
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/private/menu/menu.ts#L182

The WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices menu pattern specifies one level: "Escape: Close the menu that contains focus and return focus to the element or context, e.g., menu button or parent menuitem, from which the menu was opened." (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/). The APG navigation menubar example behaves that way.

The other Angular menus already do: `@angular/cdk/menu` closes only the current menu and focuses its parent trigger (https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/cdk/menu/menu.ts#L84-L90), and `mat-menu` does the same. So a menu migrated from CDK or Material to `@angular/aria` changes keyboard behaviour.

If closing the whole tree is intended, an option to close one level would help, similar to Base UI's `closeParentOnEsc`.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/github/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro
Repo: https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro (section A; `node check.mjs` runs the steps with Playwright)
Steps to reproduce:
1. Tab to "Open menu A" and press Enter.
2. ArrowDown to "Categorize" and press ArrowRight. The submenu opens with focus on "Mark as important".
3. Press Escape.

### Expected Behavior

Only the submenu closes. Focus returns to "Categorize", and the root menu stays open.

### Actual Behavior

Both menus close and focus returns to the "Open menu A" trigger.

title: bug(MatSlider): showTickMarks can exhaust memory during SSR
body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

`ngAfterViewInit()` measures the slider only in the browser, but it builds the tick marks on the server too:

```ts
if (this._platform.isBrowser) {
  this._updateDimensions();
}
// ...
this._updateTickMarkUI();
```

`_updateTickMarkUINonRange()` allocates one entry per tick mark:

```ts
this._tickMarks = Array(numActive)
  .fill(_MatTickMark.ACTIVE)
  .concat(Array(numInactive).fill(_MatTickMark.INACTIVE));
```

The template only renders them `@if (_cachedWidth)`, and the server never sets `_cachedWidth`. So during SSR the array is built and thrown away, and nothing bounds its size: it is `(max - min) / step`.

A slider whose bounds come from the URL is enough:

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'price-range',
  imports: [MatSliderModule],
  template: `
    <mat-slider [min]="min" [max]="max" [step]="step" showTickMarks>
      <input matSliderThumb />
    </mat-slider>
  `,
})
export class PriceRange {
  private readonly params = inject(ActivatedRoute).snapshot.queryParamMap;
  readonly min = Number(this.params.get('min') ?? '0');
  readonly max = Number(this.params.get('max') ?? '100');
  readonly step = Number(this.params.get('step') ?? '1');
}
```

I served it with `RenderMode.Server` and compared `/?max=1e9` with a control of the same size, `/?max=1e2`. Each cell is three fresh workers, and `fatal` means a V8 `FATAL ERROR` with exit code 134:

| Heap                | `?max=1e2` | `?max=1e9`           |
| ------------------- | ---------- | -------------------- |
| 256 MiB             | 3/3 200    | **3/3 fatal**, 3.0 s |
| 1 GiB               | 3/3 200    | **3/3 fatal**, 5.5 s |
| 4 GiB               | 3/3 200    | **3/3 fatal**, 5.8 s |
| 16 GiB              | 3/3 200    | **3/3 fatal**, 5.6 s |
| default (4,288 MiB) | 3/3 200    | **3/3 fatal**, 5.6 s |

A bigger heap doesn't help. Above 2^25 entries `Array(n)` switches to dictionary elements, and from about 2.5e8 entries the dictionary hits V8's hash table limit before the heap fills up:

```text
FATAL ERROR: invalid table size Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
```

`?min=-1e9` and `?step=1e-7` also reach a billion tick marks and are fatal too. The values don't need to look odd either: `?max=1000000&step=0.01`, a price with cents, is 1e8 tick marks and kills a 512 MiB worker.

#26322 fixed #26317 by skipping the array when `showTickMarks` is off. With it on, the count is still unbounded, and #29496 is the browser side of the same problem. #33242 rewrites the method as a `push` loop over `Math.floor((max - min) / step) + 1`, so the count doesn't change. I applied it on top of 22.2.5: `?max=1e9` still kills a 256 MiB worker, `?max=3e7` now does too, and `?step=1e-309` goes from an immediate `RangeError` to a fatal error.

Returning early from `_updateTickMarkUI()` until `_cachedWidth` is set, which the template already requires, makes every request above return 200. The browser still builds the full array once the slider has a width.


As a note I found this while adapting `MatSlider` for a design system, using its code as the base. In an e-commerce app, passing the price filter's value or range through query parameters could OOM the SSR worker, so I would think this is a normal real use case.


### Reproduction

See  https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/angular-material-slider-ssr-oom

Steps to reproduce:

1. `npm ci && npm run build`
2. `npm run serve:ssr:srr-material-oom`
3. `curl "http://localhost:4000/?max=1e9"`


### Expected Behavior

The server renders the slider without building tick marks it can't render, and the worker keeps serving other requests.


### Actual Behavior

The SSR worker aborts with a V8 fatal error (exit code 134), and every request in flight on it fails with it.


### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4, `@angular/ssr` 22.2.5, Node.js 24.16.0 (also 21.2.25 and 20.3.34)
- CDK/Material: 22.2.5 (also 21.2.14 and 20.2.14). `main` and 22.3.0-next.4 have the same code.
- Browser(s): n/a, server-side rendering
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): Windows 11 x64

title: feat(cdk Portal): Allow DomPortal to reference detached elements
body:
### Feature Description

There is a built-in security that blocks a detached element (one that has no parent node) to be used in a DomPortal, [here](https://github.com/angular/components/blob/265b8a48718fda931ef6c57b30b371fcd926707b/src/cdk/portal/dom-portal-outlet.ts#L145).
The only purpose of this bit of code is to ensure that _if_ the DOM node is obtained the nominal way, i.e from the component's view, then it gets put back where it was before, when the operation is done or it stops being used.

### Use Case

I have a dependency that generates DOM nodes (SVG nodes to be precise). I was using a custom directive that was using `inject(ElementRef).nativeElement` and `.replaceChildren(this.inputDOMNode())`, which works but is not great.

I discovered Portal and thought I could use it, but I actually can't because the built-in security prevents me from passing a detached element to DOMPortal(). I guess I could instanciate a dummy DOM node (itself detached) to attach all my SVG nodes to it before passing them to the DOMPortal, but that's nonsense really, I just don't need the housekeeping feature of placing the node back where it was found.

title: feat(Paginator): Fix the default "1 – 10 of 100" syntax
body:
### Feature Description

By default, [Paginator](https://material.angular.dev/components/paginator/overview) shows text like "1 – 10 of 100". The space around the en-dash is incorrect syntax. There is no style guide that uses that. Even British style guides, e.g., [New Hart's Rules: The Oxford Style Guide](https://oceanide.es/losarchivos/docs/new-harts-rules-2005.pdf), which use spaces around en-dashes in some situations, don't use it for ranges.

The correct text should be "1–10 of 100".

### Use Case

While this can be replaced through `MatPaginatorIntl`, the default English label should also be correct for projects that do not need i18n. I know this is a "breaking change" as it might break screenshot and text-based tests, but it can be done for a major release.

The same use cases as the observer version.

title: bug(material/datepicker): Focus moves to a date cell instead of returning to the period button after selecting a year/month (WCAG 2.4.3)
body:
### Is this a regression?

No, this behaviour has always existed.

### Description

When the calendar’s period button (“Choose month and year”) is activated by keyboard, the calendar switches to the multi-year view and then the year view. After the user selects a year and then a month, the calendar returns to the month view and focus moves to a date cell in the calendar grid. It does not return to the period button that opened the view.

This affects keyboard and screen reader users. They can’t easily change the month or year again, because the next Tab or Shift+Tab stop is unpredictable. They have to navigate back through the grid to reach the period button. We believe this fails WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.3 (Focus Order) in accessibility audits, because the focus destination after the interaction doesn’t preserve a logical, predictable order relative to the control that triggered it.

### Reproduction

This reproduces on the official Angular Material documentation example: https://material.angular.dev/components/datepicker/overview#datepicker-custom-icon

Steps to reproduce (keyboard only):
1.Open the datepicker with the “Open calendar” button (Enter).
2.Press Tab until the “Choose month and year” period button is focused, then press Enter.
3.Use the arrow keys to select a year and press Enter.
4.Use the arrow keys to select a month and press Enter.
5.Observe where focus lands.


### Expected Behavior

Focus returns to the period button that opened the view, so users can change the month/year again or Tab onward predictably. Alternatively, expose an option to control this, for example an input on mat-calendar.

### Actual Behavior

Focus moves to a date cell (.mat-calendar-body-cell) in the month grid. The period button loses focus and the user has to navigate back to it manually.

### Environment

- Angular: 19.2.14
- CDK/Material: 19.2.19
- Browser(s): Chrome, Safari
- Operating System : macOS

title: bug(aria/accordion): Enter/Space inside a panel toggles the accordion instead of activating the focused element
body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Pressing Enter on a link (or Space on a button) inside an expanded `ngAccordionPanel` collapses the panel instead of activating the link/button.

`ngAccordionGroup` handles `keydown` for the whole group, including panel content, and calls `preventDefault()` on Enter/Space, so the focused element never gets activated. Arrow keys and Home/End are affected too, e.g. Home in an input inside a panel moves focus to the trigger.

The click handler only reacts to events coming from a trigger (`_findTriggerPattern`), the keydown handler doesn't check that:
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/952685f9370ba718f832d745512db7c9a04e1bcd/src/aria/private/accordion/accordion.ts#L73-L97

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/z5sxyaq6?file=src%2Fmain.ts

Steps to reproduce:
1. Expand "Section 1".
2. Tab to "Link inside panel" or "Button inside panel" and press Enter / Space.
3. Expand it again, click into the input and press Home.

### Expected Behavior

The link/button is activated (shows up in the log) and the panel stays open. Home moves the caret in the input.

### Actual Behavior

The panel collapses, nothing is activated. Home moves focus to the trigger.

title: Feature (MatDialog): Add an option to prevent duplicate dialogs
body:
### Feature Description

Currently, Angular Material’s MatDialog allows the same component to be opened multiple times, resulting in multiple instances of the same dialog being displayed simultaneously.

In some applications, this behavior is undesirable. For example, repeated user interactions or multiple event emissions can accidentally open the same dialog more than once.

Developers must currently implement their own duplicate detection logic using MatDialog.openDialogs or MatDialog.getDialogById() before calling MatDialog.open().

Proposed solution

It would be useful to have a built-in option in MatDialogConfig to prevent duplicate instances of the same component from being opened.

For example:

this.dialog.open(MyDialogComponent, {
  preventDuplicates: true,
});

When this option is enabled, attempting to open a component that already has an open dialog could either:

* Return the existing MatDialogRef without creating another instance.
* Ignore the new request and keep the existing dialog open.

The exact behavior could be determined by the maintainers.

Ideally, duplicate detection would be scoped to the component type, with an option to customize the behavior if needed.

Benefits

* Avoids accidentally opening multiple instances of the same dialog.
* Reduces repetitive boilerplate across applications.
* Provides a consistent, framework-level solution.
* Keeps applications simpler and less error-prone.

Alternatives considered

Currently, developers can manually inspect openDialogs or use getDialogById() before opening a dialog. However, this requires additional application-level logic and does not provide a straightforward, reusable option for this common use case.

Would this feature be a good fit for Angular Material’s MatDialog API? I’d be happy to contribute a PR if the maintainers consider this approach appropriate.

### Use Case

_No response_

bug(aria/menu): any DOM change inside an open submenu moves focus up and collapses it
body:
### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description Any DOM change inside an open `ngMenu` (a ripple, an icon that renders late, an `@if` inside an item) moves focus back up the menu tree and collapses the open submenu, even though no menu item was added, removed or moved. What happens: 1. `Menu` starts `_collection.startObserving(this.element)` in `afterNextRender`. The `MutationObserver` in `SortedCollection` bumps `_version` on any `childList` change in the menu's subtree. 2. `orderedItems` has no `equal`, so every bump produces a new array, and `Menu._items` / `_itemPatterns` change identity too. 3. The `afterRenderEffect` in `Menu`'s constructor that calls `this._pattern.listBehavior.goto(activeItem)` tracks the item list by accident: `ListFocus.focus()` reads `inputs.items()` through `isListDisabled()`. So it re-runs and focuses the menu's active item. 4. Focus moves from the open submenu to an item in a menu above it, and `MenuPattern.onFocusOut` closes the submenu. Possible fixes (any one of these avoids it): - Give `SortedCollection.orderedItems` an element-wise `equal`, so a version bump that changes no order isn't propagated. - Read the item list `untracked` in the `goto(activeItem)` effect; it only needs to re-run when `visible()` changes. - Bump `_version` only when an added node contains a registered item (the `TODO(ok7sai)` in `SortedCollection` already plans to replace the observer). ### Reproduction StackBlitz link: not attached. The standalone component below is the whole reproduction; it needs only `@angular/aria` (bootstrapped with `provideZonelessChangeDetection()`). ```ts import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core'; import { Menu, MenuItem, MenuTrigger } from '@angular/aria/menu'; @Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [Menu, MenuItem, MenuTrigger], styles: `[data-visible='false'] { opacity: 0.3; }`, template: `
Item A
Item B
Item B1
Item B2
Last item @if (menuB2.visible() && tick() % 2) { • }
`, }) export class App { protected readonly tick = signal(0); constructor() { setInterval(() => this.tick.update((n) => n + 1), 1000); } } ``` Steps to reproduce: 1. Focus **Open** and press Enter. 2. Press ArrowDown, ArrowRight, ArrowDown, ArrowRight. Focus is now on **Last item**, with both submenus open. 3. Wait up to a second, until the `@if` renders its dot. ### Expected Behavior The submenus stay open and focus stays on **Last item**: the change adds no menu item, so the menu state shouldn't change. ### Actual Behavior **Item B2** collapses (`aria-expanded="false"`) and focus moves to **Item B2**. Without the `@if` (or with the interval removed), both submenus stay open and focus stays on **Last item**. It reproduces every time, and the same way with a third submenu level. ### Environment - Angular: 22.1.4 - CDK/Material: @angular/cdk 22.1.4; @angular/aria 22.1.4 and 22.2.3 (the code involved is unchanged in 22.3.0-next.2) - Browser(s): Chromium 153 - Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS

bug(aria/combobox): ComboboxPopup throws NG0950 when destroyed before its first change detection
body:
### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description `ComboboxPopup.ngOnDestroy` calls `this.combobox()._unregisterPopup()`. The `combobox` input is `input.required()`. If the view that holds the popup is destroyed before its first update pass, the input was never set, and reading it throws `NG0950: Input "combobox" is required but no value is available yet`. Angular reports this as "Error during cleanup of component", and in tests it fails the test ("1 fixture threw errors during cleanup"). This happens in any unit test that creates a component containing a combobox and does not run change detection before teardown, for example a plain "should create" test, or a test that only checks providers. ### Reproduction ```ts import { Component } from '@angular/core'; import { TestBed } from '@angular/core/testing'; import { Combobox, ComboboxPopup, ComboboxWidget } from '@angular/aria/combobox'; import { Listbox, Option } from '@angular/aria/listbox'; @Component({ imports: [Combobox, ComboboxPopup, ComboboxWidget, Listbox, Option], template: `
Pick one
alpha
 `, }) class Repro {} it('destroys cleanly before the first change detection', () => { const fixture = TestBed.createComponent(Repro); expect(() => fixture.destroy()).not.toThrow(); // throws NG0950 }); ``` ### Expected Behavior Destroying the popup without a first change detection does nothing (there is nothing to unregister). ### Actual Behavior `NG0950: Input "combobox" is required but no value is available yet`, from `ComboboxPopup.ngOnDestroy` (`src/aria/combobox/combobox-popup.ts`, line 67 on `main`). A possible fix: register in `ngOnInit` and keep the registered combobox in a field, then unregister that field (if set) in `ngOnDestroy`, instead of reading the input again. Workaround: wrap the `ng-template ngComboboxPopup` in `@if (combobox) { … }`, so the popup is only created in an update pass. ### Environment - Angular: 22.2.1 - CDK/Material: @angular/cdk 22.2.3, @angular/aria 22.2.3 (also in 22.3.0-next.2 and `main`) - Browser(s): any (seen in Vitest with happy-dom) - Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS

title: bug(material/menu): menu restores focus to its trigger after a menu item opens a dialog (animations disabled / prefers-reduced-motion)
body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

 When a mat-menu item opens a MatDialog and animations are disabled (provideNoopAnimations / animations disabled, or the user's OS has reduced motion so `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` matches), the dialog ends up with no focus: focus is moved back to the menu trigger behind the dialog's backdrop.

Cause: with animations disabled the dialog's initial focus runs synchronously during the menu item's click (in the microtask after the click listener). The click then reaches the menu panel, which emits `closed('click')`, and `MatMenuTriggerBase._destroyMenu` calls `this.focus(this._openedBy)` unconditionally, without checking where focus currently is. With animations enabled the dialog focuses ~150ms later, after the menu has closed, so the problem doesn't show.

Since `prefers-reduced-motion` comes from an OS setting (e.g. Windows "Animation effects" off), regular users hit this, and keyboard and screen-reader users land on a control hidden behind the modal.

This was reported in #14879, which was closed as a duplicate of #11696 before the reporter clarified it only happens with NoopAnimationsModule; it was then locked. The menu code on `main` still restores focus unconditionally.

Possible fix, following the dialog's own guard from #17300 ("don't move focus if it was moved during close animation"): in `_destroyMenu`, when the close reason is `'click'`, skip restoring focus if it is already inside a different overlay pane (not the menu's own pane, not a menu panel such as a submenu, and not the overlay pane that contains the trigger itself). Every other close (Escape, Tab, backdrop click, programmatic close) keeps today's
behaviour. This doesn't change the accessibility position in #11696: focus still returns to the trigger whenever the menu owns it; it only stops the menu from pulling focus out of a modal that an item just opened. Happy to send a PR with tests if this direction is acceptable.

### Reproduction

  StackBlitz (from #14879, older Angular/Material):
  https://stackblitz.com/edit/checkbox-reactive-2zhjpp?file=app%2Fapp.component.ts

  I wasn't able to save a new StackBlitz, so this links the reproduction from #14879. The bug is not specific to that
  old version:

  - It reproduces on Angular 21.2.25 / @angular/cdk + @angular/material 21.1.2 in an application with animations
  disabled through the OS setting (Windows "Animation effects" off, so `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` matches and
  Material disables its animations). After a menu item opens a MatDialog, `document.activeElement` is the menu trigger
  behind the dialog's backdrop, not the dialog's `cdkFocusInitial` button.
  - The cause is unchanged on `main`: `MatMenuTriggerBase._destroyMenu` in `src/material/menu/menu-trigger-base.ts`
  still ends with

      if (this.restoreFocus && (reason === 'keydown' || !this._openedBy || !this._triggersSubmenu())) {
        this.focus(this._openedBy);
      }

    with no check of where focus currently is, so whenever the dialog takes focus before the menu finishes closing
  (always the case with animations disabled), the menu takes it back.

  Steps (old StackBlitz, which uses NoopAnimations):
  1. Open the StackBlitz and click the menu trigger.
  2. Click the menu item that opens the dialog.
  3. In the console, run `document.activeElement`: it is the menu trigger, not the dialog's button.

  Single-file reproduction for current versions (Angular/Material 21; paste as main.ts in a new Angular project):

  import {Component, inject} from '@angular/core';
  import {bootstrapApplication} from '@angular/platform-browser';
  import {MatButtonModule} from '@angular/material/button';
  import {MatMenuModule} from '@angular/material/menu';
  import {MatDialog, MatDialogModule} from '@angular/material/dialog';

  @Component({
    imports: [MatButtonModule, MatDialogModule],
    template: `
      <mat-dialog-content>Delete this item?</mat-dialog-content>
      <mat-dialog-actions>
        <button mat-button mat-dialog-close cdkFocusInitial>Cancel</button>
        <button mat-button [mat-dialog-close]="true">Delete</button>
      </mat-dialog-actions>
    `,
  })
  export class ConfirmDialog {}

  @Component({
    selector: 'app-root',
    imports: [MatButtonModule, MatMenuModule, MatDialogModule],
    template: `
      <button mat-button [matMenuTriggerFor]="menu">Menu</button>
      <mat-menu #menu="matMenu">
        <button mat-menu-item (click)="open()">Open dialog</button>
      </mat-menu>
    `,
  })
  export class App {
    private dialog = inject(MatDialog);
    open() { this.dialog.open(ConfirmDialog); }
  }

  bootstrapApplication(App);

  On 21, emulate reduced motion (DevTools > Rendering > "Emulate CSS media feature prefers-reduced-motion: reduce", then
  reload) or set the OS animation setting off, then click Menu > Open dialog and check `document.activeElement`.

### Expected Behavior

Focus stays on the dialog's initial focus target (the "Cancel" button with cdkFocusInitial), showing its focus indicator, exactly as it does when animations are enabled. The menu should not move focus back to its trigger while an overlay opened by the menu item holds focus.

### Actual Behavior

The dialog opens, but focus is on the menu trigger ("Menu") behind the dialog's backdrop: document.activeElement is the trigger button with cdk-focused / cdk-mouse-focused. The dialog shows no focused control, Enter re-activates the hidden trigger, and Tab starts from outside the dialog. The dialog's FocusTrap did focus "Cancel" first; the menu's _destroyMenu then called focus() on the trigger. 

document.activeElement after the dialog opens: button.mat-mdc-menu-trigger  (the menu trigger, behind the backdrop)

### Environment

  - CDK/Material: 21.1.2 (the same unconditional restore is still in src/material/menu/menu-trigger-base.ts on main)

title: bug(aria/tabs): the tab list loses its only Tab stop when the active tab is removed after an interaction
body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

When the tab that currently holds the roving `tabindex="0"` (the *active* tab, `TabListPattern.activeTab`) is removed from the tab list after the user has already interacted with the list, **no remaining tab gets `tabindex="0"`**. Every tab ends up with `tabindex="-1"`, so the tab list is no longer reachable with `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` (WCAG 2.1.1 / 2.4.3).

It is easy to hit with `selectionMode="explicit"`, where the active tab (focus) and the selected tab can differ, but the cause does not look specific to it: any removal of the active item after the first interaction should behave the same.

Cause, from reading the source (the guard is still on `main`): `TabListPattern.setDefaultState()` is the only place that re-assigns `activeItem`, and it is guarded.

```js
setDefaultStateEffect() {
  if (this.hasBeenInteracted()) return;   // never runs again after the first interaction
  this.setDefaultState();
}
// onKeydown / onClick / onFocusIn: this.hasBeenInteracted.set(true)
```

After the first focus / key / click, `hasBeenInteracted` stays `true`. If the active tab is then destroyed, `activeItem` still points to the removed tab, so no tab in `items()` matches and the roving `tabindex` is `-1` everywhere. Nothing falls back to the selected tab or to the first focusable tab.

A possible fix is to re-run the default-state logic when the active item is no longer part of `items()`, regardless of `hasBeenInteracted`:

```js
setDefaultStateEffect() {
  const active = this.activeTab();
  if (this.hasBeenInteracted() && active !== undefined && this.inputs.items().includes(active)) return;
  this.setDefaultState();
}
```

Related: #33934 (same area of code, but about a focus moved by a script, not about a removed active tab); #32969 / 0f5b0eee introduced the `hasBeenInteracted` guard.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/duypg9mo?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.ts

Steps to reproduce:
1. `Tab` into the tab list (focus lands on `A`), press `ArrowDown` once: focus moves to `B`, which is now the active tab (`tabindex="0"`); `A` stays selected because the selection is explicit.
2. Press `Tab` three times: the panel itself, the input, then the `remove B` button.
3. Press `Enter` on `remove B`: the active tab `B` is destroyed.
4. Inspect the tabs: `A` and `C` both have `tabindex="-1"`.
5. Press `Shift+Tab` repeatedly: focus goes back through the input and the panel, then to the previous focusable element of the page. The tab list is skipped entirely.

Reproduced on `@angular/aria` 22.2.1 and 22.2.3.

### Expected Behavior

After the active tab is removed, a remaining tab (the selected one, else the first focusable) becomes the active tab and gets `tabindex="0"`, so the tab list keeps exactly one Tab stop.

### Actual Behavior

All tabs have `tabindex="-1"`. The tab list cannot be reached with `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`, and the arrow keys cannot help since focus cannot enter the list.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.1
- CDK/Material: `@angular/aria` 22.2.1 and 22.2.3, `@angular/cdk` 22.2.1 and 22.2.3
- Browser(s): Microsoft Edge (Chromium), also driven with real key events over the Chrome DevTools Protocol
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): Windows 11

title: bug(mat-datepicker): date parse errors are not propagated to Signal Forms
body:
### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

The datepicker input provides a matDatepickerParse validation error when the user enters text that cannot be parsed as a date.

This error is available when using Reactive Forms, but when using Signal Forms, the error does not reach the errors signal of the field tree. The value of the form field stays as `null`.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-d3y2q7gw?file=src%2Fmain.ts,src%2Fmain.ts

Steps to reproduce:
1. Start the application.
2. Enter an invalid date string into the Reactive Forms datepicker.
3. Observe that the control reports a matDatepickerParse error.
4. Enter the same invalid date string into the Signal Forms datepicker.
5. Observe that the Signal Forms field does not report the corresponding parse error in field().errors().

### Expected Behavior

I would expect the date parse errors to also be available to the Signal Form.

If I understand correctly, this seems to be in line with the direction of the Angular Signal Forms API, for example with https://angular.dev/api/forms/signals/transformedValue to report parse errors in custom controls.

### Actual Behavior

The date parse errors are not available to the Signal Form. Since the form value remains as `null` for invalid values, distinguishing between an empty form and invalid input is not possible in the schema.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.2
- CDK/Material: 22.2.2
- Browser(s): Chrome, Firefox, Safari
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS

title: bug(COMPONENT): Angular ARIA tab must allow eager loading of tab content
body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

## Description

Angular Aria's tabs implementation appears to require tab panel content to be declared using `ng-template[ngTabContent]`, which prevents consumers from eagerly rendering tab panel content in the DOM.

This is problematic for use cases where all tab panels need to be initialized upfront, rather than lazily instantiated when their associated tabs become active. For example, a tab panel may contain a component that needs to initialize early, or preload data that is required for SEO (in SSR setup).

Currently, `ngTabContent` can only be applied to an `ng-template`, and the implementation warns when a tab panel does not contain the expected content directive. Applying `ngTabContent` directly to a component or a regular element does not work because it does not match the directive's selector.

It would be useful to provide a supported way to eagerly instantiate tab panel content while retaining the existing tab panel API and accessibility behavior.

## Reasoning

The WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide recommends automatic tab activation on focus when the associated panel can be displayed without noticeable latency. It also notes that this typically requires panel content to be preloaded; otherwise, automatic activation introduces delays that significantly hinder efficient keyboard navigation.

Eager loading is therefore a legitimate use case for accessible tabs, particularly when panel content requires initialization or data fetching before it can be displayed.

Providing an explicit mechanism for eager content instantiation would allow developers to avoid unnecessary delays during tab navigation without having to implement their own tab behavior or work around the current content directive requirements.

### Reproduction

Link: https://angular.dev/guide/aria/tabs#example-1



### Expected Behavior

I expect the ngTabContent to have a selector on its own without the ng-template infront, so that the tab content can be eagerly loaded

### Actual Behavior

The ngTabContent selector has ng-template in front of it which prevents us from eagerly loading tab content that may contain useful information and is needed upfront and without layout shift

### Environment

- Angular: latest
- CDK/Material: N/A
- Browser(s): latest
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): N/A
